text: For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea, and all underwent baptism into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ. But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness. Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired. Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.” Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day. …

For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread, and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.” For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

Love is patient; love is kind. Love is not jealous, does not boast, is not puffed up, does not behave shamefully, does not seek its own interests, is not provoked, does not keep account of wrong, does not rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells among you? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person. For God’s temple is holy, and that is what you are.

Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough? Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed. So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband— but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.
In the same way, the Lord directed those who proclaim the good news to live from the good news.

Am I saying these things merely in a human way, or does not the law also say them? For in the law of Moses it is written, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes.” Is it oxen that concern God, or does He surely say it for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of sharing. If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it a great matter if we reap your material things?

Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For everything in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the boastfulness of life—is not from the Father, but is from the world. And the world is passing away, and its desire; but the one who does the will of God abides forever.

And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments. The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person. But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him. The one who says that he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.

For this is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another, not as Cain, who was from the evil one and slaughtered his brother. And for what reason did he slaughter him? Because his own works were evil, but his brother’s were righteous.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

But whoever has this world’s means of living and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as He gave us a commandment.

Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and is already in the world now.

And this is the confidence we have toward Him: if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us. And if we know that He hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked of Him.

As children of obedience, do not conform yourselves to the former desires of your ignorance, but, in accordance with the Holy One who called you, become holy yourselves in all your conduct, because it is written, “You shall be holy, because I am holy.”
having been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.

For “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like a flower of grass. The grass withered, and the flower fell, but the word of the Lord remains forever.” And this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.

For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His footsteps. He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth. When He was reviled, He did not revile in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but entrusted His cause to the One who judges justly.

He Himself bore our sins in His body upon the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live to righteousness. By His wound you were healed. For you were wandering like sheep, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

For it stands in Scripture: “Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen, precious cornerstone, and the one who believes in Him will certainly not be put to shame.” Therefore, the honor is for you who believe; but for those who do not believe, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner,” and “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble, disobeying the word; to this they were also appointed.

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s possession, so that you may proclaim the excellences of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light. Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

For “The one who wishes to love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit. He must turn away from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it. For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears attend to their petition, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”

who were once disobedient, when the patience of God waited in the days of Noah while the ark was being prepared, in which a few—that is, eight souls—were brought safely through water. Corresponding to this, baptism now saves you—not a removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal to God for a good conscience—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

Let your adornment not be the outward kind—braiding hair, putting on gold ornaments, or dressing in garments— but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God. For this is how the holy women of former times, who hoped in God, also adorned themselves, submitting themselves to their own husbands, as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her children if you do good and do not fear any terror.
not repaying evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but, on the contrary, blessing, because you were called for this, so that you might inherit a blessing.

Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you, which comes upon you for testing, as though something strange were happening to you. But insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that you may also rejoice with exultation at the revelation of His glory. If you are reviled for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you.

Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed: Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly; not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

Likewise, you who are younger, submit yourselves to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” Therefore, humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that He may exalt you in due time,
casting all your anxiety upon Him, because He cares for you.

Be sober; be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that the same kinds of sufferings are being experienced by your brotherhood in the world.

Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you. For you yourselves know precisely that the day of the Lord comes in this way, like a thief in the night. When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes upon them, as labor pain upon a pregnant woman, and they will certainly not escape. But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief. For you are all sons of light and sons of day. We are not of night or darkness. So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us keep watch and be sober.
Rejoice always. Pray unceasingly. Give thanks in everything, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.

Let a woman learn in quietness, in all submission. But I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness. For Adam was formed first, then Eve, and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, being deceived, came to be in transgression. But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with self-restraint.

Command those who are rich in the present age not to be high-minded nor to set their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but on God, who richly provides us all things for enjoyment, to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous, ready to share, storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of the life that is truly life.

But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out. But having food and coverings, with these we will be content. But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge human beings into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.
This third time I am coming to you. “On the mouth of two witnesses and three every matter will be established.”

Therefore, having such hope, we use great boldness, and are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel might not gaze at the end of what was being brought to an end. But their minds were hardened. For until this very day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant, not being unveiled, because in Christ it is brought to an end. But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart. But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed. Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. And we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.

For it is not that there should be relief for others and affliction for you, but on the basis of equality: at the present time your abundance is for their lack, so that their abundance may also be for your lack, so that there may be equality. As it is written, “The one with much had no excess, and the one with little had no shortage.”

Now this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows in blessings will also reap in blessings. Let each give as he has decided in his heart, not out of sorrow or compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we became eyewitnesses of His majesty. For He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice such as this was borne to Him by the Majestic Glory: “This is My Son, My Beloved, in whom I have taken pleasure”— and we ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain. And we have the prophetic word more firmly established, to which you do well to pay attention as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts,

and reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemning them to overthrow, having made them an example of things to come for ungodly people, and rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the lawless people’s conduct in debauchery— for by what he saw and heard, that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day over their lawless deeds— then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a rushing roar, and the elements will be dissolved by burning heat, and the earth and the works in it will be found. Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be in holy acts of conduct and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved by fire and the elements melt in burning heat?

But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, as some consider slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing anyone to perish but all to come to repentance.

For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat. For we hear that some among you are walking disorderly, not working at all but working at everyone else’s business. Now such people we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread. But you, brothers, do not lose heart in doing good.

The saying is faithful: for if we died with Him, we will also live with Him; if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us; if we are unfaithful, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.

Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, even though they are strangers, who have borne witness to your love before the Church. You will do well to send them onward in a manner worthy of God, for they went out for the sake of the Name, receiving nothing from the Gentiles. We therefore ought to support such people, so that we may become fellow workers with the truth.

He commanded us to proclaim to the people and bear solemn witness that He is the One appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. All the prophets bear witness to Him: everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”

After they fell silent, James spoke: “Men, brothers, listen to me. Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name. With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written: ‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright, so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things known from long ago.’ Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God, but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood. … For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”

Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel: ‘In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams. Even upon My male slaves and My female slaves in those days I will pour out My Spirit, and they will prophesy. I will give wonders in heaven above and signs on the earth below: blood and fire and a cloud of smoke. The sun will be changed into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes. And everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.’

For David says concerning Him, ‘I kept the Lord before me always, for He is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken. Therefore my heart rejoiced and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope, because You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor allow Your Holy One to see decay. You have made known to me the paths of life; You will fill me with gladness in Your presence.’ Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day. Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one of his descendants upon his throne, he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay. …

Therefore, exalted to God’s right hand and having received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, He has poured out this which you see and hear. For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’ Therefore let the whole house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified.”

Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you, for your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself.”

I know that after my departure fierce wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock. Even from among you yourselves men will arise, speaking distorted things to draw the disciples away after themselves. Therefore stay awake, remembering that for three years, night and day, I never ceased admonishing each one with tears.
In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

Moses said, ‘The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to him in everything he says to you. Every person who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed from among the people.’
Salvation is in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among human beings by which we must be saved.”
Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than human beings.

Our fathers had the Tent of Testimony in the wilderness, as the One who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern he had seen. Our fathers in their turn received it and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the nations’ land, whose people God drove out before our fathers. It remained until the days of David, who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling for the God of Jacob. But Solomon built Him a house. Yet the Most High does not dwell in things made by hands, as the prophet says: ‘Heaven is My throne, and the earth the footstool of My feet. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or what place is there for My rest? Did not My hand make all these things?’

Therefore put on, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, tender compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against someone. Just as the Lord forgave you, so also must you.

Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another. … Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as needed, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
Be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your anger,

Be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your anger, nor give a place to the devil. … Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.

Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the Church and gave Himself for her, … “For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.” This mystery is great, but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the Church. Nevertheless, let each one of you also love his own wife as himself, and let the wife respect her husband.

For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light, for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth, testing what is pleasing to the Lord. And do not share in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them,

Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. “Honor your father and mother”—which is the first commandment with a promise— “so that it may be well with you and you may live long upon the earth.”

For through law I died to law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ. And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.

Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, “And to seeds,” as concerning many, but as concerning one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ. What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise. For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise. But God has graciously given it to Abraham through promise. Why, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator. … So the law became our guardian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith. But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.

And Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the nations by faith, proclaimed the gospel beforehand to Abraham: “In you all the nations will be blessed.” So then, those who are of faith are blessed with believing Abraham.

For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman. But the one by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, and the one by the free woman through promise. These things are being interpreted allegorically, for these women are two covenants: one from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery, which is Hagar. Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is enslaved with her children. But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. … But what does Scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall certainly not inherit with the son of the free woman.” Therefore, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman but of the free woman.

For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not make freedom a base of operations for the flesh, but through love serve one another as slaves. For the whole law is fulfilled in one saying: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some transgression, you who are spiritual are to restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself, lest you too be tempted. Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins. Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me. In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You took no pleasure. Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Your will, O God.’” After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You did not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law— He then said, “Look, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second. By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

By faith Moses, when grown, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh’s daughter, choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to have the temporary enjoyment of sin. He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking toward the reward. By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger, for he endured as though seeing the invisible One.

By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, God testifying concerning his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks. By faith Enoch was taken away so as not to see death, and he was not found, because God took him away. For before his taking away he had received testimony that he had pleased God. And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for the one approaching God must believe that He is and that He becomes a rewarder of those who seek Him. By faith Noah, instructed concerning things not yet seen, acted with reverent fear and prepared an ark for the salvation of his household. Through this he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness according to faith.

Pursue peace with everyone, and sanctification, without which no one will see the Lord. Watch lest anyone fall short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness grow up and cause trouble, and through it many be defiled, lest anyone be sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who sold his own birthright for a single meal. For you know that even afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, although he sought it with tears.

and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline, nor faint when reproved by Him. For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and scourges every son He receives.” Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline? But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh as disciplinarians and respected them. Shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live? For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness. …

Let brotherly love remain. Do not forget hospitality, for through it some unknowingly entertained angels. Remember the prisoners as fellow prisoners, and those being mistreated, as you yourselves also are in a body.

We have an altar from which those serving the tent have no authority to eat. For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest brings into the holy places for sin are burned outside the camp. Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the gate, so that He might sanctify the people through His own blood. So let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach. For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the one to come.

Let marriage be honored among all, and the marriage bed undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers. Let your manner of life be free from the love of money, being content with what is present; for He Himself has said, “I will certainly not leave you, nor will I ever forsake you.” So we may say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper; I will not fear. What will a human being do to me?”

Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested Me with a trial and saw My works for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, ‘They always wander in their heart, and they did not know My ways,’ as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest.’” Watch out, brothers, lest there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin. … So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God. For the one who entered His rest also himself rested from his works, just as God did from His own. Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.

For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him. Abraham also apportioned to him a tenth of everything. His name is interpreted first as king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace. Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither a beginning of days nor an end of life, but made like the Son of God, he remains a priest continually. … And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek, who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life. For it is testified, “You are a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”

For, finding fault with them, He says, “Look, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will conclude a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord. For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws into their mind, I will also inscribe them upon their hearts, and I will be their God, and they will be My people. And they shall certainly not teach, each his fellow citizen and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because all will know Me, from their small to their great. …

With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship. But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance. … But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation— and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption. For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!

Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of various kinds, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.

But become doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror, for he looked at himself and went away and immediately forgot what he was like. But the one who looks closely into the complete law, the law of freedom, and continues in it, becoming no forgetful hearer but a doer of work, will be blessed in his doing.
Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind. For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord, a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.

And the Lord said unto me: Say unto them, You shall not go up, neither shall you fight, for I am not with you; and you shall not be crushed before your enemies.
And I spoke unto you, but you did not hearken unto me; and you transgressed the word of the Lord, and forced your way up into the hill country.
And the Amorites who dwelt in that hill country came out to meet you, and pursued you as bees do, and wounded you from Seir unto Hormah.
And you sat down and wept before the Lord; but the Lord did not hearken unto your voice, neither gave He heed unto you.
And you dwelt in Kadesh many days, as many days as you dwelt there.
beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to make this law plain, saying:
The Lord our God spoke unto us in Horeb, saying: Let it suffice you to have dwelt in this mountain.

Turn and set forth, and enter the hill country of the Amorites and all the neighbouring places of Arabah, the hill country and the plain, the southwest and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates.
Behold, I have delivered the land before you. Enter and inherit the land which I sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and unto their seed after them.
And I spoke unto you at that time, saying: I shall not be able to bear you alone.
At that time the Lord said unto me: Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like unto the first, and come up unto Me into the mountain; and you shall make for yourself an ark of wood.
And I abode in the mountain forty days and forty nights; and the Lord hearkened unto me at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy you.
And the Lord said unto me: Go, set forth before this people, and let them enter and inherit the land which I sware unto their fathers to give them.

10:12 And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,

And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and His ordinances which I command you this day, that it may be well with you?
Behold, unto the Lord your God belong heaven and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all that is therein.
Yet the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them, and chose their seed after them, even you, above all the nations, as at this day.
And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and shall stiffen your neck no more.
For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearful God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;
who executes judgment for the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow, and loves the sojourner, to give him bread and clothing.
And you shall love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
And I will write upon the tablets the words which were upon the first tablets, which you broke; and you shall put them in the ark.
You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him, and you shall cleave unto Him, and you shall swear by His name.
He is your boast, and He is your God, who has done among you these great and glorious things which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy souls; but now the Lord your God has made you as the stars of heaven in multitude.
And I made an ark of decay-resistant wood, and hewed two tablets of stone like unto the first; and I went up into the mountain, with the two tablets in my hands.
And He wrote upon the tablets, according to the first writing, the ten words which the Lord spoke unto you in the mountain out of the midst of the fire; and the Lord gave them unto me.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets into the ark which I had made; and they were there, as the Lord commanded me.
And the sons of Israel set out from Beeroth of the sons of Iakim to Misadai. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they set out to Gadgad, and from Gadgad to Jotbathah, a land of flowing torrents.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister, and to bless in His name, unto this day.
Therefore the Levites have no portion or inheritance among their brethren; the Lord Himself is his inheritance, as He spoke unto him.
And you shall love the Lord your God, and keep His charge, and His ordinances, and His judgments, all your days.
For the land whither you go to inherit it is not as the land of Egypt, whence you came forth, where they sow seed and water it with their feet, as a garden of herbs.
But the land whither you go to inherit it is a land of hills and plains; it shall drink water of the rain of heaven,
a land which the Lord your God cares for; the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year.
And if you diligently hearken unto all His commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
He shall give the rain unto your land in its season, the early and the latter rain; and you shall gather in your grain, and your wine, and your oil.
And He shall give grass in your fields for your cattle; and when you have eaten and are filled,
take heed unto yourself, lest your heart be enlarged, and you transgress, and serve other gods, and bow down unto them,

and the Lord be kindled to wrath against you, and shut up heaven, so that there is no rain, and the land does not yield her fruit, and you perish speedily from the good land which the Lord has given you.
And you shall lay these words in your heart and in your soul, and bind them for a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immovable before your eyes.
And you shall teach them unto your children, to speak of them when you sit in the house, and when you walk in the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
And know this day that I speak unto you, not unto your children, who have neither known nor seen the chastening of the Lord your God, and His mighty deeds, and His mighty hand, and His uplifted arm,
And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your houses and of your gates,
that your days and the days of your sons may be prolonged upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.
11:22 And it shall be, if you diligently hearken unto all these commandments which I command you this day to do, to love the Lord our God, and to walk in all His ways, and to cleave unto Him,
And it shall be, if you diligently hearken unto all these commandments which I command you this day to do, to love the Lord our God, and to walk in all His ways, and to cleave unto Him,
that the Lord shall cast out all these nations from before you, and you shall inherit nations great and mightier than you.

Every place whereon the sole of your foot shall tread shall be yours. From the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, and from the great river, the river Euphrates, even unto the western sea, shall be your borders.
None shall stand before you; the Lord your God shall lay the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the land whereon you shall tread, as the Lord has spoken unto you.
Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day;

and the curses, if you do not hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day, and wander from the way which I commanded you, going to serve other gods which you have not known.
And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land whither you pass over to inherit it, that you shall set the blessing upon Mount Gerizim, and the curse upon Mount Ebal.
and His signs and His wonders which He did in the midst of Egypt unto Pharaoh king of Egypt and unto all his land,
Behold, are they not beyond the Jordan, behind the way of the setting sun, in the land of Canaan that lies toward the west, adjoining Gilgal, near the lofty oak?
For you pass over the Jordan, to enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession for ever; and you shall inherit it, and dwell therein.
And you shall take heed to do all His ordinances and these judgments, which I set before you this day.

and what He did unto the host of the Egyptians, unto their chariots and their horsemen, when He caused the water of the Red Sea to overflow them as they pursued you, and the Lord destroyed them unto this day,
and what He did unto you in the wilderness, until you came unto this place,

and what He did unto Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them, and their houses, and their tents, and all their substance that was with them, in the midst of all Israel.
For your eyes have seen all the great works of the Lord, which He has done unto you this day.
And you shall keep all His commandments which I command you this day, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land whither you pass over the Jordan to inherit it,
that you may prolong your days upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give unto them and unto their seed after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And these are the ordinances and judgments which you shall take heed to do in the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you for a possession, all the days that you live upon the earth.
And you shall pass over the Jordan, and dwell in the land which the Lord your God gives you to inherit; and He shall give you rest from all your enemies round about, and you shall dwell in safety.

And it shall be, at the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there, you shall bring thither all that I command you this day: your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your tithes, and the firstfruits of your hands, and your gifts, and all the choice gifts which you shall vow unto your God.

And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you, and your sons, and your daughters, and your male slaves, and your female slaves, and the Levite within your gates; for he has neither portion nor inheritance with you.
Take heed unto yourself, that you do not offer your whole burnt offerings in every place that you see,
but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose in one of your tribes, you shall offer there your whole burnt offerings, and you shall do there all that I command you this day.

Nevertheless, you may slaughter and eat flesh according to all your desire, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you in every city. The unclean among you and the clean may eat it together, as the gazelle or the deer.
12:16 Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.

You may not eat within your cities the tithe of your grain, or of your wine, or of your oil, nor the firstborn of your cattle or of your sheep, nor any of the vows which you shall vow, nor your pledged offerings, nor the firstfruits of your hands;

but you shall eat them before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for Himself, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the sojourner within your cities. And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God in all that you put your hand unto.
Take heed unto yourself, that you do not forsake the Levite all the time that you live upon the land.
You shall utterly destroy all the places wherein the nations whose possession you inherit served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under the leafy tree.

And if the Lord your God enlarges your borders, as He has spoken unto you, and you say: I will eat flesh, because your soul desires to eat flesh, you may eat flesh according to all the desire of your soul.

And if the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there is too far from you, you shall slaughter of your cattle and of your sheep which God has given you, as I commanded you, and eat within your cities according to the desire of your soul.
As the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it; the unclean among you and the clean shall eat it alike.
Take diligent heed that you do not eat blood; for its blood is life, and the life shall not be eaten with the flesh.

12:23 Take diligent heed that you do not eat blood; for its blood is life, and the life shall not be eaten with the flesh.

12:24 You shall not eat it; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.

12:25 You shall not eat it, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, if you do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
You shall not eat it; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
You shall not eat it, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, if you do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
Only your holy things which you have, and your vowed offerings, you shall take, and come unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.

And you shall prepare your whole burnt offerings; you shall offer the flesh upon the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall pour the blood of your sacrifices against the base of the altar of the Lord your God; and you shall eat the flesh.
Keep and hear and do all the words which I command you, that it may be well with you and with your sons for ever, if you do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
And if the Lord your God destroys from before you the nations whither you go to inherit their land, and you inherit their possession and dwell in their land,
And you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire; and their name shall perish from that place.

take heed unto yourself, that you do not seek to follow them after they have been destroyed from before you. You shall not inquire after their gods, saying: How do these nations serve their gods? I also will do so.
You shall not do so unto the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did unto their gods, for they burn their sons and their daughters with fire unto their gods.
You shall not do so unto the Lord your God,
but unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose in one of your tribes, to set His name there, that it may be called upon, you shall seek and come thither.

And you shall bring thither your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your firstfruits, and your vowed offerings, and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep.
And you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in all that you put your hand unto, you and your houses, because the Lord your God has blessed you.
You shall not do all that we do here this day, every man that which is pleasing in his own sight;
for you have not yet come unto the rest and unto the inheritance which the Lord your God gives you.
Every word which I command you this day, you shall take heed to do; you shall not add unto it, neither shall you take away from it.
You shall surely report him; your hands shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people.
And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; for he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear and fear, and shall no more do such an evil thing among you.
And if you hear it said in one of your cities which the Lord your God gives you to dwell in,
Lawless men have gone forth from among you, and have turned aside all the inhabitants of their city, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known,
then you shall inquire and search diligently; and behold, if the matter is clearly true, and this abomination has been done among you,
you shall surely slay all the inhabitants of that city with the sword; you shall utterly devote it to destruction, and all that is therein.

And you shall gather all its spoil into its streets, and burn the city with fire, and all its spoil, all together before the Lord your God; and it shall be uninhabited for ever, and shall not be built again.

And nothing of that which is devoted to destruction shall cleave to your hand, that the Lord may turn from the fierceness of His wrath, and grant you mercy, and have mercy upon you, and multiply you, as the Lord sware unto your fathers,
if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep all His commandments which I command you this day, to do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
And if there arises among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and he gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, whereof he spoke unto you, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known,

you shall not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or unto that dreamer of dreams; for the Lord God tests you, to know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
13:5 You shall walk after the Lord your God, and fear Him, and keep His commandments, and hearken unto His voice, and be joined unto Him.
You shall walk after the Lord your God, and fear Him, and keep His commandments, and hearken unto His voice, and be joined unto Him.

And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall die; for he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you from bondage, to thrust you out of the way wherein the Lord your God commanded you to walk. And you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.

And if your brother, the son of your father or of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own soul, entices you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known, you nor your fathers,
of the gods of the nations round about you, whether near unto you or far from you, from one end of the earth unto the other,
you shall not consent unto him, neither shall you hearken unto him; neither shall your eye spare him, nor shall you yearn for him, nor conceal him.
You are sons of the Lord your God; you shall not perform purification rites, neither shall you make a bald place between your eyes for the dead.
And whatsoever does not have fins and scales, you shall not eat; they are unclean unto you.
Every clean bird you may eat.
And these you shall not eat of them: the eagle, and the griffon vulture, and the sea-eagle,
and the vulture, and the kite, and those like it,
and every raven, and those like it,
and the ostrich, and the owl, and the gull,
and the heron, and the swan, and the ibis,
and the diving bird, and the hawk, and those like it, and the hoopoe, and the night-raven,
and the pelican, and the plover, and those like it, and the purple swamphen, and the bat.
All creeping things among the flying creatures are unclean unto you; you shall not eat of them.
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, out of all the nations upon the face of the earth.
Every clean flying creature you may eat.

You shall not eat anything that dies of itself; it shall be given unto the resident alien within your cities, and he shall eat it, or you may sell it unto a foreigner; for you are a holy people unto the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.
You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed, the yield of your field, year by year.

And you shall eat it before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there. You shall bring the tithes of your grain, and of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep, that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.

And if the way is too long for you, so that you cannot carry them, because the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there is far from you, when the Lord your God has blessed you,
then you shall sell them for silver, and take the silver in your hands, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose.

And you shall spend the silver for whatsoever your soul desires, for cattle, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever your soul desires; and you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice, you and your house,
and the Levite within your cities; for he has neither portion nor inheritance with you.
After three years you shall bring forth all the tithe of your produce; in that year you shall lay it up within your cities.

And the Levite, for he has neither portion nor inheritance with you, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow within your cities shall come, and eat, and be filled; that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works which you do.
You shall eat no abominable thing.
These are the beasts which you may eat: a calf of the cattle, and a lamb of the sheep, and a young male goat of the goats,
deer, gazelle, bubalos, goat-stag, white-rumped antelope, oryx, and giraffe.
Every beast that divides the hoof, and cleaves its hoof into two parts, and brings up the cud among the beasts, these you may eat.

And these you shall not eat of those that bring up the cud, and of those that divide the hoof and cleave its parts: the camel, and the hare, and the rock hyrax; for they bring up the cud, but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean unto you.
And the swine, for it divides the hoof and cleaves its parts, but does not chew the cud, is unclean unto you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, neither shall you touch their carcasses.
And these you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatsoever has fins and scales, you may eat.
At the end of seven years you shall make a release.

You shall freely give unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs; and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him. For because of this the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
For the needy shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you to do this thing, saying: You shall freely open your hands unto your poor brother and unto the needy in your land.
And if your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold unto you, he shall serve you six years; and in the seventh year you shall send him forth free from you.
And when you send him forth free from you, you shall not send him away empty.
You shall furnish him generously out of your sheep, and out of your grain, and out of your winepress; as the Lord your God has blessed you, you shall give unto him.
And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you thence; therefore I command you to do this thing.
And if he says unto you: I will not go forth from you, because he loves you and your house, and because it is well with him beside you,
then you shall take an awl, and pierce his ear against the door, and he shall be your household slave for ever; and unto your female slave you shall do likewise.
It shall not seem hard unto you when they are sent forth free from you, for he served you six years for the yearly wage of a hired worker; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all that you do.

Every firstborn male that is born among your cattle and among your sheep you shall sanctify unto the Lord your God. You shall do no work with your firstborn calf, neither shall you shear the firstborn of your sheep.

And this is the ordinance of the release: you shall release every debt of yours which your neighbour owes you; and you shall not exact it of your brother, for a release unto the Lord your God has been proclaimed.
You shall eat it before the Lord, year by year, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, you and your house.
And if there is a blemish in it, lameness or blindness or any grievous blemish, you shall not sacrifice it unto the Lord your God.
You shall eat it within your cities; the unclean among you and the clean shall eat it alike, as the gazelle or the deer.
15:23 Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
Of a foreigner you may exact whatsoever he owes you; but you shall release your brother’s debt unto you.
For there shall be none in need among you; for the Lord your God shall surely bless you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, to inherit it,
if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all these commandments which I command you this day.

For the Lord your God has blessed you, as He has spoken unto you; and you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.

Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.
Keep the month of new produce, and observe the Passover unto the Lord your God; for in the month of new produce you came forth out of Egypt by night.
And you shall keep the Feast of Weeks unto the Lord your God, according to the ability of your hand, of that which He gives you, as the Lord your God has blessed you.

And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the Levite within your cities, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow among you, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
And you shall remember that you were a household slave in the land of Egypt; and you shall keep and do these commandments.
You shall keep the Feast of Tents seven days, when you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the Levite, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow within your cities.

You shall keep a feast for seven days unto the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for Himself; and if the Lord your God blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, you shall rejoice.

Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,
but every man according to the ability of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you.
You shall appoint judges and recording officers for yourself in all your cities which the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.
And you shall sacrifice the Passover unto the Lord your God, sheep and cattle, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
You shall pursue justly that which is just, that you may live, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you.
You shall not plant for yourself a sacred grove, any tree, beside the altar of the Lord your God which you shall make for yourself.
You shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which the Lord your God has hated.

You shall eat no leaven with it; you shall eat unleavened bread with it for seven days, the bread of affliction, for you came forth out of Egypt in haste; that you may remember the day of your departure out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
No leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders seven days; neither shall any of the flesh which you sacrifice in the evening of the first day remain overnight until the morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in any of your cities which the Lord your God gives you,

but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at the setting of the sun, at the time when you came forth out of Egypt.
And you shall boil it, and roast it, and eat it in the place which the Lord your God shall choose; and in the morning you shall turn and go unto your houses.

You shall eat unleavened bread for six days; and on the seventh day shall be a concluding feast, a feast unto the Lord your God. You shall do no work therein, save that which is done for a person’s needs.
You shall count seven complete weeks unto yourself; when you begin to put the sickle to the harvest, you shall begin to count seven weeks.
You shall not sacrifice unto the Lord your God a calf or a sheep wherein is a blemish, any evil defect; for it is an abomination unto the Lord your God.

And you shall do according to the matter which they declare unto you from the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there; and you shall take diligent heed to do according to all that is laid down for you as law.
You shall do according to the law and according to the judgment which they tell you; you shall not turn aside from the word which they declare unto you, to the right hand or to the left.

And the man who acts presumptuously, and will not hearken unto the priest who stands to minister in the name of the Lord your God, or unto the judge who shall be in those days, that man shall die; and you shall remove the evil one from Israel.
And all the people shall hear and fear, and shall act ungodly no more.
And if you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and inherit it, and dwell therein, and say: I will set a ruler over me, as do the other nations round about me,

you shall surely set over yourself a ruler whom the Lord your God shall choose. You shall set a ruler over yourself from among your brethren; you may not set a foreign man over yourself, for he is not your brother.

For he shall not multiply horses unto himself, neither shall he cause the people to return unto Egypt, that he may multiply horses unto himself; for the Lord has said: You shall not return by this way again.
And he shall not multiply wives unto himself, neither shall his heart turn aside; and he shall not greatly multiply silver and gold unto himself.
And it shall be, when he sits in his rule, that he shall write for himself this second law in a scroll, from the Levitical priests.
And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all these commandments and these ordinances, to do them,
And if there is found among you, within any of your cities which the Lord your God gives you, a man or a woman who does evil before the Lord your God, transgressing His covenant,

that his heart may not be lifted up above his brethren, and that he may not turn aside from the commandments, to the right hand or to the left; that he may prolong his days in his rule, he and his sons, among the sons of Israel.
and they go and serve other gods, and bow down unto them, unto the sun, or unto the moon, or unto any of the array of heaven, which He has not commanded,
and it is told you, you shall inquire diligently; and behold, if the matter is true, and this abomination has been done in Israel,
then you shall bring forth that man or that woman, and you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die.
Upon the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he who is condemned to death be put to death; he shall not die upon the testimony of one witness.
And the hand of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people; and you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.

And if a matter in judgment is too hard for you, between blood and blood, and between judgment and judgment, and between injury and injury, and between dispute and dispute, matters of judgment within your cities, you shall arise and go up unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
And you shall come unto the Levitical priests, and unto the judge who shall be in those days; and they shall inquire, and declare unto you the judgment.
The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, shall have neither portion nor inheritance with Israel. The offerings of the Lord are their inheritance; they shall eat them.
There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
18:13 You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.
The Lord your God shall raise up unto you a prophet from among your brethren, like unto me; you shall hearken unto him,

according to all that you asked of the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, saying: We will no more hear the voice of the Lord our God, neither will we see this great fire any more, lest we die.
And the Lord said unto me: All that they have spoken is right.
I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brethren, like unto you, and will put My word in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I command him.
And the man who will not hearken unto whatsoever the prophet shall speak in My name, I will exact retribution from him.
And they shall have no inheritance among their brethren; the Lord Himself is his inheritance, as He spoke unto him.
But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken?

Whatsoever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come to pass, nor is fulfilled, that is the word which the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken in ungodliness; you shall not spare him.
And this shall be the priests’ due from the people, from them that sacrifice a sacrifice, whether a calf or a sheep: they shall give unto the priest the foreleg, and the cheeks, and the stomach.
And you shall give unto him the firstfruits of your grain, and of your wine, and of your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep.
For the Lord your God has chosen him out of all your tribes, to stand before the Lord your God, to minister and to bless in His name, he and his sons among the sons of Israel.
And if a Levite comes from any of your cities, from among all the sons of Israel where he sojourns, according to the desire of his soul, unto the place which the Lord shall choose,
then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as do all his brethren the Levites who stand there before the Lord.
He shall eat an allotted portion, apart from the sale according to his ancestral family.
And when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
And when the Lord your God destroys the nations whose land your God gives you, and you inherit their possession, and dwell in their cities and in their houses,
that innocent blood may not be shed in your land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and that there may be none guilty of blood among you.
But if a man hates his neighbour, and lies in wait for him, and rises up against him, and strikes him mortally, so that he dies, and flees unto one of these cities,
then the elders of his city shall send and take him thence, and deliver him into the hands of the kinsman who avenges blood, and he shall die.
Your eye shall not spare him; and you shall cleanse the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, and it shall be well with you.
You shall not remove your neighbour’s boundaries, which your fathers set in your inheritance, which was allotted unto you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.

One witness shall not suffice to testify against a man concerning any injustice, or any trespass, or any sin which he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, and at the mouth of three witnesses, shall every matter be established.
And if an unrighteous witness rises up against a man, accusing him of ungodliness,
then the two men between whom is the dispute shall stand before the Lord, and before the priests, and before the judges who shall be in those days.
And the judges shall inquire diligently; and behold, if the unrighteous witness has testified falsely, and has stood against his brother,
then you shall do unto him as he wickedly purposed to do unto his brother; and you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of your land which the Lord your God gives you.
And those who remain shall hear and fear, and shall no more do such an evil thing among you.
Your eye shall not spare him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
Mark out the way for yourself, and divide into three parts the territory of your land which the Lord your God apportions unto you; and there shall be a refuge there for every slayer.
And this shall be the ordinance for the slayer who shall flee thither and live: whosoever strikes his neighbour unintentionally, having borne him no hatred aforetime,

as when a man goes with his neighbour into the forest to gather wood, and his hand is jolted with the axe as he cuts the wood, and the iron slips from the wood and strikes his neighbour, so that he dies, he shall flee unto one of these cities and live;

lest the kinsman who avenges blood pursue the slayer while his heart is hot, and overtake him, if the way is long, and strike him mortally, so that he dies, though no sentence of death is due unto him, for he bore his neighbour no hatred aforetime.
Therefore I command you this thing, saying: You shall set apart three cities for yourself.
And if the Lord your God enlarges your borders, as He sware unto your fathers, and the Lord gives you all the land which He promised to give unto your fathers,
if you hearken to do all these commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to walk in all His ways all your days, then you shall add three cities more unto these three,
And we turned and departed into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea, as the Lord had spoken unto me; and we compassed Mount Seir many days.
The Emim dwelt there aforetime, a nation great and numerous and strong as the Anakim.
These also are reckoned as Rephaim, like the Anakim; and the Moabites call them Emim.

And the Horites dwelt in Seir aforetime; but the sons of Esau destroyed them, and blotted them out from before them, and dwelt in their stead, as Israel did in the land of its inheritance, which the Lord gave unto them.
Now therefore arise, and set forth, and pass through the Ravine Zered. And we passed through the Ravine Zered.

And the time wherein we journeyed from Kadesh-barnea until we passed through the Ravine Zered was thirty and eight years, until the whole generation of men of war had fallen, dying out of the camp, as God had sworn unto them.
And the hand of God was upon them, to consume them out of the camp, until they had fallen.
And it came to pass, when all the men of war had fallen, dying out from among the people,
that the Lord spoke unto me, saying:
You shall pass this day through the borders of Moab, even Seir,

and you shall draw near unto the sons of Ammon. Do not deal as enemies with them, neither join battle with them; for I will give you none of the land of the sons of Ammon for a possession, because I have given it unto the sons of Lot for a possession.
And the Lord said unto me:
It is reckoned a land of Rephaim; for the Rephaim dwelt there aforetime, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a nation great and numerous and mightier than you, like the Anakim. And the Lord destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who inherited the land and dwelt in their stead unto this day,
even as they did for the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, when they blotted out the Horites from before them, and inherited the land, and dwelt in their stead unto this day.
And the Hivites who dwelt in settlements as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came forth from Cappadocia blotted them out, and dwelt in their stead.

Now therefore arise, and set forth, and pass through the Ravine Arnon. Behold, I have delivered into your hands Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to inherit it; join battle with him.
This day begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you before all the nations under heaven, who, when they hear your name, shall be troubled and shall suffer pangs before you.
And I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying:
I will pass through your land. I will pass along the way; I will turn neither to the right nor to the left.
You shall sell me food for silver, and I will eat; and you shall sell me water for silver, and I will drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
as the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, and the Moabites who dwell in Aroer, did for me, until I pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord our God gives us.
Let it suffice you to have compassed this mountain; turn therefore northward.
And Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through his land; for the Lord our God hardened his spirit and strengthened his heart, that he might be delivered into your hands, as at this day.
And the Lord said unto me: Behold, I have begun to deliver before you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to inherit his land.
And Sihon king of Heshbon came out to meet us, he and all his people, unto battle at Jahaz.
And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed every city in succession, with their women and their children; we left none alive as a captive.
Only the cattle we took as plunder, and the spoil of the cities we took.

From Aroer, which is upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, and the city which is in the ravine, even unto the hill country of Gilead, there was no city that escaped us; the Lord our God delivered them all into our hands.
Only unto the land of the sons of Ammon we did not draw near, all that borders upon the torrent Jabbok, and the cities in the hill country, as the Lord our God commanded us.
And command the people, saying: You are passing through the borders of your brethren, the sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir; and they shall fear you, and be exceedingly wary of you.
Do not join battle with them, for I will give you none of their land, no, not so much as a footstep; for I have given Mount Seir unto the sons of Esau for a possession.
Buy food from them for silver, and eat; and you shall take water from them by measure for silver, and drink.

For the Lord our God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. Consider how you passed through that great and fearful wilderness. Behold, these forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.
And we passed by our brethren, the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, along the way of Arabah, from Ailon and from Ezion-geber; and we turned and passed along the wilderness way of Moab.

And the Lord said unto me: Do not deal as enemies with the Moabites, neither join battle with them; for I will give you none of their land for a possession, for I have given Seir unto the sons of Lot to inherit.

And when you go forth unto war against your enemies, and see horse and rider and a people more numerous than you, you shall not fear them; for the Lord your God is with you, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
