And I stood between the Lord and you at that time, to declare unto you the words of the Lord; for you were afraid of the fire, and did not go up into the mountain. He said:
I am the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
You shall not make unto yourself an idol, nor any likeness of anything in heaven above, or upon the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.

You shall not bow down unto them, neither shall you serve them; for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the sins of fathers upon children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate Me,
And these are the commandments, and the ordinances, and the judgments which the Lord our God commanded me to teach you, that you should do them in the land whither you go to inherit it,
And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land which He sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you, great and good cities which you did not build,
houses full of all good things which you did not fill, hewn cisterns which you did not hew, vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant, and you have eaten and are filled,
take heed unto yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him, and you shall cleave unto Him, and you shall swear by His name.
You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the nations round about you,
for the Lord your God in the midst of you is a jealous God; lest the Lord your God be kindled to wrath against you, and destroy you from the face of the earth.
You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested Him at Testing.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, the testimonies and the ordinances which He commanded you.
6:18 And you shall do that which is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, that it may be well with you, and that you may enter and inherit the good land which the Lord sware unto your fathers,
And you shall do that which is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, that it may be well with you, and that you may enter and inherit the good land which the Lord sware unto your fathers,
to drive out all your enemies from before you, as He has spoken.

that you may fear the Lord your God, and keep all His ordinances and His commandments which I command you this day, you, and your sons, and your sons’ sons, all the days of your life, that you may prolong your days.
And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying: What are the testimonies, and the ordinances, and the judgments which the Lord our God commanded us?
that you shall say unto your son: We were household slaves unto Pharaoh in the land of Egypt; and the Lord brought us forth thence with a mighty hand and with an uplifted arm.
And the Lord gave signs and wonders, great and grievous, in Egypt, against Pharaoh and against his house, before our eyes.
And He brought us forth thence, that He might bring us in, to give us this land which He sware to give unto our fathers.
And the Lord commanded us to do all these ordinances, to fear the Lord our God, that it might be well with us all our days, and that we might live, as at this day.
And there shall be mercy for us, if we take heed to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as the Lord commanded us.

And hear, O Israel, and take heed to do them, that it may be well with you, and that you may multiply greatly, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has spoken, to give you a land flowing with milk and honey.

And these are the ordinances and judgments which the Lord commanded the sons of Israel in the wilderness, when they came forth out of the land of Egypt: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength.
And these words, which I command you this day, shall be in your heart and in your soul.
And you shall teach them to your sons, and speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk in the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immovable before your eyes.
And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your houses and of your gates.

And when the Lord your God brings you into the land whither you go to inherit it, and removes great nations from before you, the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations numerous and mightier than you,
and repays them that hate Him to their face, to destroy them. He shall not delay with them that hate Him; He shall repay them to their face.
And you shall keep these commandments, and ordinances, and judgments, which I command you this day to do.
And it shall be, when you hearken unto all these ordinances, and keep and do them, that the Lord your God shall keep with you the covenant and the mercy which He sware unto your fathers.

you shall not fear them. You shall surely remember all that the Lord your God did unto Pharaoh and unto all the Egyptians,

who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and to test you, and to do you good in your latter days.

And it shall be, if you utterly forget the Lord your God, and go after other gods, and serve them, and bow down unto them, I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall surely perish.

And you shall remember all the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, to afflict you and to test you, that the things in your heart might be known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.
As the other nations which the Lord destroys from before you, so shall you perish, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

And He afflicted you, and made you hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers did not know, that He might declare unto you that man shall not live by bread alone, but man shall live by every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.

And I took hold of the two tablets, and cast them out of my two hands, and broke them before your eyes.

And I besought the Lord forty days and forty nights, during which I besought Him; for the Lord had said that He would destroy you.

And I prayed unto God, and said: O Lord, Lord, King of the gods, destroy not Thy people and Thy portion, whom Thou hast redeemed by Thy great strength, whom Thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt by Thy great strength, and by Thy mighty hand, and by Thine uplifted arm.
Remember Thy servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, unto whom Thou didst swear by Thyself. Look not upon the hardness of this people, nor upon their ungodliness, nor upon their sins,

lest the inhabitants of the land whence Thou hast brought us forth say: Because the Lord was not able to bring them into the land which He promised them, and because He hated them, He brought them forth to slay them in the wilderness.

And you shall know this day that the Lord your God does not give you this good land to inherit for your righteous deeds; for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day when you came forth out of Egypt until you came unto this place, you continued in disobedience toward the Lord.

Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, serve the Lord your God. Only leave your sheep and your cattle behind. Let your household go with you.”
And Moses said, “You shall also give us whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, which we shall offer to the Lord our God.

And Pharaoh said, “Depart from me! Take care not to see my face again; for on the day you appear before me, you shall die.”
And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh, and said to him, “Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to reverence Me? Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
But if you will not let My people go, behold, at this hour tomorrow I will bring many locusts upon all your borders.

And they shall cover the face of the land, and you shall not be able to see the land; and they shall devour all that remains of the land which the hail left to you, and every tree growing for you upon the land.

And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your attendants, and all the houses throughout the land of the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor their forefathers have ever seen, from the day they came upon the earth to this day.” And Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh’s attendants said to him, “How long shall this be a hindrance to us? Let the men go, that they may serve their God. Or do you want to know that Egypt is destroyed?”
Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. He said to them, “Go, serve your God. But who are those who will go?”
The Lord said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from here. When he lets you go, he will drive you out altogether, with everything.
Therefore speak secretly in the people’s hearing, and let each man ask his neighbour and each woman her neighbour for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.”
The Lord gave His people favour in the Egyptians’ sight, and they lent to them. The man Moses became very great in the sight of the Egyptians, Pharaoh, and all his attendants.

And all these servants of yours shall come down to me, and bow before me, saying, ‘Go out, you and all your people whom you lead.’ And after this I will go out.” And Moses departed from Pharaoh in anger.

You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.

I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.

For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and from the first day you shall remove leaven out of your houses; whoever eats leaven, from the first day to the seventh day, that soul shall be destroyed from Israel.

The first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be a holy appointed day for you. You shall do no servile work on them, except what must be done for each person; that alone may be done for you.
You shall keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring your host out of the land of Egypt. You shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, from evening until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month, you shall eat unleavened bread.

For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses; whoever eats anything leavened, that soul shall be destroyed from the congregation of Israel, whether a resident foreigner or a native of the land.
“This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.”
Moses called the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, “Go and take a sheep for your families, and slaughter the Passover.
Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood beside the door, and touch the lintel and both doorposts with the blood beside the door. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning.

you shall say to them, ‘This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, because He sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses.’” The people bowed down and worshipped.

Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.

Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

And if your son asks you later, saying, ‘What is this?’ you shall say to him, ‘With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, He killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human firstborn and firstborn of the livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to the Lord every male that opens the womb, and every firstborn of my sons I will redeem.’
And it shall be a sign upon your hand, and a fixed reminder before your eyes; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt.”
“Consecrate to Me every firstborn, the first offspring opening every womb among the sons of Israel, both human and animal. It is Mine.”

And you shall declare to your son in that day, saying, ‘It is because of this that the Lord God acted for me when I came out of Egypt.’
And it shall be to you a sign upon your hand, and a memorial before your eyes, that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand the Lord God brought you out of Egypt.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
Was this not the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness.”

And Moses said to the people, “Take courage; stand, and behold the salvation from God, which He shall accomplish for us today. For as you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall see them no more for ever.
The Lord shall fight for you, and you shall keep silence.”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Why do you cry to Me? Speak to the sons of Israel, that they set forth.

“Speak to the sons of Israel, that they turn back and encamp opposite the settlement, between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon; before them you shall encamp by the sea.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the water return and cover the Egyptians, both their chariots and their riders.”
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and toward daybreak the water returned to its place. The Egyptians fled beneath the water, and the Lord shook the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
Pharaoh will say to his people, ‘These sons of Israel are wandering in the land, for the wilderness has shut them in.’

Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God, saying: “Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider He has cast into the sea.

This is what the Lord commanded: Gather from it, each for those belonging to him, an omer per person according to your number. Each of you shall gather with your tent companions.”
The sons of Israel did so and gathered, some much and some little.
They measured it by the omer. The one with much had no excess, and the one with little had no lack. Each gathered for those belonging to his household.
Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it until morning.”
They did not listen to Moses. Some left part of it until morning, and it swarmed with worms and stank. Moses was embittered against them.
They gathered it morning by morning, each what he needed. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered twice what was needed, two omers per person. All the congregation’s leaders came in and reported it to Moses.

And Moses said to them, “This is the word which the Lord has spoken: Tomorrow is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord. What you would bake, bake; and what you would boil, boil; and all that remains, lay up to keep until morning.”
They left some of it until morning, as Moses instructed them. It did not stink, and no worm was in it.
Moses said, “Eat today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord. It will not be found in the field.
You shall gather for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath; there will be none on it.”
On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found none.
And the Lord said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to listen to My commandments and My law?

Behold, the Lord has given you this day, the Sabbath. Therefore on the sixth day He gave you bread for two days. Each of you shall stay in your houses; no one shall go out from his place on the seventh day.”

And Moses said, “This is the word which the Lord has commanded: Fill an omer with manna to keep throughout your generations, that they may see the bread which you ate in the wilderness, when the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
Moses said to Aaron, “Take one golden jar, put an omerful of manna in it, and set it before God to keep throughout your generations.”
As the Lord instructed Moses, Aaron set it before the Testimony to keep.

And Moses said, “When the Lord gives you meat to eat in the evening, and bread in the morning until you are full, it is because the Lord has heard your murmuring with which you murmur against us. And what are we? For your murmuring is not against us, but against God.”
Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, ‘Come near before God, for He has heard your murmuring.’”

And they shall judge the people at all times; the weighty matter they shall bring to you, but the lesser judgments they shall judge themselves; and they shall lighten your burden, and bear it with you.
If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to stand; and all this people shall come to their own place in peace.”
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times. They brought every weighty matter to Moses, but judged every light matter themselves.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go down, solemnly warn the people, and purify them today and tomorrow. Let them wash their garments

No hand shall touch him; for he shall surely be stoned, or shot through with a dart; whether beast or man, he shall not live. When the sounds and the trumpets and the cloud depart from the mountain, they shall go up upon the mountain.’”
Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated them, and they washed their garments.
He said to the people, “Be ready for three days. Do not approach a woman.”
The Lord descended on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. The Lord called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
God said to Moses, “Go down and solemnly warn the people, lest they come near God to gaze and a multitude of them fall.

And Moses said to God, “The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai; for Thou hast solemnly warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds about the mountain, and consecrate it.’”
And the Lord said to him, “Go, descend, and come up, you and Aaron with you; but do not let the priests and the people force their way up to God, lest the Lord destroy some of them.”

“I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

You shall have no other gods except Me.
You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any likeness of things in heaven above, or in the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.

and showing mercy to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My ordinances.
You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain; for the Lord shall by no means hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain.
Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
For six days you shall labour and do all your works;
“And these are the ordinances which you shall set before them.
And if he takes another wife to himself, he shall not deprive her of her necessities, her clothing, or her conjugal companionship.

If you acquire a Hebrew slave, he shall serve you for six years; and in the seventh year he shall go out free, without payment.

eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
And if a man strikes the eye of his household slave or of his female slave, and blinds it, he shall set them free for their eye.

But if a ransom is imposed on him, he shall give for the ransom of his life all that they impose on him.

And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.

the owner of the pit shall make restitution. He shall give silver to the animal’s owner, and the dead animal shall be his.

an oath by God shall be between them that he has not acted dishonestly concerning any of his neighbour’s deposit. The owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.

“You shall not receive an empty report. You shall not agree with the unrighteous to become an unrighteous witness.
