And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel. The Israelite woman’s son and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
And the Israelite woman’s son pronounced the Name and cursed, and they brought him unto Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
And they placed him in custody, to judge him by the Lord’s command.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.
And speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: A man who curses God shall bear sin.

Let one who names the Lord’s name surely be put to death. Let the whole congregation of Israel stone him with stones. Whether resident foreigner or native-born, when he names the Lord’s name, let him die.
24:17 And if a man strikes a human being and the person dies, he shall surely be put to death.
And if a man strikes a human being and the person dies, he shall surely be put to death.
And one who strikes an animal and it dies shall repay life for life.
And if anyone causes an injury unto his neighbour, as he has done unto him, so shall it be done unto him in return:
Command the sons of Israel to bring Me pure beaten olive oil for light, to burn a lamp continually.
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has caused an injury unto a man, so shall it be inflicted upon him.
24:21 One who strikes a human being and the person dies shall surely be put to death.
One who strikes a human being and the person dies shall surely be put to death.
There shall be one judgment for the resident foreigner and the local inhabitant, for I am the Lord your God.
And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel. They brought the one who cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The sons of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses.
Outside the veil, in the Tent of Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord continually. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations.
You shall burn the lamps upon the pure lampstand before the Lord until morning.
And you shall take fine flour and make twelve loaves from it. Each loaf shall contain two tenths.
And you shall place them in two arrangements, six in each arrangement, on the pure table before the Lord.
And you shall put pure frankincense and salt upon the arrangement. They shall be set before the Lord as a memorial for the loaves.
On the Sabbath day he shall set it before the Lord continually, before the sons of Israel as an everlasting covenant.
And it shall belong unto Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat these things in a holy place, for this is most holy for him from the things sacrificed unto the Lord, an everlasting ordinance.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:

And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout the land unto all who dwell therein; this shall be a year of release, a signal unto you; and each one shall depart unto his possession, and each of you shall depart unto his ancestral homeland.
This is a signal of release: the fiftieth year shall be a year for you. You shall not sow, reap what grows of itself, or gather its consecrated produce.
For it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the fields.
In the year of release, at its signal, each shall return to his possession.
But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.
According to the number of years after the signal you shall acquire from your neighbour; according to the number of harvest years he shall sell to you.
As the years increase, you shall increase its purchase price; as the years decrease, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.
Let no man oppress his neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
And you shall do all My statutes and all My judgments, keep them, and do them; then you shall dwell confidently on the land.
And the land shall yield its produce, and you shall eat to fullness and dwell confidently upon it.
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, the land which I give unto you shall rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord.
But if you say, “What shall we eat in this seventh year, if we neither sow nor gather our produce?”
then I will send My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall produce its harvest for the three years.
And you shall sow in the eighth year and eat old produce. Until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you shall eat old stores from the old.
And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; for you are resident foreigners and lodgers before Me;
and throughout all the land of your possession, you shall provide redemption for the land.
But if your brother who is with you becomes poor, and sells some of his possession, and his nearest kinsman comes, he shall redeem that which his brother sold.
If someone has no kinsman but prospers by his hand and enough is found for his redemption,
then he shall calculate the years of his sale and repay the excess to the man to whom he sold himself; then he shall depart to his possession.

If his hand does not prosper enough to repay him, the sale shall remain with the one who acquired it until the sixth year of release. It shall go out at the release, and he shall depart to his possession.
But if anyone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, its redemption shall be possible until a year of days is fulfilled; that shall be its redemption period.
For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vine and gather its fruit.

If it is not redeemed before its whole year is complete, the house in the city that has a wall shall be confirmed permanently to its buyer throughout his generations. It shall not go out at the release.
But houses in settlements that have no surrounding wall shall be reckoned with the field of the land. They shall always be redeemable and shall go out at the release.
And the cities of the Levites—the houses in their cities of possession—shall always be redeemable by the Levites.

And whosoever redeems from the Levites, the sale of their houses in the city of their possession shall go out at the release; for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the sons of Israel.
And the fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, for this is their everlasting possession.
If your brother becomes poor and grows weak in his hands beside you, you shall support him as a resident foreigner and a lodger, and your brother shall live with you.
You shall take no interest or increase from him, and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
You shall not give him your silver at interest or give your food for an increase.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother is brought low beside you and is sold to you, he shall not serve you with the service of a household slave.
But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath, a rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord. You shall not sow your field or prune your vine.
He shall be with you as a hired worker or a lodger; he shall work beside you until the year of release.
And he shall go out at the release, and his children with him. He shall depart to his kin and return to his ancestral possession.
For these are My household slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; one shall not be sold with the sale of a household slave.
You shall not wear him down with toil, but you shall fear the Lord your God.
And your male slave and your female slave, as many as you have from the nations which are round about you: from them you may acquire a male slave and a female slave.
And you may also acquire from the sons of the lodgers among you and from their relatives who come to be in your land; they shall become your possession.
And you shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be held by you permanently. But among your brethren, the sons of Israel, no one shall wear down his brother with toils.
If the hand of the resident foreigner or lodger beside you gains means, and your brother becomes needy and is sold to the resident foreigner or lodger beside you, a foreigner by birth,
after he is sold to him, he shall have a right of redemption. One of his brethren may redeem him,
his father’s brother or the son of his father’s brother may redeem him, or one of his close kin from his tribe may redeem him; but if, having prospered by his hands, he redeems himself,
And you shall not reap the things growing of themselves in your field or gather the grapes of your consecration. It shall be a year of rest for the land.

then he shall calculate with the one who acquired him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of release. His sale price shall be like a hired worker’s pay; he shall be with him year by year.
If many years remain for someone, he shall repay his redemption from his sale money in proportion to them.
If few years remain until the year of release, he shall calculate with him according to his years and repay his redemption.
He shall be with him as a hired worker year by year; you shall not wear him down with toil before you.
If he is not redeemed by these means, he shall go out in the year of release, he and his children with him.
For the sons of Israel are household slaves to Me; these are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
And the land’s Sabbath produce shall be food for you, your male slave, your female slave, your hired worker, and the lodger attached to you.
And all its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
And you shall count unto yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and the seven weeks of years shall be unto you forty-nine years.

And you shall make proclamation with a trumpet sound throughout your land in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall make proclamation with a trumpet throughout your land.

You shall not make for yourselves images made by hand, neither carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor place a conspicuous stone in your land to bow down unto it; I am the Lord your God.
And you shall eat old stores and old stores of old stores, and clear out the old before the new.
And I will place My covenant among you, and My soul shall not abhor you;
and I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be My people.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt while you were slaves. I shattered the bond of your yoke and led you with boldness.
But if you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
but disobey them, and your soul is indignant at My judgments, so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to dissolve My covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will bring distress upon you, scab and jaundice that waste your eyes and melt away your life. You shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
And I will shatter the arrogance of your pride, and make your heaven iron, and your land as bronze;
You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
and your strength shall be in vain. Your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit.
And if after these things you walk crookedly and will not obey Me, I will add seven blows upon you according to your sins.
And I will send the wild animals of the land against you. They shall devour you, consume your livestock, and make you few, so that your roads become desolate.
And if by these things you are not disciplined, but walk crookedly toward Me,
then I too will walk with you in contrary anger, and I too will strike you seven times in return for your sins.
And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.
When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
If after these things you do not obey Me, but walk crookedly toward Me,
then I Myself will walk with you in contrary anger, and I will discipline you seven times according to your sins.
And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.
If you walk in My ordinances, keep My commandments, and do them,
And I will lay waste your pillars, and destroy your wooden images made by hand, and place your limbs upon the limbs of your idols; and My soul shall be indignant with you;
and I will make your cities desolate, and lay waste your holy places; and I will in no wise smell the savour of your sacrifices;
and I Myself will desolate your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall marvel at it.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you. Your land shall become desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.
Then the land shall welcome its Sabbaths and all the days of its desolation, and you shall be in your enemies’ land. Then the land shall keep Sabbath and welcome its Sabbaths.
All the days of its desolation it shall keep Sabbath for the Sabbaths it did not keep during your Sabbaths when you inhabited it.

And upon those who remain of you I will bring cowardice into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a leaf borne along shall pursue them; and they shall flee as those fleeing from war, and fall when none pursues;
and brother shall disregard brother as in war, though no one runs after them. You shall not be able to withstand your enemies.
And you shall perish among the nations, and your enemies’ land shall devour you.
And those who remain of you shall be ruined because of your sins; they shall waste away in the land of their enemies.
then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
And they shall confess their sins and their fathers’ sins, because they transgressed and disregarded Me, and because they walked crookedly before Me.
And I too walked with them in contrary anger, and I will destroy them in their enemies’ land. Then their uncircumcised heart will feel shame, and then they will accept their sins.
And I will remember the covenant of Jacob and the covenant of Isaac, and the covenant of Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

And the land shall be abandoned by them. Then the land shall receive its Sabbaths when it is desolated because of them, and they shall accept their lawless deeds, because they disregarded My judgments and were indignant at My ordinances in their soul.
And yet even so, while they were in their enemies’ land, I did not disregard them or become indignant with them so as to consume them and dissolve My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
And I will remember for them the former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery, before the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.
These are the judgments and the ordinances and the law which the Lord gave between Himself and the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
And your threshing shall reach the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall reach the sowing. You shall eat your bread to satisfaction and dwell securely in your land.
And war shall not pass through your land. I will give peace in your land. You shall lie down, with no one to frighten you, and I will destroy harmful animals from your land.
And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you in slaughter.
And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue tens of thousands; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
And I will look upon you, increase you, multiply you, and establish My covenant with you.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
He shall not exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does exchange it, animal for animal, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
If it concerns any unclean livestock of a kind not presented as a gift unto the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest.
And the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
If he does redeem it, he shall add a fifth to its valuation.
And if a man consecrates his house as holy unto the Lord, the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it shall be his.
If a man consecrates unto the Lord part of the field of his possession, the valuation shall be according to its seed: fifty didrachmas of silver for a kor of barley.
If he consecrates his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to its valuation.

If he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years remaining until the year of release, and a deduction shall be made from its assessment.
If the one who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall add a fifth of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord,
If he does not redeem the field and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it.
When the release has passed, the field shall be holy unto the Lord like land set apart. It shall become the priest’s possession.
If he consecrates unto the Lord part of a field he acquired, which is not part of the field of his inherited possession,
the priest shall calculate for him the total valuation from the year of release, and he shall repay the valuation on that day as holy unto the Lord.
And in the year of release the field shall be returned to the man from whom he acquired it, whose possession the land was.
And every valuation shall be by sacred weights; the didrachma shall be twenty obols.
And every firstborn which is born among your livestock shall belong unto the Lord, and none shall consecrate it; whether calf or sheep, it is the Lord’s.

If it is one of the unclean four-footed animals, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and add a fifth to it, and it shall be his. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold according to its assessed value.

But every devoted thing which a man dedicates unto the Lord, of all that he has, from man unto livestock, and from the field of his possession, he shall neither sell nor redeem; every devoted thing shall be most holy unto the Lord.
And whatsoever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.
the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight.
Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord.
But if a man indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add a fifth part unto it, and it shall be his.
And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.
You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; but if you do indeed exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.
For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female.
From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.
If it concerns livestock of a kind presented as a gift unto the Lord, whatever one gives from these unto the Lord shall be holy.
And if his gift unto the Lord is a sacrifice of deliverance, if he brings it from his cattle, whether male or female, he shall bring it unblemished before the Lord.
and both kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver, removing it with the kidneys;

and lay his hands upon its head; and they shall slaughter it before the Lord beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood round about upon the altar.
And from it he shall offer up an offering unto the Lord: the fat which covers the belly, and all the fat upon the belly,
and both kidneys, and all the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer it up upon the altar: an offering, a sweet savour unto the Lord. All the fat is the Lord’s.

And from the sacrifice of deliverance they shall bring an offering unto the Lord: the fat which covers the belly, and all the fat upon the belly,
and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer them up upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offerings, upon the wood upon the fire upon the altar: an offering, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And if his gift is from the flock, as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, whether male or female, he shall bring it unblemished.
If he brings a lamb as his gift, he shall bring it before the Lord,
and lay his hands upon the head of his gift, and slaughter it beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood round about upon the altar.

as it is taken from the calf of the sacrifice of deliverance; and the priest shall offer it up upon the altar of offering.

they shall carry the whole calf outside the camp unto a clean place, where they pour out the ashes, and burn it upon wood with fire; it shall be burned upon the place where the ashes are poured out.

And if the whole congregation of Israel is unintentionally ignorant, and a matter escapes the eyes of the congregation, and they do any of the things which the commandments of the Lord forbid, and commit an offence,
and the sin which they have committed becomes known unto them, the congregation shall bring an unblemished calf from the cattle for sin, and bring it beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands upon the calf’s head before the Lord, and they shall slaughter the calf before the Lord.
And the anointed priest shall bring some of the calf’s blood into the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall dip his finger in some of the calf’s blood, and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the holy veil.

And the priest shall put some of the blood upon the horns of the altar of compounded incense, which is before the Lord, which is in the Tent of Testimony; and he shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of offerings beside the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And he shall remove all the fat from it, and offer it up upon the altar.
Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a soul sins unintentionally before the Lord against the ordinances of the Lord concerning things which must not be done, and does any one of them:
And he shall do with the calf as he did with the calf of the sin offering; thus it shall be done. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and their sin shall be forgiven them.
And they shall carry the whole calf outside the camp, and burn the calf as they burned the former calf. It is the sin offering of the congregation.
And if the ruler sins, and unintentionally does any of the things which the commandments of the Lord their God forbid, and sins and commits an offence,
and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring as his gift an unblemished male young goat from the goats.
And he shall lay his hand upon the young goat’s head; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

And the priest shall put some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings.
And he shall offer up all its fat upon the altar, as the fat of a sacrifice of deliverance. And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.
And if one soul from the people of the land sins unintentionally, by doing any of the things which the commandments of the Lord forbid, and commits an offence,
and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring an unblemished female young goat from the goats; he shall bring it for the sin which he has committed.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his sin offering; and they shall slaughter the female young goat of the sin offering in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.
if the anointed high priest sins so that the people sin, he shall bring, for his sin which he has committed, an unblemished calf from the cattle unto the Lord, for his sin.
And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar.

And he shall remove all the fat, as fat is removed from a sacrifice of deliverance; and the priest shall offer it up upon the altar for a sweet savour unto the Lord. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
And if he brings a sheep as his gift for a sin offering, he shall bring an unblemished female.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sin offering; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of whole burning; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burning.

And he shall remove all its fat, as the fat of a sheep is removed from the sacrifice of deliverance; and the priest shall place it upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offering of the Lord. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.
And he shall bring the calf beside the door of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord, and lay his hand upon the calf’s head before the Lord, and slaughter the calf in the presence of the Lord.
And the anointed priest whose hands have been consecrated shall take some of the calf’s blood, and bring it into the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the Lord, toward the holy veil.

And the priest shall put some of the calf’s blood upon the horns of the altar of compounded incense before the Lord, which is in the Tent of Testimony; and he shall pour out all the calf’s blood beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings, which is beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And he shall remove all the fat from the calf of the sin offering: the fat which covers the inward parts, and all the fat upon the inward parts,
and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys,
And if a soul sins, and hears the voice of a solemn adjuration, and he is a witness, whether he has seen or has knowledge of the matter, if he does not declare it, he shall bear the sin.
And he shall prepare the second as a whole burnt offering, as is fitting. And the priest shall make atonement for the sin which he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

And if his hand cannot obtain a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring his gift for the sin which he has committed: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour for sin. He shall pour no oil upon it, neither shall he put frankincense upon it, for it is for sin.
And he shall bring it unto the priest; and the priest shall take from it a full handful, and place its memorial portion upon the altar of whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a sin offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed in any one of these matters, and he shall be forgiven. But what remains shall be the priest’s, as the sacrifice of fine flour.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

If a soul is overtaken by forgetfulness, and sins unintentionally concerning the holy things of the Lord, he shall bring unto the Lord for his offence an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, for the offence which he has committed.

And he shall repay that wherein he has sinned against the holy things, and add a fifth part unto it, and give it unto the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven.
And if a soul sins, and does any of the things which the commandments of the Lord forbid, though he did not know it, and incurs guilt and bears the sin,

he shall bring unto the priest an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver, for a guilt offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his ignorance, wherein he acted ignorantly and did not know it, and he shall be forgiven.
For he has indeed committed an offence before the Lord.

Or if a soul touches any unclean thing, whether a dead thing, or an unclean thing torn by wild beasts, or one of the dead things, or one of the unclean abominations, or a carcass of unclean livestock,
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

If a soul sins, and utterly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and deals falsely with his neighbour concerning a deposit, or a partnership, or robbery, or any wrong which he has done unto his neighbour,
or finds a lost thing and deals falsely concerning it, and swears unjustly concerning any of all the things which a man may do so as to sin therein,

then it shall be, when he has sinned and incurred guilt, that he shall return the plunder which he seized, or that which he obtained by wrong, or the deposit which was entrusted unto him, or the lost thing which he found,

concerning every matter about which he swore unjustly. And he shall repay the principal, and add a fifth part unto it; he shall repay it unto the one to whom it belongs, on the day when he is convicted.
And for his offence he shall bring unto the Lord an unblemished ram from the flock, of a value corresponding to the offence which he has committed against Him.
And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.
or touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness of a man by touching which he is defiled, and it escapes his notice, but afterward he knows it and incurs guilt;
or if a soul swears, declaring with his lips to do evil or to do good, whatsoever a man declares with an oath, and it escapes his notice, and he knows it and sins in any one of these matters,
he shall confess the sin concerning that wherein he has sinned.

And he shall bring unto the Lord, for the offence and the sin which he has committed, a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female young goat from the goats, for sin. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed, and his sin shall be forgiven him.

And if his hand cannot provide enough for a sheep, he shall bring unto the Lord for the sin which he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
And he shall bring them unto the priest, and the priest shall bring the one for sin first; and the priest shall pinch its head at the neck joint, but shall not divide it.
And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the offering for sin upon the wall of the altar; but the remaining blood he shall drain at the base of the altar, for it is for sin.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it unto them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; it is most holy, as the offering for sin and the guilt offering.
Every male among the priests shall eat it; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations, from the offerings of the Lord. Whosoever touches them shall be sanctified.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

This is the gift of Aaron and his sons which they shall bring unto the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour as a continual sacrifice, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It shall be made upon a griddle with oil; he shall bring it mixed, in rolled pieces, a sacrifice of fragments, a sacrifice for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his stead shall prepare it. It is an everlasting law; it shall all be fully performed.
And every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burned, and shall not be eaten.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Speak unto Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the offerings for sin before the Lord; they are most holy.
The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.

Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of whole burning. The whole burnt offering shall remain upon its burning place upon the altar all night until morning; and the fire of the altar shall burn upon it, and shall not be quenched.
Whosoever touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and if any of its blood is sprinkled upon a garment, what it was sprinkled upon shall be washed in a holy place.
And the earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water.
Every male among the priests shall eat them; they are most holy unto the Lord.
And none of the offerings for sin whose blood is brought into the Tent of Testimony to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten; they shall be burned with fire.

And the priest shall put on a linen tunic, and he shall put linen undergarments about his body; and he shall remove from the altar the burnt remains of the whole burning which the fire has consumed, and place them beside the altar.
And he shall take off his robe, and put on another robe, and carry the burnt remains outside the camp unto a clean place.

And the fire upon the altar shall burn from it, and shall not be quenched; and the priest shall burn wood upon it in the morning, and pile the whole burnt offering upon it, and place upon it the fat of the offering of deliverance.
And a fire shall burn continually upon the altar; it shall not be quenched.
This is the law of the sacrifice which the sons of Aaron shall bring before the Lord, opposite the altar.

And he shall take a handful from the fine flour of the sacrifice, with its oil and the frankincense upon the sacrifice, and offer it up upon the altar as an offering: a sweet savour, its memorial portion unto the Lord.
But Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
And this is the law of the ram for the guilt offering; it is most holy.
And every sacrifice prepared with oil, or not so prepared, shall belong unto all the sons of Aaron, unto each an equal share.
This is the law of the sacrifice of deliverance which they shall bring unto the Lord.
If he brings it for praise, he shall bring with the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour prepared with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil.
He shall bring his gifts with leavened loaves, with a sacrifice of praise and deliverance.
And he shall bring one of all his gifts as a portion set apart unto the Lord; it shall belong unto the priest who pours the blood of the offering of deliverance.
And the flesh of the sacrifice of praise and deliverance shall be his, and shall be eaten on the day when it is given; they shall leave none of it until morning.
And if he sacrifices his gift as a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day when he brings his sacrifice, and on the morrow.
And what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire.

But if he eats any of the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for him who brings it, neither shall it be reckoned unto him; it is a defilement. And the soul that eats of it shall bear the sin.
And flesh which touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Whosoever is clean shall eat flesh.
In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord; and he shall pour the blood round about upon the base of the altar.
But the soul that eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall perish from among his people.

And if a soul touches any unclean thing, human uncleanness, or unclean four-footed beasts, or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, that soul shall perish from among his people.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: You shall eat no fat of cattle, or sheep, or goats.
And fat from animals that have died, or from those torn by wild beasts, may be used for any work; but it shall in no wise be eaten as food.
Whosoever eats fat from the livestock from which an offering is brought unto the Lord, that soul shall perish from among his people.
You shall eat no blood in any dwelling place of yours, whether of birds or of livestock.

7:26 You shall eat no blood in any dwelling place of yours, whether of birds or of livestock.

7:27 Every soul that eats blood, that soul shall perish from among his people.
Every soul that eats blood, that soul shall perish from among his people.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: He who brings a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord shall bring his gift unto the Lord from the sacrifice of deliverance.
And he shall bring all its fat from it: the loin, and all the fat which covers the inward parts, and all the fat upon the inward parts,
His hands shall bring the offerings unto the Lord: the fat upon the breast and the lobe of the liver; he shall bring them to place them as a gift before the Lord.
And the priest shall offer up the fat upon the altar; and the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.
And the right foreleg you shall give as a portion set apart unto the priest from your sacrifices of deliverance.
He among the sons of Aaron who brings the blood of the offering of deliverance and the fat shall have the right foreleg as his portion.

For the breast of the presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart have I taken from the sons of Israel, from your sacrifices of deliverance; and I have given them unto Aaron the priest and unto his sons as an everlasting statute from the sons of Israel.
This is Aaron’s anointing and the anointing of his sons from the offerings of the Lord, on the day when he brought them forward to serve as priests unto the Lord,
as the Lord commanded to be given them from the sons of Israel on the day when he anointed them: an everlasting statute throughout their generations.
This is the law of the whole burnt offerings, and the sacrifice, and the offering for sin, and the guilt offering, and the consecration, and the sacrifice of deliverance,
as the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day when He commanded the sons of Israel to bring their gifts before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver; these he shall remove with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer them up upon the altar as an offering unto the Lord. It is for guilt.
Every male among the priests shall eat them; they shall eat them in a holy place. They are most holy.
As the offering for sin, so also the guilt offering: one law is theirs. It shall belong unto the priest who makes atonement with it.
And the priest who brings a man’s whole burnt offering shall have the hide of the whole burnt offering which he brings.
And every sacrifice made in an oven, and every sacrifice made upon a hearth or upon a griddle, shall belong unto the priest who brings it.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And Moses took some of the anointing oil,

and sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with belts, and put turbans on them, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the calf for the sin offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.
And Moses took all the fat on the inward parts, the lobe on the liver, both kidneys and the fat on them, and Moses offered them up on the altar.
And he burned up the calf, its hide, its flesh, and its dung with fire outside the camp, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the ram for the whole burnt offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And he divided the ram limb by limb, and Moses offered up the head, the limbs, and the fat.
And he washed the belly and feet with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar: a whole burnt offering for a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Moses brought the second ram forward, a ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it upon Aaron’s right earlobe, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.

And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on their right earlobes, the extremities of their right hands, and the extremities of their right feet. Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he took the fat, the loin, the fat on the belly, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right foreleg.
And from the basket of consecration before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and the right foreleg.
And he put everything on Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands and offered them up as a portion set apart before the Lord.
And Moses took them from their hands, and Moses offered them up on the altar upon the whole burnt offering of consecration, which is a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
And Moses took the breast and removed it as a presentation before the Lord from the ram of consecration. It became Moses’ portion, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.

And Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him. He consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

And Moses said unto Aaron and his sons: Boil the flesh in the court of the Tent of Testimony, in a holy place, and there you shall eat it, and the loaves in the basket of consecration, as I have been directed, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them.
And what remains of the flesh and loaves shall be burned up with fire.
And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, until the day is fulfilled, the day of your consecration; for he shall consecrate your hands for seven days.
As he has done this day, the Lord commanded it to be done, to make atonement for you.
And you shall remain at the door of the Tent of Testimony seven days, day and night; you shall keep the charges of the Lord, so that you do not die, for thus the Lord God commanded me.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses did as the Lord directed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses said unto the congregation: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

And he clothed him with the tunic, girded him with the belt, clothed him with the under-robe, and put the shoulder-piece on him. He girded him according to the shoulder-piece’s workmanship and fastened him securely in it.
And he placed the oracle-piece on it and put Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece.
And he put the turban on his head and placed on its front the gold plate, the consecrated holy object, as the Lord directed Moses.
And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.
And he offered up the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver of the sin offering on the altar, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he burned up the flesh and hide with fire outside the camp.
And he slaughtered the whole burnt offering. Aaron’s sons brought him the blood, and he poured it all around against the altar.
And they brought him the whole burnt offering limb by limb, the parts and the head, and he placed them on the altar.
And he washed the belly and feet with water and placed them upon the whole burnt offering on the altar.
And they presented the gift of the people; and he took the male young goat for the sin offering of the people, and slaughtered it as the first.
And he presented the whole burnt offering and prepared it as was fitting.
And he presented the sacrifice, filled his hands with some of it, and placed it on the altar, apart from the morning whole burnt offering.
And he slaughtered the calf and ram of the people’s sacrifice of deliverance. Aaron’s sons brought him the blood, and he poured it all around against the altar.
And as for the fat from the calf and ram—the loin, the fat covering the belly, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the lobe on the liver—
And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.
he placed the fat upon the breasts; and they offered up the fat upon the altar.
And Aaron removed the breast and the right foreleg as a portion set apart before the Lord, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Aaron lifted his hands over the people and blessed them. He came down after preparing the offering for sin, the whole burnt offerings, and the deliverance offerings.
And Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Testimony. They came out and blessed all the people, and the Lord’s glory appeared to all the people.
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed what was on the altar, both the whole burnt offerings and the fat. All the people saw, were astonished, and fell on their faces.
And speak unto the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male young goat from the goats for sin, and a calf and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a whole offering,
and a calf and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.
And they brought what Moses commanded opposite the Tent of Testimony, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the Lord.
And Moses said: Do this thing which the Lord said, and the glory of the Lord shall appear among you.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Draw near unto the altar, and prepare your offering for sin and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your house; and prepare the gifts of the people, and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Aaron drew near unto the altar and slaughtered the calf for the sin offering.
And Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood, put it on the altar’s horns, and poured the blood at the altar’s base.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Testimony, on the first day of the second month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, saying:
For the sons of Joseph: for Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; for Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
For Benjamin: Abidan son of Gideoni.
For Dan: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
For Asher: Pagiel son of Ocran.
For Gad: Eliasaph son of Reuel.
For Naphtali: Ahira son of Enan.
These are the men called from the congregation, rulers of the tribes by ancestral houses; they are commanders of Israel’s thousands.
And Moses and Aaron took these men who had been called by name.

And they assembled the whole congregation on the first day of the month of the second year and registered them by their descent and ancestral houses, counting their names, from twenty years old and upward, every male, head by head.
As the Lord instructed Moses, they were registered in the wilderness of Sinai.
Take the sum of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, by their families, by their ancestral houses, according to the number of their names, head by head, every male
from twenty years old and upward, every one who goes out in Israel’s army: register them with their army; you and Aaron shall register them.
And one of the rulers from each tribe shall be with you; they shall be according to their ancestral houses.
But the Levites, from their ancestral tribe, were not registered among the sons of Israel.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
See that you do not register the tribe of Levi together with them, neither shall you take their number among the sons of Israel.
And these are the names of the men who shall stand with you. For Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur.

And you shall appoint the Levites over the Tent of Testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that is therein. They shall carry the Tent and all its furnishings, and they shall minister therein, and shall camp round about the Tent.
And when the Tent sets out, the Levites shall take it down; when it camps, they shall erect it. Let an outsider who approaches die.
And the sons of Israel shall camp, each in his own formation and each according to his own command, with their army.

But let the Levites camp before the Lord round about the Tent of Testimony, and there shall be no offence among the sons of Israel. And the Levites themselves shall keep the charge of the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel did everything that the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.
For Simeon: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
For Judah: Nahshon son of Amminadab.
For Issachar: Nethanel son of Zuar.
For Zebulun: Eliab son of Helon.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And in the days of your gladness, and at your feasts, and at your new moons, you shall blow the trumpets over your whole burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of deliverance; and it shall be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.
And in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud rose from the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel set out with their equipment in the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud stood in the wilderness of Paran.
And they set out first by the voice of the Lord through Moses.
Make two silver trumpets for yourself; you shall make them of hammered work; and they shall be for you to summon the congregation and to set the camps in motion.

And Moses said unto Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ kinsman by marriage: We are setting out for the place of which the Lord said: I will give this unto you. Come with us, and we will do you good; for the Lord has spoken good concerning Israel.
And you shall blow them, and the whole congregation shall gather at the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And he said: Do not leave us, for you were with us in the wilderness, and you shall be an elder among us.
But if they blow one, all the rulers, the leaders of Israel, shall come unto you.
And you shall blow a signal, and the camps encamped toward the east shall set out.

And you shall blow a second signal, and the camps encamped toward the southwest shall set out; and you shall blow a third signal, and the camps encamped toward the sea shall set out; and you shall blow a fourth signal, and the camps encamped toward the north shall set out. They shall blow a signal at their departure.
And when you gather the congregation, you shall blow, but not with a signal.
And Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be an everlasting statute for you throughout your generations.

But if you go out to war in your land against the adversaries who resist you, you shall give a signal with the trumpets; and you shall be remembered before the Lord, and shall be delivered from your enemies.
Where can I get meat to give all this people? For they weep before me, saying: Give us meat to eat!

And the Lord said unto Moses: Gather unto Me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you yourself know to be elders of the people and their scribes; and you shall bring them unto the Tent of Testimony, and they shall stand there with you.

And I will come down and speak there with you, and will take of the Spirit that is upon you and put it upon them; and they shall help you bear the onrush of the people, and you shall not bear them alone.

And you shall say unto the people: Purify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat; for you wept before the Lord, saying: Who will feed us meat? For it is well with us in Egypt. And the Lord will give you meat to eat, and you shall eat meat.
You shall eat not for one day, nor for two, nor for five days, nor for ten days, nor for twenty days;

for a whole month you shall eat, until it comes out of your nostrils, and it shall be unto you a bilious sickness; because you disobeyed the Lord, who is among you, and wept before Him, saying: Why did we come out of Egypt?
And Moses said: The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand on foot; and Thou hast said: I will give them meat to eat, and they shall eat for a whole month.
Could sheep and cattle be slaughtered for them and be enough? Could all the food of the sea be gathered for them and be enough?
And the Lord said unto Moses: Shall the hand of the Lord not suffice? Now you shall know whether My word shall overtake you or not.
And Moses went out and told the people the Lord’s words. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

And the Lord came down in a cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the Spirit that was upon him and put it upon the seventy men, the elders. When the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not do so again.
And the Lord said unto Moses: If her father had spat in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days? Let her be set apart outside the camp for seven days; afterward she shall enter.
And Miriam was set apart outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was cleansed.
And afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
And immediately the Lord said unto Moses, Miriam, and Aaron: Come out, all three of you, to the Tent of Testimony. And the three came out to the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony. Aaron and Miriam were called, and both came forward.
And He said unto them: Hear My words: If there is a prophet among you unto the Lord, I will make Myself known unto him in a vision, and I will speak unto him in sleep.
Not so My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
I will speak unto him mouth to mouth, in visible appearance, and not through riddles; and he saw the glory of the Lord. And why were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?
And the Lord’s fierce anger was upon them, and He departed.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, of the sons of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Iabi;
from the tribe of Gad, Gaddiel son of Machi.
These were the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses named Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
And Moses sent them to search out the land of Canaan, and said unto them: Go up by this wilderness, and you shall go up into the hill country;
and you shall see the land, what it is, and the people settled upon it, whether they are stronger or weak, whether they are few or many;
And is the land on which they are settled good or bad? What are the towns in which they live—walled or unwalled?

Send men for yourself, and let them search out the land of the Canaanites, which I give unto the sons of Israel for a possession. You shall send one man from each tribe, according to the groups of their ancestral families, each a leader among them.

And what is the land like—rich or neglected? Are there trees therein or not? And persevere, and you shall take of the fruits of the land. And the days were days of spring, forerunners of the grape harvest.
And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran through the Lord’s voice. All these men were leaders of the sons of Israel.
And these were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Salamiel son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Souri;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
And the whole congregation raised its voice, and the people wept all that night.
And the whole congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the Lord’s glory appeared in a cloud over the Tent of Testimony among all the sons of Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses: How long will this people provoke Me? How long will they refuse to believe Me, despite all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with death and destroy them, and I will make you and your father’s house into a nation greater and much more numerous than this one.
And Moses said unto the Lord: Egypt will hear that by Thy strength Thou didst bring this people up from among them.

Indeed, all those living in this land have heard that Thou, the Lord, art among this people, that Thou appearest eye to eye, O Lord, and that Thy cloud stands over them, and Thou goest before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
And if Thou wipe out this people as one man, the nations who have heard Thy name will say,
Because the Lord was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to them, He laid them low in the wilderness.
And now let Thy strength be exalted, O Lord, as Thou hast spoken, saying:

The Lord is long-suffering, and abundant in mercy, and true, taking away lawlessness and wrongdoing and sins; yet He will in no wise cleanse the guilty, repaying the sins of fathers upon children unto the third and fourth generations.
Forgive this people’s sin according to Thy great mercy, as Thou hast been gracious to them from Egypt until now.
And all the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron. The whole congregation said to them: If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
And the Lord said unto Moses: I am gracious to them according to your word.
But as I live, and as My name lives, the glory of the Lord shall fill all the earth;
all the men who have seen My glory and the signs I did in Egypt and this wilderness, and have tested Me this tenth time and have not listened to My voice,

shall certainly not see the land I swore to their fathers. But their children who are here with Me, who do not know good or evil, every inexperienced young person—to these I will give the land. None of those who provoke Me shall see it.
But My servant Caleb, because a different spirit was in him and he followed Me, I will bring into the land he entered, and his seed shall inherit it.
Amalek and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn and depart for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
And why is the Lord bringing us into this land to fall in war? Our wives and children will become plunder. So now it is better for us to return to Egypt.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And I will bring into the land the children whom you said would become plunder, and they shall inherit the land from which you turned away.
And your bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
But your sons shall live as herders in the wilderness for forty years and bear your whoredom, until your bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
According to the number of days you searched out the land—forty days, a day for a year—you shall bear your sins for forty years, and you shall know the fury of My anger.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I will certainly do this to this evil congregation that has banded together against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
And the men Moses had sent to inspect the land came back and grumbled against it before the congregation, bringing out evil words about the land.
And those men who spoke evil against the land died in the plague before the Lord.
And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived, out of those men who had gone to explore the land.
And Moses spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
And they said to one another, Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.
And they rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying: Here we are! We will go up to the place the Lord has spoken of, for we have sinned.
And Moses said: Why do you transgress the Lord’s word? Things will not go well for you.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you, and you shall fall before your enemies.
Amalek and the Canaanites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you turned away in disobedience unto the Lord, the Lord will not be among you.
And they forced their way up to the top of the mountain. The ark of the Lord’s covenant and Moses did not move from the camp.
And Amalek and the Canaanites who lived on that mountain came down, routed them, and cut them down as far as Erman. Then they returned to the camp.
And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, among those who had explored the land, tore their garments.
And they said to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel: The land we inspected is exceedingly, exceedingly good.
If the Lord chooses us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not become deserters from the Lord. Do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. Their season has passed away from them, but the Lord is among us. Do not fear them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
and half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
Thus you shall do for each calf, or each ram, or each lamb from the sheep or from the goats.
According to the number that you prepare, thus you shall do for each one according to their number.
Every native-born person shall do such things in this way when presenting offerings of sweet savour unto the Lord.

But if a sojourner who joins you in your land, or whosoever is among you throughout your generations, makes an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, as you do, so shall the congregation do unto the Lord.
You shall have one law, both you and the sojourners joined unto you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the sojourner be before the Lord.
One law and one ordinance shall apply to you and the sojourner attached to you.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land whither I bring you,
then it shall be, when you eat of the loaves of the land, that you shall take a portion, a gift set apart unto the Lord.
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land of your dwelling, which I give unto you,
As the firstfruits of your dough, you shall set apart a loaf for a portion set apart; as a portion from the threshing floor, so you shall take it,
the firstfruits of your dough; and you shall give unto the Lord a portion set apart throughout your generations.
But when you err, and do not carry out all these commandments which the Lord spoke unto Moses,
as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave command to you and onward throughout your generations,

And if it happened unintentionally, out of the congregation’s sight, the whole congregation shall prepare one unblemished calf from the cattle as a whole burnt offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, with its sacrifice and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat for sin.

And the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, and they shall be forgiven, because it was unintentional. They have brought their gift, an offering unto the Lord for their sin, before the Lord for their unintentional acts.
And forgiveness shall extend throughout the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and to the sojourner attached to you, because it was unintentional for the whole people.
But if one soul sins unintentionally, he shall present one year-old female goat for sin.
And the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who acted unintentionally and sinned unintentionally, making atonement for that person.
For the native among the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner joined unto them, they shall have one law for whosoever acts unintentionally.

and you make whole burnt offerings unto the Lord, a whole offering or a sacrifice, to honour a vow, or willingly, or at your feasts, to make a sweet savour unto the Lord, whether from the cattle or from the sheep,
And the soul that acts with a presumptuous hand, whether of the natives or of the sojourners, provokes God; that soul shall be destroyed from his people,
because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is upon him.
And while the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
And those who found him gathering wood on the Sabbath day brought him unto Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
And they placed him in custody, because they had not determined what they should do to him.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: The man must certainly be put to death. Stone him with stones, all the congregation.
And the whole congregation brought him outside the camp, and the whole congregation stoned him with stones outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Let them make for themselves fringes upon the corners of their garments throughout their generations; and you shall put a blue thread upon the fringes of the corners.

And it shall be among your fringes; and you shall see them, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them; and you shall not turn aside after your thoughts and after your eyes, after which you go a whoring,
And the one presenting a gift unto the Lord shall bring a sacrifice of one tenth of an oiphi of fine flour mixed with one quarter of a hin of oil.
that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.
And you shall prepare wine for a drink offering, a fourth of a hin, with the whole burning or with the sacrifice; you shall prepare this much for each lamb, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And for a ram, when you prepare it for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice, you shall prepare a sacrifice of two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a third of a hin.
And you shall present wine for a drink offering, a third of a hin, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
But if you prepare an animal from the cattle for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice to honour a vow, or for a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord,
he shall present with the calf a sacrifice of three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, half a hin,
And He brought you near, and all your brethren, the sons of Levi, with you. Do you seek to serve as priests?
Thus you and all your congregation have gathered against God. As for Aaron, who is he, that you grumble against him?
And Moses said to Korah: Consecrate your congregation, and be ready before the Lord tomorrow, you, they, and Aaron.
And each of you shall take his fire pan and place incense on it; each shall present his fire pan before the Lord, two hundred fifty fire pans. You and Aaron shall each bring his fire pan.
And each took his fire pan, put fire on it, and placed incense on it. Moses and Aaron stood beside the entrances of the Tent of Testimony.
And Korah gathered all his congregation against them beside the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, and the Lord’s glory appeared to the whole congregation.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once.
And they fell on their faces and said: O God, God of the spirits and of all flesh, if one man sinned, will the Lord’s anger be against the whole congregation?
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the congregation, saying: Withdraw all around from Korah’s congregation.
And Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and all the elders of Israel went with him.
And he said to the congregation: Separate yourselves from the tents of these stubborn men. Touch none of their possessions, lest you perish with them in all their sin.
And they withdrew from around Korah’s tent. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood beside the entrances of their tents, with their wives, their children, and their baggage.
And Moses said: By this you shall know that the Lord sent me to do all these deeds, and that they did not come from myself.
If these men die the death of all people, and a visitation comes upon them according to the visitation of all people, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord displays a portent, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them, their households, their tents, and everything that belongs to them, and they go down alive to Hades, then you shall know that these men have provoked the Lord.

And he said to Korah and all his congregation, God has looked upon and known those who are His and those who are holy, and has brought them near to Himself. Those He chose for Himself He brought near to Himself.
Do this: take fire pans for yourselves, Korah and all his congregation.
And put fire on them and place incense on them before the Lord tomorrow. The man the Lord chooses shall be holy. Let that suffice for you, sons of Levi!
And Moses said to Korah: Listen to me, sons of Levi.

Is this too little for you, that the God of Israel distinguished you from Israel’s congregation and brought you near to Himself to perform the ministries of the Lord’s tent and stand before the congregation to serve them?
And the Lord said unto Moses
Withdraw from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once. They fell on their faces.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Take the fire pan, put fire from the altar on it, and place incense on it. Carry it quickly into the camp and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord; it has begun to strike the people.
And Aaron took it just as Moses had told him and ran into the congregation. The outbreak had already begun among the people. He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,
and stood between the dead and the living, and the outbreak subsided.
And those who died in the outbreak numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from those who died because of Korah.
And Aaron returned unto Moses at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, and the outbreak subsided.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and take from them one staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
And write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for they shall give one staff for each tribe of their ancestral houses.
And you shall place them in the Tent of Testimony, opposite the testimony, where I will make Myself known unto you.
and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: Take up the bronze fire pans from among those burned up, and scatter this strange fire there, for they have consecrated
And the staff of the man I choose shall sprout. I will remove from Myself the sons of Israel’s grumbling, which they direct against you.
And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one staff for each leader according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.
And Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the Tent of Testimony.
And the next day Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Testimony, and there Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted: it brought forth a shoot, flowered with blossoms, and produced nuts.
And Moses brought all the staffs out from before the Lord to all the sons of Israel. They looked, and each man took his staff.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Put Aaron’s staff before the testimonies, to be kept as a sign for the sons of the disobedient. Let their grumbling against Me cease, and they shall certainly not die.
And Moses and Aaron did so. Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so they did.
And the sons of Israel said unto Moses: Behold, we are consumed! We are lost! We are utterly spent!
Everyone who touches the Lord’s tent dies. Must we die to the very end?

the fire pans of these sinners at the cost of their lives. Make them into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, because they were presented before the Lord and were made holy, and became a sign to the sons of Israel.
And Eleazar son of Aaron the priest took the bronze fire pans presented by those who had been burned, and they applied them as a covering for the altar,

as a reminder to the sons of Israel that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to place incense before the Lord, so that he will not become like Korah and his faction, as the Lord had spoken through Moses.
And the next day the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the Lord’s people!
And when the congregation banded together against Moses and Aaron, they rushed toward the Tent of Testimony. The cloud covered it, and the Lord’s glory appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came into the area before the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
And the Lord said unto Aaron, saying: You and your sons and your father’s house shall bear the sins concerning the holy things; and you and your sons shall bear the sins concerning your priesthood.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.
Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.
And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.
And bring your brethren, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near unto you; and let them join you and minister unto you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
