And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And you shall speak unto the Levites, and shall say unto them: When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for an allotment, you shall take from it a portion set apart unto the Lord, a tithe of the tithe.
And your portions set apart shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as a portion set apart from the winepress.

Thus you shall also take of the portions set apart unto the Lord, from all your tithes which you receive from the sons of Israel; and from them you shall give a portion set apart unto the Lord unto Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts you shall take a portion set apart unto the Lord, or from all the firstfruits the consecrated portion thereof.
And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
And you shall say unto them: When you take the firstfruits from it, it shall be reckoned unto the Levites as produce from the threshing floor and as produce from the winepress.
And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your wage in return for your ministries in the Tent of Testimony.
And you shall incur no sin through it, when you take the firstfruits from it; and you shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, lest you die.
And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.
And you shall keep the charges of the holy things and the charges of the altar, and there shall be no wrath among the sons of Israel.
And I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel, a gift given unto the Lord, to perform the ministries of the Tent of Testimony.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil; and you shall perform the ministries, a gift of your priesthood; and the outsider who approaches shall die.

And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
And the one who gathers the heifer's ashes shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for the sons of Israel and the attached sojourners.
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

This is the provision of the law which the Lord commanded, saying: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and let them bring unto you a red heifer without blemish, wherein is no defect, and upon which no yoke has been laid.

And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.
And you shall give it unto Eleazar the priest, and they shall bring it outside the camp unto a clean place, and shall slaughter it before him.
And Eleazar shall take some of its blood and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the Tent of Testimony.
And they shall burn it before him; its skin, flesh, and blood, together with its dung, shall be burned.
And the priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material, and they shall throw them into the burning heifer.
And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening.
And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes and bathe his body, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And a clean person shall gather the heifer's ashes and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the sons of Israel as water of sprinkling; it is a means of purification.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
The formation of the camp of Reuben, with their army, shall be toward the southwest. The ruler of the sons of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-six thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Simeon; the ruler of the sons of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Gad; the ruler of the sons of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
All those registered in the camp of Reuben, with their army, numbered one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty. They shall set out second.
And the Tent of Testimony and the camp of the Levites shall be raised in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they shall set out, each beside his neighbour according to command.
The formation of the camp of Ephraim, with their army, shall be toward the sea. The ruler of the sons of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His army, those registered, numbered forty thousand five hundred.
Let the sons of Israel camp, each beside his neighbour, by formation and by the signs of their ancestral houses. The sons of Israel shall camp opposite, around the Tent of Testimony.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Manasseh; the ruler of the sons of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His army, those registered, numbered thirty-two thousand two hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Benjamin; the ruler of the sons of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His army, those registered, numbered thirty-five thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Ephraim, with their army, numbered one hundred eight thousand one hundred. They shall set out third.
The formation of the camp of Dan, with their army, shall be toward the north. The ruler of the sons of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His army, those registered, numbered sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Asher; the ruler of the sons of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-one thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Naphtali; the ruler of the sons of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
And those camping first toward the east shall be the formation of Judah’s camp, with their army. The ruler of the sons of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-three thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Dan numbered one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last, by their formation.
This is the enrolment of the sons of Israel by their ancestral houses. The whole enrolment of the camps, with their armies, was six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites were not registered together with them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the sons of Israel did everything that the Lord instructed Moses. So they camped by their formations, and so they set out, each beside his neighbour, by their divisions and ancestral houses.
His army, those registered, numbered seventy-four thousand six hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Issachar; the ruler of the sons of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-four thousand four hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Zebulun; the ruler of the sons of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Judah, with their army, numbered one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred. They shall set out first.
And Moses and Aaron assembled the congregation before the rock. He said to them: Listen to me, you disobedient people! Surely we are not to bring water out of this rock for you?
And Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with the staff. Abundant water came out, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
And the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron: Because you did not believe so as to show Me holy before the sons of Israel, you shall not bring this congregation into the land that I have given them.
This is the Water of Dispute, because the sons of Israel reviled before the Lord, and He was shown holy among them.
And the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom:
Let Aaron be gathered to his people, for you shall certainly not enter the land that I have given to the sons of Israel, because you provoked Me at the Water of Reviling.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor before the whole congregation.
And strip Aaron of his robe and clothe his son Eleazar. Let Aaron be gathered and die there.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded, and he brought him up Mount Hor before the whole congregation.
And he stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died on the summit of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
And the whole congregation saw that Aaron had been released, and all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Take the staff, and gather the congregation, you and Aaron your brother; and speak unto the rock before them, and it shall give its waters; and you shall bring water out of the rock for them, and shall give the congregation and their livestock to drink.
And Moses took the staff that was before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded.
And from there they went to the well. This is the well of which the Lord said unto Moses: Gather the people, and I will give them water to drink.
Then Israel sang this song over the well: Lead the singing for it!
A well: rulers dug it; kings of nations hewed it out in their kingdom, when they exercised dominion. From the well they went to Manthanain.
Therefore those who speak in riddles will say: Come to Heshbon, so that Sihon's city may be built and prepared.
And they turned and went up by the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet them with all his people, for battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto Moses: Do not fear him, for I have handed him, all his people, and all his land into your hands. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.
And he struck him, and his sons, and all his people, until he left none of his alive; and they inherited their land.

And the people came unto Moses and said: We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Therefore pray unto the Lord, and let Him remove the serpents from us. Moses prayed unto the Lord for the people.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Make a serpent for yourself, and set it upon a standard; and it shall be, if a serpent bites a man, that everyone bitten, when he looks upon it, shall live.
And Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on a standard. Whenever a serpent bit a person, that person looked at the bronze serpent and lived.
And Balaam said to God: Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent them to me, saying:
Behold, a people has come out of Egypt and covers the face of the land; they are encamped next to me. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I can strike them and drive them from the land.
And God said to Balaam: You shall not go with them or curse the people, for they are blessed.
I will honour you richly, and I will do for you whatever you say. Come and curse this people for me.
And God came to Balaam at night and said to him: If these men are here to summon you, rise and follow them. But you shall do what I tell you.
And Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
And God grew angry because he went. God's angel rose to obstruct him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants beside him.
And the donkey saw God's angel opposing them in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. She turned off the road into the plain, and he struck her with the staff to direct her onto the road.
And God's angel stood in the furrows of the vineyards, with a fence on either side.
And the donkey saw God's angel and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot. He whipped her again.
And God's angel went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn right or left.
And the donkey saw God's angel and crouched beneath Balaam. Balaam became angry and beat the donkey with his staff.
And God opened the donkey's mouth, and she says to Balaam: What have I done unto you that you have struck me this third time?
And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you have mocked me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have stabbed you already.
And the donkey says to Balaam: Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this day? Have I acted like this toward you out of deliberate disregard? He said: No.
God uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he sees the Lord's angel opposing him in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bent down and prostrated himself on his face.
And God's angel said to him: Why have you struck your donkey this third time? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is not fitting before me.
And the donkey saw me and turned away from me this third time. If she had not turned away, I would now have killed you and preserved her.
And Balaam said unto the Lord's angel: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were opposing me in the road. Now, if this does not please you, I will turn back.
And God's angel said to Balaam: Go with the men, but take care to speak the word that I tell you. Balaam went with Balak's officials.

And now come and curse this people for me, for they are stronger than we are. If we can strike some of them, I will drive them from the land. I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.
And God came to Balaam and said to him: Who are these men with you?
And Balaam said to Balak: Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven calves and seven rams for me here.
Who has measured Jacob’s seed exactly, and who will count Israel's clans? May my soul die among righteous souls, and may my seed be like their seed!
And Balak said to Balaam: What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies, and look, you have pronounced a blessing!
And Balaam said to Balak: Must I not take care to speak what God puts in my mouth?
And Balak said to him: Come with me to another place, from which you shall not see them except for a part; you shall in no wise see them all. Curse them for me from there.
And Balaam said to Balak: Stand beside your sacrifice, while I go to inquire of God.
And God met Balaam, put a word in his mouth, and said: Return to Balak and speak these words.
And he returned to him, and there he stood beside his whole burning, with all the officials of Moab. Balak said to him: What did the Lord say?
And he took up his parable and said: Rise, Balak, and hear! Listen as a witness, son of Zippor!
God is not as a man, to be led astray, nor as a son of man, to be threatened; having spoken, shall He not act? Shall He speak, and not abide by it?
Behold, I have been taken up to bless. I will bless and certainly will not reverse it.
There shall be no toil in Jacob, neither shall distress be seen in Israel; the Lord his God is with him; the glories of rulers are in him.
God brought them out of Egypt; his glory is as that of a one-horned beast.
There is no omen-taking in Jacob and no divination in Israel. At the appointed time it shall be said to Jacob and Israel what God will accomplish.
Behold, a people will rise like a lion cub and exult like a lion. It will not sleep until it eats prey and drinks the blood of the slain.
And Balak said to Balaam: Neither curse them for me nor bless them at all!
And Balaam answered Balak: Did I not tell you that I must do the word that God speaks?
And Balak said to Balaam: Come; I will take you to another place. If it pleases God, curse them for me from there.
And Balaam said to Balak: Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven calves and seven rams for me here.

And Balaam said to Balak: Stand beside your sacrifice, while I go to see whether God will appear to meet me. Whatever He shows me, I will tell you. Balak stood beside his sacrifice, and Balaam went to inquire of God; he went straight on.
And God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to Him: I have prepared the seven altars and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
And God put a word in Balaam's mouth and said: Return to Balak and thus you shall speak.
And he returned to him, and there he stood beside his whole burnt offerings, with all the officials of Moab.

And God's Spirit came upon him, and he took up his parable and said: Balak summoned me from Mesopotamia, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: Come, curse Jacob for me; come, call down a curse on Israel for me.
Why should I curse whom the Lord does not curse? Why should I call down a curse on whom God does not curse?
From the tops of mountains I shall see them, and from the hills I shall observe them. Behold, a people who will dwell alone, not counted among the nations.
And Balak became angry with Balaam and clapped his hands. He said to Balaam: I summoned you to curse my enemy, and look, you have thoroughly blessed them this third time!
Now flee to your own place! I said I would honour you, but now the Lord has deprived you of glory.
And Balaam said to Balak: Did I not tell the messengers whom you sent to me:
Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the Lord's word to do evil or good on my own. Whatever God says, I must say.
And now look, I am returning to my place. Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people at the end of the days.
And Israel lodged at Shittim, and the people profaned themselves by engaging in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has stopped My wrath against the sons of Israel by being zealous with My zeal among them, and I did not consume the sons of Israel in My zeal.
Therefore say: Behold, I give him a covenant of peace.
And it shall be for him and his seed after him an everlasting covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.
The name of the Israelite man struck down with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, a ruler of an ancestral house of Simeon.
And the name of the Midianite woman who was struck down was Cozbi daughter of Zur, a ruler of the nation of Ommoth, an ancestral house of Midian.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, saying:
Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them,

for they are hostile to you through the deceit by which they deceive you because of Peor and because of Cozbi, daughter of a Midianite ruler, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague because of Peor.
And they invited them to the sacrifices of their idols. The people ate from their sacrifices and bowed down to their idols.
And Israel was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor, and the Lord became angry with Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Take all the leaders of the people and make a public example of them before the Lord in the sunlight, and the Lord's fierce anger will turn away from Israel.
And Moses said to Israel's tribes: Each of you shall kill his own kinsman who was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor.

And an Israelite man came and brought his brother to the Midianite woman before Moses and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, rose from among the congregation, and took a lance in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the chamber and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her womb. The plague against the sons of Israel stopped.
And those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
And after the plague, the Lord spoke unto Moses and Eleazar the priest:
Take the sum of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral houses, everyone who goes out to line up for battle in Israel.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke in Araboth of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
From twenty years old and upward, as the Lord commanded Moses. These are the sons of Israel who came out of Egypt:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
The land shall be divided among these for inheritance according to the number of names.
To the more numerous you shall increase the inheritance, and to the fewer you shall reduce their inheritance. Each shall receive its inheritance according to their registration.
The land shall be divided by lots. They shall inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
You shall divide their inheritance by the lot between the more numerous and the fewer.
And the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, of the clan of Manasseh among the sons of Joseph, came forward. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brother.

But if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative from his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a rule of judgment for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Go up the mountain on the farther side—this is Mount Nebo—and see the land of Canaan that I am giving to the sons of Israel as a possession.
And you shall see it, and you also shall be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was gathered at Mount Hor,

because you transgressed My word in the wilderness of Zin during the congregation’s resistance, when you were to sanctify Me; you did not sanctify Me at the water before them. This is the Water of Dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
And Moses said unto the Lord:
Let the Lord, the God of spirits and of all flesh, appoint a man over this congregation,
who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord's congregation will not be like sheep without a shepherd.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: Take unto yourself Joshua son of Nun, a man who has spirit within him, and you shall lay your hands upon him,
and shall set him before Eleazar the priest, and shall instruct him before all the congregation, and shall give instructions concerning him before them,
And they stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the rulers, and the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, saying:
and shall put of your glory upon him, that the sons of Israel may obey him.

And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and they shall ask him for the judgment of the manifestations before the Lord. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in: he, the sons of Israel together, and the whole congregation.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
And he laid his hands on him and presented him, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the congregation that rose against the Lord in Korah's congregation; he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Let our father's name not be erased from his clan because he has no son. Give us a possession among our father's brothers.
And Moses brought their case before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brethren, and shall assign their father’s allotment unto them.
And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man dies, and has no son, you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter.
But if he has no daughter, you shall give the inheritance to his brother.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
a Sabbath whole burnt offering on each Sabbath, besides the continual whole burning and its drink offering.
And at the new moons you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, and one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs;
For each calf, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil; for each ram, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil;
For each lamb, a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil: a sacrifice, a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
Their drink offering shall be wine: half a hin for each calf, a third of a hin for each ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the whole burnt offering month by month throughout the year.
And one male goat from the goats for sin unto the Lord; besides the continual whole burning shall it be offered, and its drink offering.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord's Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is a festival. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
And the first day shall be a holy appointed assembly for you. You shall do no laborious work.
And you shall bring whole burnt offerings, offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, one ram, seven year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished for you.
Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them, saying: You shall take care to present My gifts, My donations, My offerings of sweet savour unto Me at My feasts.
And their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf and two tenths for each ram.
You shall prepare a tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs;
And offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,
besides the continual morning whole burning, which is a continual whole burnt offering.
These you shall prepare in this manner each day for seven days, a gift, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord; besides the continual whole burnt offering you shall prepare its drink offering.
And the seventh day shall be a holy summoned assembly for you. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And on the day of new produce, when you present a new sacrifice unto the Lord at the festival of weeks, you shall have a holy appointed assembly. You shall do no laborious work.
And you shall bring whole burnt offerings for a sweet savour unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf and two tenths for each ram;
a tenth for each of the seven lambs;
And you shall say unto them: These are the offerings which you shall bring unto the Lord: two unblemished year-old lambs each day for a continual whole burning;
and one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you.
These are apart from the continual whole burnt offering. You shall prepare their sacrifice for Me—they shall be unblemished—and their drink offerings.
you shall offer the one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the second lamb toward evening.
And you shall prepare a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour for a sacrifice, mixed with oil, a fourth of a hin.
It is a continual whole burnt offering, instituted at Mount Sinai as a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And its drink offering shall be a fourth of a hin for each lamb; in the holy place you shall pour out a drink offering of strong drink unto the Lord.
And you shall offer the second lamb toward evening; you shall prepare it according to its sacrifice and according to its drink offering for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And on the Sabbath day you shall bring two unblemished year-old lambs, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and a drink offering,
And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall hold a holy appointed assembly. You shall do no laborious work. It shall be a day of signalling for you.
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.

And also offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you, besides the sin offering of atonement, the continual whole burning, its sacrifice and its drink offering, according to the prescription, as a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall hold a holy appointed assembly. You shall do no laborious work and shall keep a festival unto the Lord for seven days.

And on the first day you shall present whole burnt offerings, offerings, as a sweet savour unto the Lord: thirteen calves from the cattle, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished.
Their sacrifices shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each of the thirteen calves and two tenths for each of the two rams,
and one tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
And on the second day offer twelve calves from the cattle, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice and their drink offering for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour unto the Lord: one calf from the cattle, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
On the third day offer eleven calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice and their drink offering for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the fourth day offer ten calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the fifth day offer nine calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the sixth day offer eight calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the calf and two tenths for the ram,
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
On the seventh day offer seven calves, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calves, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, according to their prescription.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.
And on the eighth day you shall hold a closing festival. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour, offerings unto the Lord: one calf, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifices and their drink offerings for the calf, the ram, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
And also offer one male goat for sin, besides the continual whole burning, their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.

You shall offer these unto the Lord at your festivals, apart from your vows, your freewill offerings, your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your drink offerings, and your sacrifices of deliverance.
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
And also offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,

besides the whole burnt offerings of the new moon, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, and the continual whole burnt offerings, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, according to their prescription, as a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And on the tenth day of this month you shall have a holy appointed assembly; and you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no work.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour unto the Lord, offerings: one calf from the cattle, one ram, and seven year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished for you.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the calf and two tenths for the one ram,
And these are the generations of Aaron and Moses on the day when the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the Tent of Testimony, and they shall keep their priesthood, and all that concerns the altar and is within the veil. And the outsider who touches shall die.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the sons of Israel. They shall be their ransom, and the Levites shall be Mine.

For every firstborn is Mine. On the day when I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated unto Myself every firstborn in Israel, from man unto livestock. They shall be Mine; I am the Lord.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
Register the sons of Levi by their ancestral houses, by their divisions, by their families. You shall register every male from one month old and upward.
And Moses and Aaron registered them by the voice of the Lord, as the Lord instructed them.
And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And these are the names of Gershon’s sons by their divisions: Libni and Shimei.
And the sons of Kohath by their divisions: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
And these are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
And the sons of Merari by their divisions: Mahli and Mushi. These are the divisions of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
To Gershon belonged the division of Libni and the division of Shimei. These are the divisions of Gershon.
Those registered, counting every male from one month old and upward, numbered seven thousand five hundred.
And the sons of Gershon shall camp behind the Tent, toward the sea.
And the ruler of the ancestral house of the division of Gershon is Eliasaph son of Lael.
And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Testimony is the Tent, the covering, and the covering at the door of the Tent of Testimony,
and the hangings of the court, the curtain at the gate of the court by the Tent, and the remaining things for all its work.
To Kohath belonged the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite, and Uzzielite divisions. These are the divisions of Kohath.
Counting every male from one month old and upward, there were eight thousand six hundred, keeping charge of the holy things.
The divisions of the sons of Kohath shall camp beside the Tent toward the southwest.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests whose hands were consecrated for priestly service.
And the ruler of the ancestral house of the divisions of Kohath is Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
And their charge is the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the holy utensils with which they minister, the covering, and all their work.
And the ruler over the rulers of the Levites is Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, appointed to keep charge of the holy things.
To Merari belonged the division of Mahli and the division of Mushi. These are the divisions of Merari.
Those registered, counting every male from one month old and upward, numbered six thousand fifty.
And the ruler of the ancestral house of the division of Merari is Zuriel son of Abihail. They shall camp beside the Tent toward the north.
The appointed charge of the sons of Merari is the capitals of the Tent, its bars, pillars, and bases, all their furnishings, and their work,
and the pillars around the court, their bases, pegs, and cords.

And those camping before the Tent of Testimony on the east are Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary for the charges of the sons of Israel. And the outsider who touches shall die.
All those registered among the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron registered by the voice of the Lord by their divisions, every male from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.

And Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord when they offered strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. And Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with Aaron their father.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying: Register every firstborn male among the sons of Israel from one month old and upward, and take their number by name.

And you shall take the Levites for Me, I am the Lord, in place of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the sons of Israel.
And Moses registered every firstborn among the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded.
And all the firstborn males, counted by name from one month old and upward, numbered twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the Levites’ livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be Mine. I am the Lord.
And for the ransom of the two hundred seventy-three firstborn sons of Israel who exceed the number of Levites,
you shall take five shekels head by head; you shall take them according to the sacred didrachma, twenty obols to the shekel.
And you shall give the silver unto Aaron and unto his sons, as the ransom of those who exceed their number.
And Moses took the silver, the ransom of those in excess, for the redemption of the Levites.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
From the firstborn of the sons of Israel he took the silver: one thousand three hundred sixty-five sanctuary shekels.
And Moses gave the ransom of those in excess unto Aaron and his sons by the voice of the Lord, as the Lord instructed Moses.
Take the tribe of Levi, and you shall set them before Aaron the priest, and they shall minister unto him;
And they shall keep his charges and the charges of the sons of Israel before the Tent of Testimony, performing the work of the Tent.
And they shall keep all the furnishings of the Tent of Testimony and the charges of the sons of Israel, according to all the work of the Tent.
And you shall give the Levites unto Aaron and unto his sons, the priests. These are given unto Me as a gift from the sons of Israel.
And Moses told the sons of Israel everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.

But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.

But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.
These are the ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.
And Moses spoke to the rulers of the tribes of Israel, saying: This is the word that the Lord has commanded:
Any person who vows a vow unto the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction upon himself, shall not profane his word. He shall do everything that comes from his mouth.
If a woman vows a vow unto the Lord or imposes a restriction while in her father’s house in her youth,

and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.
If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And they burned all their towns in their settlements and their farmsteads with fire.
And they took all the plunder and all their spoils, from people to livestock,
and brought the captives, the spoils, and the plunder unto Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the sons of Israel, at the camp at Araboth Moab, which is on the Jordan opposite Jericho.
And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the rulers of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
And Moses was angry with the overseers of the force, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds who were returning from the battle formation,
and Moses said to them: Why have you taken every female alive?
For these women, according to Balaam’s word, caused the sons of Israel to turn away and disregard the Lord’s word because of Peor, and the plague came upon the Lord’s congregation.
And now kill every male among all the dependents, and kill every woman who has known a male’s bed.
Take alive all the female dependents who have not known a male’s bed.
And you shall camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who killed someone or touches someone slain shall be purified on the third day and the seventh day, both you and your captives.
Exact vengeance for the sons of Israel from the Midianites. Finally you shall be gathered to your people.
And you shall thoroughly purify every covering, every leather article, every object made from goats’ hair, and every wooden article.
And Eleazar the priest said to the men of the force who were returning from the battle formation, This is the ordinance of the law that the Lord prescribed unto Moses:
Only the gold, and the silver, and the bronze, and the iron, and the lead, and the tin,
everything that passes through fire shall also be cleansed, but it shall be purified with the water of purification. Everything that does not pass through fire shall pass through water.
And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day and be cleansed; afterward you shall enter the camp.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take a total of the spoils of captivity, from people to livestock, you, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the congregation’s ancestral houses.
And you shall divide the spoils between the warriors who go forth into battle and the whole congregation.

And you shall set apart a levy unto the Lord from the warriors who went forth into battle: one living being out of five hundred, from the men, and from the livestock, and from the cattle, and from the sheep, and from the goats.
And you shall take it from their half; and you shall give unto Eleazar the priest the firstfruits of the Lord.
And Moses spoke to the people, saying: Equip men from among you to draw up for battle before the Lord against Midian, to repay Midian with vengeance from the Lord.

And from the half belonging to the sons of Israel you shall take one out of fifty, from the men, and from the cattle, and from the sheep, and from the donkeys, and from all the livestock; and you shall give them unto the Levites who keep the charges in the Tent of the Lord.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
And the surplus of the plunder that the warriors had taken was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,
And seventy-two thousand cattle,
And sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand human beings in all, from the women who had not known a man’s bed.
And the half-share belonging to those who went out to war numbered three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
and the levy for the Lord from the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
And the cattle numbered thirty-six thousand, and the levy for the Lord was seventy-two.
And the donkeys numbered thirty thousand five hundred, and the levy for the Lord was sixty-one.
Send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to draw up for battle.
And the human beings numbered sixteen thousand, and their levy for the Lord was thirty-two persons.
And Moses gave the levy for the Lord, the portion set apart unto God, to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
From the half belonging to the sons of Israel, which Moses had separated from the warriors—
And the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
And thirty-six thousand cattle,
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand human beings—

and Moses took from the half belonging to the sons of Israel one out of fifty, from the men and from the livestock, and gave them unto the Levites who kept the charges of the Tent of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And all those appointed over the army’s units of a thousand, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, approached Moses.
And they said unto Moses: Your servants have counted the warriors in our company, and not even one of them is missing.
And they counted out a thousand from each tribe from the thousands of Israel: twelve thousand equipped for battle.
And we have brought the gift unto the Lord, each man whatever gold article he found—armlets, bracelets, rings, wrist ornaments, and hair ornaments—to make atonement for us before the Lord.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, every article worked by hand.
And all the gold, the portion set apart that they set aside for the Lord from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
And the warriors had taken plunder, each for himself.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the Tent of Testimony as a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord.
And Moses sent them, a thousand from each tribe, with their force and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, with the sacred vessels and the signalling trumpets in their hands.
And they drew up for battle against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
And they killed the kings of Midian together with their slain: Evi, Zur, Rekem, Hur, and Robok, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword together with their slain.
And they took the women of Midian and their dependents as spoil, and plundered their livestock, all their possessions, and their resources.
And they approached him and said: Let us build sheepfolds here for our livestock and towns for our dependents.
And Moses said to them: If you act according to this word, if you equip yourselves before the Lord for war,
and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the Lord until His enemy is wiped out from before Him,

and the land is brought under dominion before the Lord, then afterward you shall return. You shall be guiltless before the Lord and toward Israel, and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.
But if you do not do so, you shall sin before the Lord, and you shall recognize your sin when evils overtake you.
And you shall build for yourselves towns for your dependents and folds for your livestock; and you shall do that which comes out of your mouth.
And the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad said unto Moses: Your servants will do as our lord commands.
Our dependents, our wives, and all our livestock will remain in the towns of Gilead.
But your servants will cross over, all armed and drawn up in formation before the Lord for war, as the lord says.
And Moses appointed over them Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel.

And Moses said to them: If the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad cross the Jordan with you, everyone equipped for war before the Lord, and you gain dominion over the land before you, you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.

But if they do not cross over equipped with you for war before the Lord, you shall bring their dependents, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and they shall receive an inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad answered: Everything our lord says unto his servants, we will do.
We will cross over equipped before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and you shall give us our possession on this side of the Jordan.

And Moses gave to the sons of Gad, the sons of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of the sons of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land and its towns with its boundaries, the towns of the surrounding land.
And they said: If we have found favour before you, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.
And these are the stations of the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt with their force under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
And Moses recorded their departures and their stations through the Lord’s word. These are the stations of their journey.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
and you shall destroy all who inhabit the land before you, remove their lookout places, destroy all their cast idols, and remove all their pillars.
And you shall destroy all who inhabit the land and settle in it, for I have given you their land as an allotment.

And you shall inherit their land by lot according to your tribes. Increase the possession of the larger groups and decrease that of the smaller groups. Wherever his name comes out shall be his. You shall inherit according to the tribes of your ancestral houses.

But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of the land from before you, those whom you leave will become splinters in your eyes and missiles in your sides, and they will act as enemies in the land where you shall settle.
And then I will do to you what I had determined to do to them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And you shall measure out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan unto Shepham.
And the boundary shall descend from Shepham to Arbela, from the east toward the springs. The boundary shall descend to Bela, along the eastern ridge of the Sea of Chennara.
And the boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its surrounding boundaries.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, as the Lord prescribed unto Moses to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
For the tribe of the sons of Reuben and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, have received their allotments.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their allotments across the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the south toward the east.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
These are the names of the men who shall obtain the land as an inheritance for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
And you shall take one ruler from each tribe to allot the land unto you.
And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are entering the land of Canaan; this shall be your inheritance, the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
from the tribe of Simeon, Salamiel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of Dan, the ruler Bakchir son of Egli;
from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the ruler Hanniel son of Ouphi;
from the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, the ruler Kemuel son of Sabatha;
from the tribe of Zebulun, the ruler Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the ruler Paltiel son of Oza;
from the tribe of the sons of Asher, the ruler Achior son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of Naphtali, the ruler Pedahel son of Benammihud.
These are the men whom the Lord commanded to distribute portions to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.
And your southwestern side shall run from the wilderness of Sin to the territory adjoining Edom. Your southwestern boundary shall begin from the part of the Salt Sea toward the east.

And the boundary shall turn around you from the southwest toward the Ascent of Akrabin and pass through Senna. Its endpoint shall be southwest of Kadesh-barnea; it shall extend to the settlement of Arad and pass through Azmon.
And the boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be the sea.
And for your sea boundary, the Great Sea shall mark the limit. This shall be your sea boundary.
And this shall be your boundary toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves beside the mountain, the mountain;
and from the mountain, the mountain, you shall measure out for them toward the entrance into Hamath; and its endpoint shall be the boundaries of Sarada.
And the boundary shall extend to Dephrona, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
and you shall set apart towns for yourselves. They shall be refuges for the killer to flee there, anyone who has struck a person unintentionally.
And the towns shall be refuges for you from the kinsman who avenges blood, so that the killer shall in no wise die before standing before the congregation for judgment.
And the towns you shall provide, the six towns, shall be refuges for you.
You shall provide three towns across the Jordan, and you shall provide three towns in the land of Canaan.

There shall be a refuge for the sons of Israel; for the sojourner and the resident stranger among you, these towns shall also be refuges, so that anyone who strikes a person unintentionally may flee there.
But if he strikes someone with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.

35:16 But if he strikes someone with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.

35:17 If he strikes someone with a stone from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.

35:18 If he strikes someone with a wooden object from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.

35:19 The kinsman who avenges blood shall himself kill the murderer. When he encounters him, he shall kill him.

35:20 If he pushes someone out of enmity and throws an object at him from ambush and that person dies,

35:21 or strikes him with his hand out of wrath and he dies, let the one who struck him surely be put to death; he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death. The kinsman who avenges blood shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
If he strikes someone with a stone from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a wooden object from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
The kinsman who avenges blood shall himself kill the murderer. When he encounters him, he shall kill him.
Instruct the sons of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from their allotted possessions. They shall also give the Levites the outlying lands around the towns.
If he pushes someone out of enmity and throws an object at him from ambush and that person dies,

or strikes him with his hand out of wrath and he dies, let the one who struck him surely be put to death; he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death. The kinsman who avenges blood shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
But if he suddenly pushes someone without enmity, or throws any object at him without ambush,
or, without his knowing, a stone capable of causing death falls upon him and he dies, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him,
And then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the kinsman who avenges blood according to these judgments.

And the congregation shall rescue the killer from the kinsman who avenges blood and restore him to the city of refuge to which he fled. He shall live there until the high priest dies, whom they anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer goes outside the boundaries of the city to which he fled,
and the kinsman who avenges blood finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge and kills the killer, the avenger is not liable.
For he must live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his possession.
And these shall be an ordinance of judgment for you throughout your generations in all your settlements.
And the towns shall be theirs to live in, and their designated lands shall be for their livestock and all their four-footed animals.
In every case of a person being struck down, you shall put the killer to death through witnesses. A single witness shall not testify against a person so as to cause his death.
And you shall not accept a ransom for a life from the killer who is guilty and liable to be killed; he shall surely be put to death.
You shall not accept a ransom concerning flight to a city of refuge, allowing him to live in the land again before the high priest dies.

And you shall in no wise stain with murder the land wherein you dwell; for this blood stains the land with murder, and atonement shall not be made for the land for the blood shed upon it, except by the blood of him who shed it.
And you shall not defile the land in which you dwell, in which I will dwell among you, for I am the Lord, dwelling among the sons of Israel.
And the lands adjoining the towns that you shall give the Levites shall extend two thousand cubits outward from the town wall all around.

And you shall measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the eastern side, and two thousand cubits on the southwestern side, and two thousand cubits on the seaward side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side; and the town shall be in the midst thereof for you, together with the adjoining lands of the towns.
And you shall give the Levites the six cities of refuge that you shall provide for the person who has killed someone to flee to, and in addition to these, forty-two towns.
All the towns you shall give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their outlying lands.

And for the towns that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, take many from those with much and fewer from those with less. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the inheritance he receives.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And the rulers of the tribe of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of Joseph’s descendants, approached and spoke before Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel.
Zelophehad’s daughters did as the Lord had prescribed unto Moses.
And Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins.
They married within the clan of Manasseh, of Joseph’s descendants, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commandments, ordinances, and judgments that the Lord commanded through Moses on the western side of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.

And they said: The Lord commanded our lord to distribute the inherited land by lot to the sons of Israel, and the Lord instructed the lord to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

And if they become wives in one of the Israelite tribes, their allotment will be taken from our fathers’ possession and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. It will be taken from our inherited allotment.

If the release comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.
And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the Lord’s instruction, saying: Thus speaks the tribe of Joseph’s descendants.
This is the word that the Lord prescribed concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: Let them marry whom they please, but they shall marry from their father’s clan.
And no inheritance among the sons of Israel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each Israelite shall hold fast to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe.

And every daughter who succeeds as next of kin to an inheritance among the Israelite tribes shall marry someone from her father’s clan, so that each Israelite may succeed as next of kin to his paternal inheritance.
And no allotment shall pass from one tribe to another; rather, the sons of Israel shall each hold fast to their own inheritance.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
And they shall put it and all its furnishings into a covering of blue leather and place it on carrying poles.
And over the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of blue leather, and insert its carrying poles.
And they shall take all the ministering utensils used in the holy place, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of blue leather, and place them on carrying poles.
And he shall put the cover upon the altar, and they shall spread a cloth entirely of purple over it.

And they shall put on it all the utensils used in its ministry: the firepans, meat forks, bowls, the cover, and all the altar utensils. They shall spread a covering of blue leather over it and insert its carrying poles. They shall take a purple cloth, cover the basin and its stand together, put them into a covering of blue leather, and place them on carrying poles.

And when the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall finish covering the holy things and all the holy utensils. Afterward the sons of Kohath shall enter to carry them, and they shall not touch the holy things, so that they do not die. These are what the sons of Kohath shall carry in the Tent of Testimony.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is overseer of the oil for light, the compounded incense, the daily sacrifice, and the anointing oil: oversight of the whole Tent and everything in it, in the holy place, in all the work.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Do not destroy the division of Kohath’s tribe from among the Levites.
Do this for them, and they shall live and shall in no wise die when they approach the most holy things: let Aaron and his sons approach, and they shall appoint each man according to his burden.
Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their divisions, by their ancestral houses,
And they shall in no wise enter to behold the holy things suddenly, lest they die.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take the sum of the sons of Gershon also, by their ancestral houses, by their divisions.
Register them from twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone entering to minister and perform his work in the Tent of Testimony.
This is the ministry of the division of Gershon, in ministering and carrying:
And it shall carry the skin curtains of the Tent, the Tent of Testimony, its covering, the blue covering above it, and the covering at the door of the Tent of Testimony,
And the court hangings by the Tent of Testimony, the remaining things, and all the ministering utensils used with them. They shall do the work.
The ministry of the sons of Gershon shall be at the mouth of Aaron and his sons, in all their ministries and all that they carry. And you shall register them by name, with all that they carry.
This is the ministry of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Testimony. Their charge is under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
You shall register the sons of Merari by their divisions, by their ancestral houses.
from twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone entering to minister and do all the work in the Tent of Testimony.
You shall register them from twenty-five years old and upward unto fifty years old, every one who enters to minister in the work of the Tent of Testimony.

And these are the things entrusted to their carrying for all their work in the Tent of Testimony: the capitals of the Tent, its bars, pillars, and bases, the covering, their bases and pillars, and the covering at the door of the Tent,

And the pillars around the court and their bases, the pillars of the curtain at the court gate and their bases, their pegs and cords, all their utensils, and all their ministries. Register them by name, with all the utensils entrusted to their carrying.
This is the ministry of the division of the sons of Merari, all their work in the Tent of Testimony, under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
And Moses, Aaron, and the rulers of Israel registered the sons of Kohath by their divisions and ancestral houses,
From twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone entering to minister and work in the Tent of Testimony.
And their enrolment by their divisions was two thousand seven hundred fifty.
This is the enrolment of the division of Kohath, everyone ministering in the Tent of Testimony, whom Moses and Aaron registered by the voice of the Lord through Moses.
And the sons of Gershon were registered by their divisions and ancestral houses,
From twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone entering to minister and do the work in the Tent of Testimony.
And this is the work of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Testimony: the most holy things.
And their enrolment by their divisions and ancestral houses was two thousand six hundred thirty.
This is the enrolment of the division of the sons of Gershon, everyone ministering in the Tent of Testimony, whom Moses and Aaron registered by the voice of the Lord through Moses.
The division of the sons of Merari was also registered by their divisions and ancestral houses,
From twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone entering to minister in the work of the Tent of Testimony.
And their enrolment by their divisions and ancestral houses was three thousand two hundred.
This is the enrolment of the division of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron registered by the voice of the Lord through Moses.
All those registered among the Levites by Moses, Aaron, and the rulers of Israel, by their divisions and ancestral houses,
From twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone entering for the work of service and the work of carrying in the Tent of Testimony,
And those registered numbered eight thousand five hundred eighty.
By the voice of the Lord, through Moses, each man was appointed to his work and what he carried. They were registered as the Lord instructed Moses.
And when the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall enter, and take down the overshadowing veil, and cover the ark of testimony with it.
And they shall put over it a covering of blue skin, lay a cloth entirely of blue above it, and insert the carrying poles.

And over the table set forth they shall spread a cloth entirely of purple, and the dishes, and the incense vessels, and the cups, and the vessels wherein he pours the drink offerings; and the continual loaves shall be upon it.
And they shall spread a scarlet cloth over it, cover it with a covering of blue leather, and insert its carrying poles through it.
And they shall take a blue cloth and cover the illuminating lampstand, its lamps, tongs, snuffers, and all the oil vessels used in ministering with them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And each man’s consecrated things shall be his; whatsoever a man gives unto the priest shall be his.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man’s wife transgresses and utterly disregards him,
and anyone lies with her with an emission of semen, and it escapes the eyes of her husband, and she conceals it, though she is defiled, and there is no witness concerning her, and she is not caught,
and a spirit of jealousy comes upon him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she is defiled; or a spirit of jealousy comes upon him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she is not defiled:

then the man shall bring his wife unto the priest, and shall present the gift on her behalf, a tenth of an oiphi of barley flour. He shall pour no oil upon it, neither shall he put frankincense upon it; for it is a sacrifice of jealousy, a memorial sacrifice bringing sin to remembrance.
And the priest shall bring her near and stand her before the Lord.
And the priest shall take clean, living water in an earthenware vessel. He shall take some earth from the floor of the Tent of Testimony and put it into the water.

And the priest shall stand the woman before the Lord, uncover her head, and put the memorial sacrifice—the sacrifice of jealousy—on her hands. In the priest’s hand shall be this curse-bringing water of testing.

And the priest shall put her under oath, and say unto the woman: If no one has lain with you, and you have not transgressed into defilement while under your own husband, be unharmed by this curse-bringing water of testing.
Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone with a seminal discharge, and everyone unclean through a dead person.
But if you have transgressed while under a husband, or have become defiled, and someone other than your husband has lain with you:

then the priest shall put the woman under the oaths of this curse, and the priest shall say unto the woman: The Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the Lord makes your thigh collapse and your belly swell;
and this curse-bringing water shall enter your belly, to make your belly swell and your thigh collapse. And the woman shall say: So be it, so be it.
And the priest shall write these curses in a scroll and wipe them off into the curse-bringing water of testing.
And he shall make the woman drink the curse-bringing water of testing, and the curse-bringing water of testing shall enter her.
And the priest shall take the sacrifice of jealousy from the woman’s hand, place the sacrifice before the Lord, and bring it near the altar.
And the priest shall take a handful from the sacrifice as its memorial portion and offer it up on the altar. Afterward he shall make the woman drink the water.

And it shall be, if she is defiled and has concealed it from her husband, that the curse-bringing water of testing shall enter her, and her belly shall swell, and her thigh shall collapse, and the woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman is not defiled, and is clean, she shall be unharmed, and shall bring forth seed.
This is the law of jealousy, when a wife transgresses while under a husband and becomes defiled,
From male unto female, send them outside the camp, and they shall in no wise defile their camps, wherein I dwell among them.
or when a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man and he is jealous of his wife. He shall set his wife before the Lord, and the priest shall perform all this law for her.
And the man shall be free from sin, and that woman shall bear her sin.
And the sons of Israel did so and sent them outside the camp. As the Lord spoke unto Moses, so the sons of Israel did.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man or woman commits any of the sins of men, and acts with utter disregard, and that soul incurs guilt,
that person shall confess the sin committed, and repay the principal of the offence, and add a fifth part thereto, and give it unto the one who was wronged.

But if the man has no next of kin to receive repayment for the offence, the repayment made unto the Lord shall be the priest’s, besides the ram of atonement, wherewith he shall make atonement for him.
And every first portion from all the things consecrated among the sons of Israel that they bring unto the Lord, unto the priest, shall belong to him.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons unto the priest, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin in connection with the dead person, and shall consecrate his head on that day,

whereon he was consecrated unto the Lord for the days of the vow. And he shall bring a year-old lamb for a guilt offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, for the head of his vow was defiled.
And this is the law of him who has vowed: on the day when he fulfils the days of his vow, he shall present his offering at the doors of the Tent of Testimony,
and he shall bring his gift unto the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for whole burning, and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for deliverance,
and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, loaves prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and their sacrifice and their drink offering.
And the priest shall present them before the Lord, and prepare his offering for sin and his whole burnt offering.
And he shall prepare the ram as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its sacrifice and its drink offering.
And he who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and put the hair upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of deliverance.

And the priest shall take the boiled foreleg from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of him who has vowed, after he has shaved the hair of his vow.
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart

And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.

This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying unto them (and they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them):
The Lord bless you and keep you;
the Lord make His face shine upon you, and have mercy upon you;
the Lord lift up His face upon you, and give you peace.

from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
