All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
But if anyone dies suddenly beside him, the head of his vow shall be defiled forthwith. He shall shave his head on the day when he is cleansed; on the seventh day it shall be shaved.

And it came to pass, on the day when Moses finished setting up the Tent, that he anointed it and sanctified it and all its vessels, and the altar and all its vessels; and he anointed them and sanctified them,
And the rulers presented gifts for the dedication of the altar on the day he anointed it. The rulers presented their gifts before the altar.
And the Lord said unto Moses: One ruler each day, a ruler each day, shall present their gifts for the dedication of the altar.
and the rulers of Israel presented offerings, twelve rulers of their ancestral houses; these are the rulers of the tribes, these are they who stood over the enrolment.
And they brought their gifts before the Lord: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon from every two rulers and a calf from each. They presented them before the Tent.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:
Take them from them, and they shall be for the works of ministry of the Tent of Testimony; and you shall give them unto the Levites, unto each according to his ministry.
And Moses took the wagons and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to their ministries.
And he gave four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their ministries, through Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
And unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, for they have the ministries of the sanctuary; they shall bear them upon their shoulders.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And you shall bring the Levites before the Lord, and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands upon the Levites.

But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Let the one who hears hear, and let the one who disobeys disobey,’ for it is an embittering house.”
and it will always be stronger than rock. Do not fear them or be terrified before their faces, for it is an embittering house.”
and pour out My wrath upon Sais, Egypt’s strength, and destroy the multitude of Memphis.
The giants will say to you, ‘Be in the depth of a pit! Whom do you surpass? Descend and lie with the uncircumcised among those wounded by the sword.’
and stretch you out upon the earth; plains will be filled with you. I will seat all the sky’s birds upon you and fill all the beasts of the whole earth with you.

Say to them, ‘I live, thus says the Lord: I do not desire the impious man’s death, but rather that he turn from his way and live. Turn back completely from your way! Why are you dying, house of Israel?’

Say to your people’s sons, ‘A righteous man’s righteousness certainly will not rescue him on the day he wanders, and an impious man’s lawlessness certainly will not harm him on the day he turns from it. A righteous man certainly will not be able to be saved.
When I say to the impious man, “You will surely be put to death,” and he turns from his sin and practices judgment and righteousness,
and returns a pledge, repays what he seized and walks in the ordinances of life without doing wrong, he will surely live and certainly will not die.
None of the sins he committed will ever be remembered, because he practiced judgment and righteousness; in these he will live.
“Son of man, speak to your people’s sons and say to them, ‘If I bring a sword upon a land, and the land’s people take one man from among themselves and appoint him as their watchman,
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
and he sees the sword coming upon the land, sounds the trumpet and signals to the people,
And you, son of man, your people’s sons talk about you beside the walls and in the houses’ gateways. A man says to his brother, ‘Let us gather and hear what comes from the Lord!’
and a hearer hears the trumpet’s sound but does not take care, and the sword comes upon him and overtakes him, his blood will be upon his own head.
Because he heard the trumpet’s sound and did not take care, his blood will be upon himself. But this one, because he took care, rescued his life.

If the watchman sees the sword coming but does not signal with the trumpet, and the people do not take care, and the sword comes and takes a life from them, that life was taken because of its own lawlessness, but I will require the blood from the watchman’s hand.’
And you, son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for Israel’s house, and you will hear a word from My mouth.

When I say to the sinner, ‘You will surely be put to death,’ and you do not speak so that the impious man may guard himself from his way, that lawless man will die in his lawlessness, but I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you forewarn the impious man of his way so that he may turn from it and he does not turn from his way, this man will die in his impiety, and you have rescued your own life.

“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy and say to the shepherds, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O shepherds of Israel, surely shepherds do not feed themselves? Do shepherds not feed the sheep?
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will stretch My hand against you and make you a wilderness, and you will be laid waste.
and fill the hills and your ravines with your wounded. In all your plains, those wounded by the sword will fall within you.
Therefore say to Israel’s house, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am not acting for you, house of Israel, but because of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you entered.

therefore prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because you were dishonored and hated by those around you, so that you became a possession for the remaining nations, and you became a topic on people’s tongues and a reproach to nations,
I am not acting because of you, says the Lord, the Lord; this will be known to you. Be ashamed and abashed because of your ways, house of Israel.

Therefore prophesy over Israel’s land and say to the mountains, hills, ravines and valleys, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have spoken in My jealousy and My wrath because you bore the nations’ reproaches.
Therefore prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am opening your tombs and will bring you up from your tombs and into Israel’s land,

‘Son of man, take a staff for yourself and write upon it Judah and Israel’s sons attached to him. Take a second staff for yourself and write upon it, For Joseph—Ephraim’s staff—and all Israel’s sons joined to him.

say to them, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will take Joseph’s tribe through Ephraim’s hand, and Israel’s tribes attached to him, and place them upon Judah’s tribe. They will become one staff in Judah’s hand.

and say to them, Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am taking all Israel’s house from among the nations where they entered, gathering them from all those around them and bringing them into Israel’s land.
He said to me, ‘Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear the Lord’s word:
He said to me, ‘Prophesy, son of man! Prophesy to the breath and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead, and let them live!’
and say, “I will go up against an abandoned land; I will come upon those resting quietly and dwelling in peace, all living in a land with no wall or bars, and they have no doors,”
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord: On that day when My people Israel are settled in peace, will you not be roused?

and come up against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will be at the end of days; I will bring you against My land so that all the nations may know Me when I am sanctified in you before them.
and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,
Be made ready; prepare yourself, you and all your assembly gathered with you, and you will be a guard for Me.

And you, son of man, say, Thus says the Lord: Say to every flying bird and all the plain’s beasts, Gather and come! Gather from all those around to My sacrifice that I have sacrificed for you, a great sacrifice upon Israel’s mountains. You will eat flesh and drink blood.
The food you are to eat will be weighed out: twenty shekels a day; eat it from time to time.
Drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin; drink it from time to time.
Eat it as a barley cake baked in embers; bake it in pellets of human dung before their eyes,
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: So the sons of Israel will eat unclean things among the nations.’”
He said to me, “Behold, I have given you cattle dung instead of human dung; prepare your loaves over it.”
lay siege to it, build forward defenses against it, throw up a palisade against it, set camps against it, and arrange missile positions all around.
Take an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Prepare your face against it; it will be besieged, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the sons of Israel.
Lie on your left side and place the injustices of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of days—one hundred fifty—that you lie upon it; bear their injustices.
I have assigned you their two injustices as a number of days, one hundred ninety days; bear the injustices of the house of Israel
Prepare your face against Jerusalem’s siege, strengthen your arm, and prophesy against it.
Behold, I have placed bonds upon you; do not turn from side to side until the days of your confinement are completed.

Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt; put them in one earthen vessel and make loaves from them for yourself. According to the number of days you sleep on your side, you will eat them one hundred ninety days.
You, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel, and they will cease from their sins. Show its appearance and its arrangement—

—and they will receive their punishment for everything they have done. You will draw the house, its exits, and its structure; make known to them all its commands and all its ordinances, and draw them before them. They will keep all My judgments and all My commands and carry them out,
together with the drawing of the house on the mountain’s summit: all its boundaries all around are most holy.”

These are the altar’s measurements in a cubit consisting of a cubit and a handbreadth: a hollow one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a ledge along its edge all around of a span. This was the altar’s height:

from the depth at the beginning of its hollow to the large lower place of atonement, two cubits, with a breadth of a cubit; and from the small place of atonement to the large place of atonement, four cubits, with a breadth of a cubit.
The Ariel was four cubits, and from the Ariel upward above the horns was a cubit.
The Ariel was twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.

The place of atonement was fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides. Its surrounding ledge ran all around it at half a cubit, and its surrounding band was a cubit all around. Its steps faced east.
He said to me, “Son of man, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: These are the altar’s commands on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and pouring blood against it.
You will give the Levitical priests who are of Zadok’s offspring and draw near to Me to minister to Me, says the Lord God, a calf from the cattle as an offering for sin.
They will take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the place of atonement, and on the base all around. They will make atonement for it.
They will take the calf for the sin offering, and it will be burned in the separated area of the house, outside the holy places.
On the second day they will take two unblemished goat kids for sin, and they will make atonement for the altar as they made atonement with the calf.
After you have completed the atonement, they will bring an unblemished calf from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the sheep.
You all will bring them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt upon them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.
For seven days you will prepare a kid for sin each day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep. They will prepare unblemished animals—
—for seven days. They will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they will fill their hands.
From the eighth day onward, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. I will accept you, says the Lord.”
Now let them drive their prostitution and the murders of their rulers away from Me, and I will dwell among them for ever.
except the Levites, who sprang away from Me when Israel strayed from Me after their reflections; they will receive their injustice—

—and will serve in My holy places as gatekeepers at the house’s gates and as ministers to the house. They will slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people, and stand before the people to serve them.
Because they ministered to them before their idols, and it became a punishment of injustice for the house of Israel, I raised My hand against them, says the Lord God.

They will not draw near to Me to serve Me as priests, nor approach the holy things of the sons of Israel, nor My most holy things. They will receive their dishonor in the straying by which they strayed.
They will assign them to keep the duties of the house, for all its works and everything they may do.

The Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the duties of My holy places when the house of Israel strayed from Me, will approach Me to minister to Me. They will stand before Me to offer sacrifice, fat, and blood to Me, says the Lord God.
They will enter My holy places and approach My table to minister to Me, and they will keep My duties.
When they enter the gates of the inner court, they will put on linen robes. They will not wear woolen things when they minister from the gate of the inner court.
They will have linen turbans on their heads and linen trousers on their hips, and they will not bind their clothing tightly.

When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they will take off the robes in which they minister, place them in the recessed chambers of the holy places, and put on other robes. They will certainly not sanctify the people with their robes.
They will not shave their heads or strip away their hair; they will certainly cover their heads.
No priest will drink wine when they enter the inner court.
They will not take a widow or a woman who has been sent away as a wife, but a virgin of Israel’s offspring; if she is a priest’s widow, they may take her.
They will teach My people the difference between holy and profane, and make known to them the difference between unclean and clean.
In a case involving blood they will stand to decide. They will uphold My judgments and judge My decisions; they will keep My ordinances and My commands at all My festivals, and sanctify My Sabbaths.
They will not approach a human corpse so as to be defiled, except that a priest may be defiled for his father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or sister who has not belonged to a husband.
After he has been cleansed, one will count seven days for him.
On whatever day they enter the inner court to minister in the holy place, they will bring an atonement offering, says the Lord God.
This will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. No possession will be given them among the sons of Israel, because I am their possession.
They will eat the sacrifices, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance. Everything set apart in Israel will belong to them.

The firstfruits of everything, the firstborn of everything, and all the contributions from all your firstfruits will belong to the priests. You will give your first produce to the priest, to place your blessings upon your houses.
The priests will not eat anything that has died of itself or has been taken by a beast, whether from the birds or from the livestock.”

The Lord said to me, “Son of man, set in your heart, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything I speak with you concerning all the commands of the Lord’s house and all its ordinances. Set your heart on the house’s entrance, according to all its exits in all the holy places.
You will say to the provoking house, to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Let all your lawless deeds be enough for you, house of Israel—

—your bringing in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My holy places. They profaned them while you offered bread, fat, and blood, and you transgressed My covenant in all your lawless deeds.
You arranged for the keeping of duties in My holy places.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: No foreign son uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh will enter My holy places, among all the foreign sons who are in the midst of the house of Israel,

“When you measure out the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a first portion for the Lord, a holy part of the land, twenty-five thousand long and twenty thousand broad. It will be holy throughout all its boundaries all around.
You are to have an honest balance, an honest measure, and an honest choenix.
The measure and the choenix will likewise have one capacity: the choenix a tenth of the gomor, and the measure a tenth of the gomor. They will be equal in relation to the gomor.
The standard weight will be twenty obols. The five shekels will be five, the ten shekels ten, and fifty shekels will make your mina.
This is the first portion you will set apart: a sixth of the measure from the gomor of wheat, and a sixth of the oiphi from the kor of barley.
The command for oil is a cotyle of oil from ten cotyles, because ten cotyles are a gomor.
One sheep from every ten sheep will be a contribution from all Israel’s families, for sacrifices, burnt offerings, and offerings for well-being, to make atonement for you, says the Lord God.
All the people will give this first portion to Israel’s ruler.

Through the ruler will come the burnt offerings, sacrifices, and libations at the festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths, and at all the festivals of the house of Israel. He will provide the offerings for sin, the sacrifice, the burnt offerings, and the offerings for well-being to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month, you all will take an unblemished calf from the cattle to make atonement for the holy place.

The priest will take some of the blood of the atonement offering and put it on the house’s doorposts, on the four corners of the sacred precinct, on the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
From this, a square of five hundred by five hundred will be for a sanctuary, with an interval of fifty cubits all around it.
You will do likewise in the seventh month, on the first of the month: you will take a portion from each, and you all will make atonement for the house.
In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, you will have the Passover festival; for seven days you will eat unleavened bread.
On that day the ruler will provide a calf for sin on behalf of himself, the house, and all the people of the land.
For the seven days of the festival, he will provide burnt offerings to the Lord: seven calves and seven unblemished rams each day for the seven days, and a goat kid each day for sin.
You will provide an offering of a cake for each calf and a cake for each ram, with a hin of oil for each cake.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth of the month, at the festival you will provide the same for seven days: the offerings for sin, the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the oil.”
From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
It will be land for the priests who minister in the holy place, for those who draw near to minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, set apart for their sanctification.
An area twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad will belong to the Levites who minister to the house, as their possession, with cities in which to dwell.
You will give the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long; like the first portion of the holy areas, these will be for the whole house of Israel.

The ruler will have land on this side and that side of the first portions of the holy areas and the city’s possession, facing the first portions of the holy areas and facing the city’s possession: the parts toward the sea, and from those toward the sea toward the east. Its length will be like one of the portions, from the sea-facing boundaries, with the length extending to the eastern boundaries of the land.
It will be his possession in Israel. Israel’s rulers will no longer oppress My people, and the house of Israel will inherit the land according to their tribes.
Thus says the Lord God: Enough, rulers of Israel! Remove injustice and suffering, and practice judgment and righteousness. Take oppression away from My people, says the Lord God.
“Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.
The ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they go out, he will go out.
At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

If the ruler makes a pledged offering, a burnt offering for well-being to the Lord, he will open for himself the gate facing east and offer his burnt offering and his offerings for well-being as he does on the Sabbath day. He will go out and close the doors after he has gone out.
He will prepare an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the Lord; in the morning he will prepare it.
In the morning he will prepare with it a grain offering of a sixth of the measure and a third of a hin of oil to mix the fine flour: a grain offering to the Lord, a permanent command.
You all will prepare the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil; you all will prepare them in the morning as a continual burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord God: If the ruler gives one of his sons a gift from his inheritance, this will belong to his sons as an inherited possession.
If he gives a gift to one of his servants, it will belong to him until the year of release, and he will return it to the ruler. But the inheritance of his sons will belong to them.

The ruler will certainly not take from the people’s inheritance to oppress them. He will give his sons an inheritance from his own possession, so that none of My people is scattered from his possession.”
He brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the north-facing recessed chamber of the priests’ holy places. Look—there was a separated place there.

The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the offerings for ignorance and for sin, and there bake the entire grain offering, so as not to carry it out into the outer court and sanctify the people.”
He brought me out into the outer court and led me around its four sides. Look—a court at one side of the court, and a court at another side of the court!
At the four sides of the court was a small court, forty cubits long and thirty cubits broad; the four had one measure.
There were recessed chambers all around them, around the four, with kitchens made underneath the recessed chambers all around.
He said to me, “These are the kitchen houses, where those ministering to the house will boil the people’s sacrificial animals.”
The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.
The ruler will present burnt offerings to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,
with a grain offering of a cake for the ram, and for the lambs an offering as the gift of his hand, with a hin of oil for each cake.
On the day of the new moon there will be an unblemished calf and six lambs, and the ram will be unblemished.
A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.
When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

When the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate. He will not return through the gate by which he entered, but will go out straight opposite it.
Thus says the Lord God: These are the boundaries of the land you will allot as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel—an addition of a measured portion.
You will inherit it, each like his brother, the land for which I raised My hand to give it to their fathers. This land will fall to you as an inheritance.
These are the boundaries of the land toward the north: from the Great Sea, descending and dividing at the entrance of Hamath—Seddada,
Berotha, Sebraim, Heliam, between the boundaries of Damascus and the boundaries of Hamath, the court of Saunan, which are above the boundaries of Auranitis.
These are the boundaries from the sea, from the court of Ainan, the boundaries of Damascus, and the parts toward the north.
The eastern parts lie between Auranitis and Damascus, and between Galaaditis and the land of Israel; the Jordan marks the boundary as far as the sea east of Palm Grove. These are the eastern parts.
The parts toward the south and southwest run from Thaiman and Palm Grove to the water of Marimoth Kades, extending to the Great Sea. This is the south and southwest side.
This is the side of the Great Sea: it forms the boundary as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, as far as its entrance. These are the sea-facing parts of Hamath.
You will divide this land for them, for the tribes of Israel.

You will cast lots for it for yourselves and for the sojourners dwelling among you who have fathered sons among you. They will be to you as native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they will eat from an inheritance among Israel’s tribes.
They will be in a tribe of sojourners, among the sojourners who are with them; there you will give them an inheritance, says the Lord God.

These are the names of the tribes: from the northern beginning, along the side of the descending, dividing way toward the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ainan, the boundary of Damascus toward the north, along the side of Hamath’s court; the eastern parts as far as the sea will belong to them—Dan, one portion.

From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,
for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the duties of the house and did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, as the Levites strayed.
They will have the first portion given from the land’s first portions, most holy, from the Levites’ boundaries.
The Levites will have the land adjoining the priests’ boundaries, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad. The whole length will be twenty-five thousand and the breadth twenty thousand.
None of it will be sold or measured out, nor will the land’s first produce be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.
The five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand will be a forewall for the city, for dwelling and its intervening space. The city will be in its midst.

These are its measurements: on the north, four thousand five hundred; on the south, four thousand five hundred; on the east, four thousand five hundred; and toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.
The city will have an intervening space: two hundred fifty toward the north, two hundred fifty toward the south, two hundred fifty toward the east, and two hundred fifty toward the sea.

The remaining length adjoining the first portions of the holy areas will be ten thousand toward the east and ten thousand toward the sea; these will be the holy place’s first portions, and its produce will be bread for the city’s workers.
The city’s workers, from all Israel’s tribes, will work it.
From Dan’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Asher, one portion.
The entire first portion will be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. You will set apart its holy portion as a square, from the city’s possession.

The remainder will belong to the ruler on this side and that side, from the holy first portions and toward the city’s possession, extending twenty-five thousand in length to the eastern boundaries, and toward the sea extending twenty-five thousand to the sea-facing boundaries, adjoining the ruler’s portions. The first portion of the holy areas and the house’s sanctuary will be in its midst.
From the Levites’ possession and from the city’s possession, it will be in the midst of the rulers; between Judah’s boundaries and Benjamin’s boundaries it will belong to the rulers.
As for the remaining tribes, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Benjamin, one portion.
From Benjamin’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Simeon, one portion.
From Simeon’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Issachar, one portion.
From Issachar’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Zebulun, one portion.
From Zebulun’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Gad, one portion.
From Gad’s boundaries toward the southwest, its boundaries will run from Thaiman and the water of Marimoth Kades, an inheritance as far as the Great Sea.
This is the land you will cast lots for among Israel’s tribes, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
From Asher’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Naphtali, one portion.
From Naphtali’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Manasseh, one portion.
From Manasseh’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Ephraim, one portion.
From Ephraim’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Reuben, one portion.
From Reuben’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Judah, one portion.

From Judah’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts, will be the first portion set apart, twenty-five thousand in breadth, with a length like one of the portions from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts. The holy place will be in their midst.
The first portion they set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad.
“And you, son of man, take a sword sharper than a barber’s razor. Obtain it for yourself and pass it over your head and your beard. Take a balance with weights and divide the hairs;

burn a quarter with fire inside the city when the days of siege are complete. Take a quarter and burn it up in its midst; cut down a quarter with the sword around it, and scatter a quarter to the wind. I will draw a sword after them.
Take a few of them in number and gather them into your cloak.
Take some of these again, cast them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it fire will go out. And you will say to the entire house of Israel,
Thus says the Lord: Clap your hand, stamp your foot, and say, “Aha! Aha!” over all the abominations of the house of Israel; they will fall by sword, death and famine.

and say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord to the mountains, hills, ravines and wooded valleys: Behold, I am bringing a sword against you, and your high places will be destroyed,
The time has come; behold, the day! Let the buyer not rejoice, nor the seller lament;
He said to me, “Go in and see the lawlessness these people are committing here.”
To these others He said while I listened, “Go behind him into the city and strike. Do not spare with your eyes, and have no mercy.

Old man, young man, maiden, infants and women—kill them to obliteration. But do not approach anyone upon whom the sign is. Begin at My holy places.” They began with the elderly men who were inside the house.
Drink, you too, a fullness of dishonor instead of glory; be tossed and shaken! The cup of the Lord’s right hand has come around to you, and dishonor has gathered upon your glory.
Woe to the one saying to wood, ‘Wake and rise!’ and to stone, ‘Be lifted up!’ It is an appearance, a plate of gold and silver, and no breath at all is in it.
The Lord answered me: “Write a vision clearly on a boxwood tablet, so that the one reading these things may pursue them.
But the Lord is in His holy sanctuary; let all the earth revere Him.”

In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.
Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.
“Thus says the Lord Almighty: Ask the priests about the law, saying:

And you, do not pray for this people or petition for them with supplication and prayer, because I will not listen when they call upon Me, in their time of affliction.

But I, like a guileless lamb led to be slaughtered, did not know. Against me they devised an evil design, saying: Come, let us put wood into his bread and wipe him out from the land of the living, and his name will certainly be remembered no more.
Hear the words of this covenant. And you will speak to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem,
Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth who seek my soul, who say: You must certainly not prophesy in the Lord’s name; otherwise you will die by our hands.

which I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them up from Egypt’s land, from the iron furnace, saying: Hear My voice and do everything I command you, and you will be My people and I will be your God,
And the Lord said to me: Read these words in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, saying: Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
Sow wheat and harvest thorns! Their allotments will not benefit them. Be ashamed of your boasting, of reproach before the Lord.
For even your brothers and your father’s house rejected you, and they shouted; they gathered behind you. Do not trust them, because they will speak good things to you.
Is My inheritance to Me a hyena’s cave, or a cave around her? Go, gather all the field’s wild beasts, and let them come to eat her!
Thus says the Lord: Go, acquire a linen waistcloth for yourself, and put it around your waist, and it will not pass through water.
Hear and give ear, and do not exalt yourselves, because the Lord has spoken.
Give glory to the Lord your God before darkness comes and before your feet stumble on dark mountains; you will wait for light, and there is death’s shadow, and they will be placed in darkness.
Say to the king and those exercising power: Humble yourselves and sit down, because your crown of glory was taken down from your head.
Lift your eyes, Jerusalem, and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock given to you, the sheep of your glory?
Take the waistcloth around your waist, and rise and go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in the rock’s opening.
And after many days the Lord said to me: Rise, go to the Euphrates, and take from there the waistcloth that I commanded you to hide there.
And the Lord said to me: Do not pray for good things for this people,
And you will say this word to them: Bring tears down upon your eyes day and night, and let them not cease, because the daughter of My people was utterly crushed, with a very painful wound.
And the Lord said to me: If Moses and Samuel stand before Me, My soul is not toward them. Send this people away, and let them go out.
And you must not take a wife, says the Lord, Israel’s God,
Thus says the Lord: Do not enter their gathering or go to beat yourself in mourning, and do not mourn them, because I have removed My peace from this people.
You must not enter a house of drinking to sit with them to eat and drink.
Behold, they say to me: Where is the Lord’s word? Let it come!
Do not become an estrangement to me, sparing me in an evil day.
Let those pursuing me be ashamed, and may I not be ashamed; may they be terrified, and may I not be terrified. Bring an evil day upon them; crush them with double crushing.
Thus says the Lord: Go and stand in the gates of your people’s sons, through which Judah’s kings enter and leave, and in all Jerusalem’s gates,
and you will say to them: Hear the Lord’s word, kings of Judah, all Judea and all Jerusalem, who enter these gates:
Thus says the Lord: Guard your souls, and do not lift burdens on the Sabbath day or go out through Jerusalem’s gates,
and do not bring burdens out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and you must do no work; consecrate the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers. And they did not hear or incline their ear,
And if you truly listen to Me, says the Lord, not bringing burdens through this city’s gates on the Sabbath day and consecrating the Sabbath day by doing no work,

And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask now among the nations: Who heard such horrifying things that virgin Israel committed so greatly?

And they said: Come, let us devise a design against Jeremiah, because law will not perish from a priest, counsel from the discerning, or word from a prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will hear all his words.
Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my claim of right.
Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear My words.
Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the sword’s hands. Let their women become childless and widowed, their men killed by death, and their young men fallen by the sword in war.
Then the Lord said to me: Go and acquire a molded earthenware jar, and bring some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests.
and say: Thus says the Lord: This is how I will smash this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is smashed that cannot be healed again.
And go out to the burial ground of the sons of their children, which is before the Charsith Gate, and read there all the words that I speak to you.

And say to them: Hear the Lord’s word, kings of Judah, men of Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and those entering these gates. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place, so that both ears of everyone hearing them will ring.
Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully. See whether such things have happened.
Turn your foot from a rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said, I will be strong, because she had loved strangers and went after them.
Hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord: Have I become a wilderness to Israel, or a land left barren? Why did My people say, We will not be ruled, and we will come to Thee no more?
And you said, I am innocent; let His fury turn away from me. Behold, I enter judgment with you because you say, I did not sin.
Hear the Lord’s word, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.

Because I heard the reproach of many gathering all around: Rise against him, and let us rise against him, all you men who are his friends! Watch his purpose, to see whether he will be deceived and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.
Sing to the Lord; praise Him, because He rescued a poor person’s life from the hand of those doing evil.
Accursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day my mother bore me not be a day to pray for!
Let that man be like the cities the Lord overthrew in fury without changing His mind. Let him hear a cry in the morning and a battle shout at noon,

House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.
Ask the Lord about us, because Babylon’s king has come against us, whether the Lord will act according to all His wonders, so that he goes away from us.
And Jeremiah said to them: Say this to Zedekiah king of Judah:
And say to this people: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have set before your face the way of life and the way of death.
Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,
Do not weep for the dead or lament him; weep bitterly for the one going out, because he will never return or see his homeland.
and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan and shout to the far side of the sea, because all your lovers have been shattered.

Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.
Therefore let their way become a slippery place for them in darkness, and they will be tripped and fall in it, because I will bring evils upon them in their year of visitation, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.
Let the prophet in whom there is a dream tell his dream, and the one to whom My word comes tell My word in truth. What has chaff to do with wheat? So are My words, says the Lord.
And if this people, a priest, or a prophet asks you, What is the Lord’s burden? say to them, You are the burden, and I will dash you down, says the Lord.
And do not name the Lord’s burden again, because a person’s own word will be his burden.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you said this word, The Lord’s burden, though I sent to you saying, Do not say The Lord’s burden,
Thus says the Lord: Let Elam’s bow be shattered, the beginning of their dominion.
saying: Turn, each from his evil way and from your evil practices, and you will dwell upon the land I gave to you and your fathers from age to age.
Do not follow foreign gods to serve them and bow down to them, so that you do not provoke Me by your hands’ works into harming you.
Go up, Gilead, and take resin for the virgin daughter Egypt. In vain you multiplied your remedies; there is no benefit for you.
Announce to Migdol and proclaim to Memphis. Say, Take your position and prepare, for the sword has devoured your smilax growth.
Call Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt by the name Saon-esbi-emoeed.
Prepare belongings for deportation, resident daughter Egypt, for Memphis will become a ruin and will be called Woe because no inhabitants remain in her.
But do not fear, My slave Jacob, nor be terrified, Israel, for I am saving you from afar and your offspring from their captivity. Jacob will return, be quiet, and sleep, and no one will trouble him.

Do not fear, My servant Jacob, says the Lord, for I am with you. I will make an end of every nation where I thrust you out, but I certainly will not make you perish. I will discipline you for judgment and certainly will not acquit you.
Take up weapons and shields, and advance to war!
Saddle the horses; mount, riders! Take your positions in your helmets. Hold your spears forward; put on your breastplates!
Let the swift not flee, nor the strong man escape. Northward, in the places beside the Euphrates, they grew weak and have fallen.
Mount the horses; prepare the chariots! Go out, warriors of the Ethiopians and Libyans equipped with weapons! And Lydians, go up and draw the bow!
Deploy against Babylon all around, all who stretch the bow. Shoot at her; do not spare your arrows.
Clap against her! Her hands were disabled, her battlements fell, and her wall was demolished. For this is vengeance from God; take vengeance upon her. Do to her as she did.
Destroy seed from Babylon, the one holding a sickle at harvest. Before the Greek sword, each will return to his people and flee to his land.
Announce among the nations and make it heard; do not hide it. Say, Babylon has been captured! Bel was disgraced, the fearless one; the delicate one was handed over, Marodach.
Go fiercely against her and her inhabitants. Take vengeance, sword, and make her disappear, says the Lord; do everything I command you.
for her times have arrived. Open her storehouses; search her like a cave and destroy her. Let no remnant of her remain.

Give orders against Babylon to many, to everyone drawing a bow. Encamp against her all around; let none of her people escape. Repay her according to her works; do to her all she did, for she resisted the Lord, Israel’s holy God.
Separate yourselves from Babylon’s midst and the Chaldeans’ land; come out and become like dragons before sheep.
The Lord has brought forth His judgment. Come, let us announce in Zion the works of the Lord our God.
Prepare the arrows; fill the quivers. The Lord roused the spirit of the Medes’ king, for His anger against Babylon is to destroy her. This is the Lord’s vengeance, vengeance for His people.
Raise a signal on Babylon’s walls; set up quivers, raise guards, prepare weapons, for the Lord has undertaken and will do what He spoke against Babylon’s inhabitants,

Raise a signal on the earth; sound a trumpet among the nations. Consecrate nations against her; give orders against her to Ararat’s kingdoms from Me and to the Ashkenazites. Set up arrow batteries against her; bring up horses against her like a multitude of locusts.
Consecrate nations against her: the king of the Medes and of all the earth, his leaders and all his generals.
Against her let the archer stretch his bow, and let the man who has armor put it on. Do not spare her young men; obliterate her whole force.
You who escape from the land, go on; do not stand still. You who are far away, remember the Lord, and let Jerusalem rise in your hearts.
Flee from Babylon’s midst; each of you save your life. Do not be cast away in her injustice, for her time of vengeance is from the Lord; He is repaying her recompense.
and say, Lord, Lord, Thou spakest against this place to destroy it and leave no inhabitants in it, from human to livestock, for it will be a ruin for ever.
and say, Thus Babylon will sink and certainly not rise because of the evils I am bringing upon her.
Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered. Lament her! Take resin for her corruption, if somehow she may be healed.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her; let each of us go to our own land, for her judgment reached heaven and rose to the stars.
sword of the Lord? How long will you not be quiet? Return to your sheath; rest and be lifted away!

Go and read these words toward the north: Return to Me, dwelling of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set My face firmly against you, because I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not be angry with you for ever.
Return, children who have withdrawn, says the Lord, because I will rule over you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you into Zion,
Lift your eyes straight ahead and see: where have you not been defiled? You sat for them on the roads like a solitary crow, and polluted the land with your prostitution and your evils.
Return, returning children, and I will heal your fractures. Behold, we will be Thy servants, because Thou art the Lord our God.

Shout aloud, Heshbon, for Gai perished! Cry out, daughters of Rabbath; put on sackcloth, be seized with distress, and beat yourselves over Melchom, for he will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.
For Kedar, queen of the courtyard, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus said the Lord: Rise and go up against Kedar, and fill the sons of Kedem!
They will take their tents and sheep, their garments, all their equipment, and camels for themselves. Call destruction against them on every side!
Flee far away; go deep to dwell, you who stay in the courtyard, for Babylon’s king planned counsel against you and devised a purpose against you.
Rise and go up against a stable nation living in refreshment, with neither doors nor pins nor bars; they lodge alone.
I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!
Move in lament for him, all who surround him, all who know his name. Say, How the renowned staff is shattered, the rod of grandeur!
Come down from glory and sit in dampness, resident Dibon. Be crushed, for Moab perished; he came up against you, ruining your fortification.
Stand on the road and look, you who live in Aroer. Ask the one fleeing and the one being saved, and say, What happened?
Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the Lord. Moab will strike with his hand and become a laughingstock himself.
Therefore wail over Moab from every side; cry out over the men of Kiradas of drought.
Flee and save your lives, and you will be like a wild donkey in the wilderness!
Give signs to Moab, for she will surely be kindled; all her cities will become an untrodden place. From where will an inhabitant come to her?
Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
And say to them: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Drink, get drunk, and vomit; you will fall and certainly not rise before the sword I am sending among you.

And prophesy these words against them and say: The Lord will give an oracle from on high; from His holy place He will raise His voice. He will give an oracular word over His place, and they will answer with Aidad, like grape-gatherers. And upon those dwelling upon the earth,
Raise a shout, shepherds, and cry out; beat yourselves in mourning, rams of the sheep, because your days for slaughter have been fulfilled, and you will fall like choice rams.
And now make your ways and works better and hear the Lord’s voice, and the Lord will cease from the evils He spoke against you.
And behold, I am in your hands. Do to me what is advantageous and better for you.

Thus said the Lord: Stand in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and deliver an oracle to all the Judeans and all who come to bow down in the Lord’s house—all the words I commanded you to deliver to them. Do not take away a word.
And say: Thus said the Lord: If you do not hear Me, walking in My ordinances that I set before your face,
And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!
And I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying: Bring your neck,
and work for Babylon’s king, because they prophesy unjust things to you.

I spoke to you, all this people, and the priests, saying: Thus said the Lord: Do not listen to the prophets’ words prophesying to you, Behold, the vessels of the Lord’s house will return from Babylon, because they prophesy unjust things to you. I did not send them.
Thus said the Lord: Make bonds and neck collars and put them around your neck,
and send them to Idumea’s king, Moab’s king, the king of Ammon’s sons, Tyre’s king, and Sidon’s king by their messengers coming to meet them in Jerusalem, to Zedekiah king of Judah.
And command them to tell their masters: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Say this to your masters:
And do not listen to your false prophets, those divining for you, those dreaming for you, your omens, or your enchantments, who say: You will certainly not work for Babylon’s king.
Go and tell Hananiah: Thus said the Lord: You smashed wooden collars, and I will make iron collars in their place.
And seek Me earnestly, and you will find Me, because you will seek Me with your whole heart,
Was it not for this that he sent to you in Babylon, saying: It is far off. Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens, and you will eat their fruit?
Send to the deportees, saying: Thus said the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nelamite: Since Shemaiah prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and made you trust in unjust things,
Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens and eat their fruits,
and take wives and beget sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands. Multiply and do not become fewer,
and seek the peace of the land where I deported you, and pray to the Lord for them, because in its peace you will have peace.
Because thus said the Lord: Do not let the false prophets among you persuade you, and do not let your diviners persuade you. Do not listen to your dreams that you dream,
Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Write in a book all the words I delivered to you as oracles,
Ask and see whether a male gave birth, and about fear in which they will hold loins and salvation. For I have seen every person with his hands upon his loins; faces turned toward jaundice—
Hear the Lord’s word, nations, and announce it to the farther islands. Say: He who winnowed Israel will gather him and guard him like one tending his flock.
Thus said the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from your tears, because your works have a reward, and they will return from enemies’ land,
Thus said the Lord: I found warmth in the wilderness among those who perished by the sword. Go, and do not destroy Israel.
Stand firm, Zion; carry out punishment; set your heart upon the shoulders. Turn back along the road you traveled, virgin Israel; turn back to your cities in mourning.
Because there is a day of calling by those making their defense in Ephraim’s mountains: Rise and go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.
Because thus said the Lord to Jacob: Rejoice and neigh aloud toward the head of the nations; make it heard and praise. Say: The Lord saved His people, Israel’s remnant!
Thus said the Lord Almighty: Take this purchase document and the document that has been read, and put it in an earthenware vessel so that it may last many days.
Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will the schemes of your troubles exist within you?
For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Break up fallow ground for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.

Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, lest My fury come out like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your practices.
Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.
Cry out to Me and I will answer you. I will announce to you great, mighty things you have not known.

When six years are complete, you must send away your Hebrew brother who is sold to you. He will work for you six years, and you must send him away free. But they did not obey Me or incline their ears.
Thus said the Lord: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, Thus said the Lord: This city will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king. He will seize it and burn it with fire.
Thus says the Lord: Go and say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants, Will you really not accept discipline and hear My words?

I sent you My servants the prophets, saying, Each of you, turn from his evil way and improve your practices. Do not follow other gods to serve them, and you will live on the land I gave you and your fathers. But you did not incline your ears or listen.
Go to the house of the Rechabites. Bring them into the Lord’s house, into one of the courts, and give them wine to drink.
They said, We certainly will not drink wine, because Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us: Neither you nor your sons must ever drink wine.
You must not build a house or sow seed, and you must not have a vineyard. You must live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the land where you spend your time.
They said to Baruch, Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Let no one know where you are.

Take a writing roll and write on it all the words I have delivered to you as oracles concerning Jerusalem, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah until today.
Take another roll again and write all the words that were on the roll which King Jehoiakim burned.
Say, Thus said the Lord: You burned this roll, saying, Why did you write in it that Babylon’s king will certainly enter and destroy this land, and people and animals will cease from it?
Read from this roll in the people’s hearing at the Lord’s house on a fast day, and read it to all Judah’s people coming from their city.
Thus said the Lord: Tell Judah’s king, who sent to you to seek Me, Pharaoh’s force, which came out to help you, will return to Egypt’s land.
For thus said the Lord: Do not suppose within yourselves, The Chaldeans will flee and leave us. They certainly will not leave.
If the rulers hear that I spoke to you, come to you, and say, Tell us what the king said to you. Hide nothing from us and we certainly will not kill you. What did the king say to you?
tell them, I am casting my appeal for mercy before the king’s eyes, not to send me back to Jonathan’s house to die there.
Go and tell Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: I am bringing My words upon this city for calamity, not good.

Behold, I am staying before you at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come against you. Gather wine and summer fruit, gather oil, put them in your containers, and live in the cities you have taken over.
Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Let me go and strike down Ishmael, and let no one know, lest he take your life and all Judah gathered to you be scattered, and Judah’s survivors perish.
Gedaliah said to Johanan, Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsehoods about Ishmael.

But if not, go off and return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom Babylon’s king appointed in Judah’s land, and live with him among the people in Judah’s land. Go wherever it seems good in your eyes to go. The chief guard gave him gifts and sent him away.
Gedaliah swore to them and their men, saying, Do not be afraid of the Chaldeans’ servants. Live in the land and work for Babylon’s king, and it will be better for you.
Ten men found there said to Ishmael, Do not kill us, for we have stores in the countryside: wheat, barley, honey, and oil. He passed them by and did not kill them among their brothers.
Do not fear Babylon’s king, whom you fear. Do not fear, says the Lord, for I am with you to rescue you and save you from his hand.
These are the things the Lord spoke concerning you, Judah’s survivors: Do not enter Egypt. And now know for certain
Let the Lord your God tell us the way we should go and the matter we should carry out.
Go up against her battlements and tear them down, but do not make a complete end. Leave her supports, because they belong to the Lord.
Hear these things now, foolish and senseless people: they have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear.
And they did not say in their heart: Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us early and late rain at the time of fulfillment of the harvest’s command, and He kept it for us.
Say, Thus said the Lord: I am sending and will bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will place his throne above these stones that you hid and raise his weapons over them.
Take large stones for yourself and hide them in the forecourt at the gate of Pharaoh’s house at Taphnas, before the eyes of Judah’s men.

We will certainly do everything that will come from our mouths: burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem. We were filled with bread, were well off, and saw no calamities.
Tell him, Thus said the Lord: Those I have built up I am tearing down, and those I have planted I am plucking up.
Are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them, for I am bringing calamities upon all flesh, says the Lord. I will give your life as gain wherever you walk.
I sent you My servants the prophets at dawn, and I sent them saying, Do not commit this act of defilement that I hate.

Take courage, sons of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem, and signal with a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a sign above Beth-haccherem, because evils have looked out from the north, and great crushing is taking place,

Thus says the Lord: Stand upon the roads and see, and ask for the Lord’s eternal paths and see which is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find purification for your souls. And they said, ‘We will not go.’
I have appointed watchers over you: Hear the trumpet’s sound! And they said, ‘We will not hear.’
Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.
Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.
Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.
Call them rejected silver, because the Lord rejected them.
Prepare yourselves for war against her! Rise, and let us go up against her at noon! Woe to us, because the day has declined, because evening’s shadows are failing!
Rise, and let us go up in the night and destroy her foundations!
For thus says the Lord: Cut down her trees; pour out a force upon Jerusalem. O false city, all oppression is within her!
For thus says the Lord: Glean, glean Israel’s remnants like a vine; turn back like the grape-gatherer to his basket.
And you, do not pray for this people, and do not ask that they receive mercy, and do not pray or approach Me on their behalf, because I will not listen.
Hear the Lord’s word, all Judea!
Thus says the Lord: Gather your whole burnt offerings with your sacrifices, and eat meat!
But this utterance I commanded them, saying: Hear My voice, and I will be your God and you will be My people; and walk in all My ways that I command you, so that it may be well with you.
Do not put your confidence in yourselves on false words, because they will not benefit you at all when they say, ‘The Lord’s temple, the Lord’s temple it is.’
For if you truly correct your ways and practices and truly execute judgment between a man and his neighbor,
and do not oppress a newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm,
then I will settle you in this place, in the land I gave your fathers, from age to age.
Why are we sitting? Gather, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and made us drink gall-water, because we sinned before Him.
Give ear now and hear: they will not speak thus; there is no person repenting of his evil, saying, ‘What have I done?’ The runner ceased from his course like a sweating horse in its neighing.

Who is the discerning person? Let him understand this; and the one to whom the word of the Lord’s mouth comes, let him announce it to you: for what reason did the land perish, kindled like a wilderness so that no one passes through it?
Thus says the Lord: Call the women who lament, and let them come; send for the skilled women, and let them speak,
and let them take up a dirge over you; let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.
Hear God’s word now, women, and let your ears receive His mouth’s words; teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor a dirge.
Thus says the Lord: Let no wise man boast in his wisdom, let no strong man boast in his strength, and let no rich man boast in his wealth,
but let whoever boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing that I am the Lord, doing mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, because in these is My will, says the Lord.
Each of you, guard against his neighbor, and do not put trust in their brothers, because every brother will trip with the heel, and every friend will walk deceitfully.

Take up mourning for the mountains and a dirge for the wilderness paths, because they failed for lack of people. They did not hear the sound of possessions; from heaven’s birds to livestock, they were displaced and went away.
because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.

Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,

You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not murder’; and ‘whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.’ But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
