Bring to the Lord, families of nations; bring to the Lord glory and honor.
Bring to the Lord glory for His name; take up sacrifices and enter His courts.
Bow down to the Lord in His holy court; let all the earth be shaken before Him.
Of David, when his land is being established. The Lord has become King! Let the earth exult; let many islands rejoice.
You who love the Lord, hate evil! The Lord guards the souls of His holy ones; He will rescue them from the hand of sinners.
Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness.
Let all who bow down to carved images be ashamed, those who boast in their idols. Bow down to Him, all His angels!
A psalm of David. Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done wonders. His right hand and His holy arm won salvation for Him.
Shout to God, all the earth; sing and exult and make music.
Make music to the Lord with a lyre, with a lyre and the sound of a psalm.
Let the sea be shaken, and all that fills it, the inhabited world and those who dwell in it.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at His footstool, for He is holy.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down toward His holy mountain, for holy is the Lord our God.
A psalm for thanksgiving. Shout to the Lord, all the earth.
Serve the Lord with gladness; enter before Him with exultation.
Know that the Lord—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the sheep of His pasture.
Know that the Lord—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the sheep of His pasture.
Enter His gates with thanksgiving, His courts with hymns. Give thanks to Him; praise His name.
Do not disobey the fear of the Lord, and do not approach Him with a divided heart.
Do not play the hypocrite in people’s talk, and keep watch over your lips.

Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall and bring dishonor upon your soul. The Lord will uncover your hidden things and cast you down in the midst of the assembly, because you did not approach the fear of the Lord and your heart is full of deceit.
Do not be clever about doing your work, and do not glorify yourself in a time of distress.
Child, glorify your soul with gentleness, and give it honor according to its worth.
Do not bear anger toward your neighbor over every wrong, and do nothing by acts of insolence.

Child, do not let your activities concern too many things. If you multiply them, you will not escape blame; even if you pursue, you will certainly not catch up, and even by running away you will certainly not escape.
Do not praise a man for his beauty or loathe a person for his appearance.
Stand firm in your covenant, occupy yourself with it, and grow old in your work.
Do not marvel at a sinner’s works, but trust the Lord and remain at your labor. For it is easy in the Lord’s eyes to make a poor person rich quickly and suddenly.
Do not say, “What need do I have, and what good things will be mine from now on?”
Do not say, “I have enough; what harm can come to me from now on?”
Call no one happy before his death, and a man will be known in his children.
Do not bring every person into your house, for the deceitful person has many ambushes.
Beware of an evildoer, for he devises evil, lest he give you lasting blame.
Do not boast in the clothing you wear or exalt yourself on a day of glory. For the Lord’s works are wonderful, and His works are hidden from human beings.
Do not find fault before investigating; understand first, and then rebuke.
Do not answer before hearing, and do not interrupt in the middle of someone’s words.
Do not quarrel about a matter that is no concern of yours, and do not sit together in the judgment of sinners.
If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there will be gratitude for your good deeds.

Even if he humbles himself and walks bowed down, keep your soul alert and guard against him. You will be toward him like someone who has wiped a mirror, and you will know that it has not completely corroded.

Do not station him beside yourself, lest he overthrow you and stand in your place. Do not seat him at your right hand, lest he seek your seat; then in the end you will recognize my words and be pierced by my sayings.
Do good to a godly person, and you will find repayment; if not from him, then from the Most High.
There will be no good things for the one who persists in evil and the one who gives no alms.
Give to the godly person, and do not support the sinner.

Do good to the humble person, and do not give to the ungodly. Hold back his loaves and do not give them to him, so that he does not use them to overpower you. For you will receive double evils for all the good things you do to him.
Give to the good person, and do not support the sinner.
Do not thrust yourself forward, lest you be pushed away; do not stand too far off, so that you are not forgotten.
Do not insist on speaking with him as an equal, and do not trust his many words. For through much talk he will test you and examine you as though smiling.
Keep watch and take very great care, because you are walking alongside your downfall.

Do not lift a burden beyond you, and do not associate with someone stronger and richer than you. What fellowship can an earthen pot have with a cauldron? One will strike, and the other will be shattered.
Take care not to be misled or brought low through your folly.
When a powerful person summons you, be retiring, and he will summon you all the more.
Child, do yourself good according to what you have, and bring offerings worthily to the Lord.
Remember that death will not delay, and the covenant of Hades has not been shown to you.
Before you die, do good to a friend; according to your strength, reach out and give to him.
Do not miss a good day, and do not let your share of a good desire pass you by.
Give and receive, and beguile your soul, for in Hades there is no seeking luxury.
Go out after her like a tracker, and lie in wait on her paths.
Do not say, “Because of the Lord I fell away,” for He will not do the things He hates.
Do not say, “He Himself led me astray,” for He has no need of a sinful man.
Do not desire a multitude of useless children, or rejoice in ungodly sons.
Do not say, “I will be hidden from the Lord; who will remember me from on high? Among a numerous people I will certainly not be known, for what is my soul in the immeasurable creation?”
Even if they multiply, do not rejoice in them unless the fear of the Lord is with them.
Listen to me, child, and learn knowledge; attend to my words with your heart.
Do not trust in their life or rely on their multitude. For one is better than a thousand, and it is better to die childless than to have ungodly children.
He said to them, “Beware of every injustice,” and commanded each of them concerning the neighbor.
Return to the Lord and leave sins behind; petition Him face to face and lessen your stumbling.
Come back to the Most High, turn away from injustice, and hate abomination intensely.
Child, do not add reproach to good deeds, or the grief of words to any gift.
Learn before speaking, and attend to your health before illness.
Examine yourself before judgment, and at the hour of visitation you will find atonement.
Humble yourself before you fall ill, and show repentance at the time of sins.
Do not be held back from repaying a vow at the right time, and do not wait until death to be justified.
Prepare yourself before making a vow, and do not become like a person testing the Lord.
Remember wrath in the days of death, and the time of retribution when the face is turned away.
Remember a time of famine in a time of fullness, poverty and need in days of wealth.
Do not walk after your desires, and restrain your appetites.
If you supply your soul with the satisfaction of desire, it will make you an object of your enemies’ gloating.
Do not rejoice in great luxury, lest you be bound to contribute to it.
Do not become poor by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
Have you heard a word? Let it die with you. Take courage; it will certainly not make you burst.
Question a friend; perhaps he did not do it, and if he did, question him so that he may not repeat it.
Question your neighbor; perhaps he did not say it, and if he has said it, question him so that he may not say it again.
Question a friend, for slander often occurs; do not trust every report.
but the one who hates chatter diminishes evil.
Never repeat a word, and you will certainly lose nothing.
Do not tell it to friend or enemy, and unless silence is a sin for you, do not reveal it.
Child, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for testing.
Look at the generations of old and see: Who trusted in the Lord and was put to shame? Who remained in His fear and was abandoned? Who called upon Him and was disregarded by Him?
Let us fall into the hands of the Lord and not into human hands, for as His greatness is, so also is His mercy.
Set your heart straight and endure; do not rush in a time of calamity.
Cling to Him and do not withdraw, so that you may grow in your last days.
Accept whatever is brought upon you, and be patient amid the changes of your humiliation.
Trust Him, and He will support you. Set your ways straight and hope in Him.
You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy, and do not turn aside, lest you fall.
You who fear the Lord, trust Him, and your reward will certainly not fail.
You who fear the Lord, hope for good things, for eternal gladness and mercy.
Child, have you sinned? Do not add to it any more, and pray concerning your earlier sins.
Flee from sin as from the presence of a snake, for if you approach it, it will bite you. Its teeth are lions’ teeth, destroying human lives.
The one who hates rebuke is in a sinner’s tracks, but the one who fears the Lord will turn back in heart.

Weep over a dead person, for he has lost the light; weep also over a fool, for he has lost understanding. Weep more gently over the dead, because he has found rest, but the fool’s life is worse than death.

Do not multiply words with a fool or go to someone without understanding. Guard against him so that you do not have trouble, and you will certainly not be stained by what he shakes off. Turn away from him, and you will find rest and will certainly not grow weary of his madness.
If you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back.

If you open your mouth against a friend, do not be afraid, for there is reconciliation—except for reproach, pride, disclosure of a secret, and a treacherous blow; at these things every friend will flee.
Establish trust with your neighbor in poverty, so that you may be filled together with him in his good circumstances. Stay with him in a time of affliction, so that you may share his inheritance.
There is an expression comparable to death; let it not be found in Jacob’s inheritance. For all these things will depart from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.
Do not accustom your mouth to crude ignorance, for sinful speech is in it.

Remember your father and mother, for you sit among dignitaries, lest you forget yourself before them and become foolish through your habit; then you will wish you had not been born and curse the day of your birth.
Listen, children, to discipline of the mouth; the one who keeps it will certainly not be caught.
Do not accustom your mouth to an oath, and do not make a habit of naming the Holy One.
Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled from my produce.
The one who obeys me will not be ashamed, and those who work in me will not sin.”
Then the Creator of all commanded me; my Creator settled my tent and said, ‘Dwell in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel.’
Do not fall for a woman’s beauty, and do not long for a woman.
Do not give water an outlet, or an evil wife freedom of speech.
If she does not walk according to your direction, cut her off from your flesh.
Keep a firm watch over a headstrong daughter, so that she does not find freedom and use it for herself.
Be on guard after a shameless eye, and do not marvel if she offends against you.
Love a friend and keep faith with him; but if you reveal his secrets, do not pursue him afterward.
Do not pursue him, because he has gone far away and escaped like a gazelle from a trap.
Do not praise a man before he reasons, for this is the testing of human beings.
The one who takes revenge will find revenge from the Lord, and He will certainly keep his sins in view.
Forgive your neighbor’s wrong, and then when you pray, your sins will be released.
Behold, fence your property with thorns; bind up your silver and gold.
Make a balance and a weight for your words, and make a door and a bar for your mouth.
Take care lest you slip through it, lest you fall before someone lying in ambush.
Remember the last things and stop being hostile; remember decay and death, and remain in the commandments.
Remember the commandments and do not be resentful toward your neighbor; remember the covenant of the Most High and overlook ignorance.
Keep away from quarrelling, and you will lessen sins, for a hot-tempered person will kindle a quarrel.
Lose silver for a brother and a friend, and do not let it corrode under a stone to destruction.
Place your treasure according to the Most High’s commandments, and it will benefit you more than gold.
Store up almsgiving in your chambers, and it will rescue you from every affliction.
Do not forget a guarantor’s favors, for he has given his life on your behalf.
Lend to your neighbor at his time of need, and in turn repay your neighbor at the appointed time.
Support your neighbor according to your ability, and take care of yourself so that you do not fall.
Be content with little or much, and you will certainly not hear the reproach of living as a guest.
Nevertheless, be patient with the lowly person and do not keep him waiting for alms.
For the commandment’s sake, support the poor person; in his need do not turn him away empty.
Listen to me, your father, children, and act accordingly, so that you may be saved.
Do not glory in your father’s dishonor, for a father’s dishonor is no glory to you.
Child, support your father in old age, and do not grieve him during his life.
Even if he loses understanding, bear with him, and do not dishonor him in all your strength.
Child, carry out your works with gentleness, and you will be loved by an acceptable person.
The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself, and you will find favor before the Lord,
Do not seek things too difficult for you, and do not investigate things beyond your strength.
Consider the things commanded you, for you have no need of hidden things.
Do not busy yourself with matters beyond your tasks, for more than human understanding has been shown to you.
he will serve those who brought him into being as masters.
Honor your father in deed and word, so that a blessing may come upon you from him.
Do not laugh together with him, so that you do not suffer together and in the end gnash your teeth.
Do not give him authority in youth.
Bruise his sides while he is little, lest he become hardened and disobey you.
Discipline your son and work upon him, so that you do not stumble through his shamelessness.
Do not give your soul over to grief, and do not afflict yourself with your deliberation.
Beguile your soul, comfort your heart, and put grief far from you; for grief has destroyed many, and there is no benefit in it.
Have you sat at a great table? Do not open your throat over it or say, “How much there is upon it!”
Remember that an evil eye is bad. What has been created worse than an eye? Therefore it weeps for every reason.
Do not stretch your hand toward whatever it looks at, and do not crowd together with it in the dish.
Understand your neighbor’s concerns from yourself, and consider every matter.
Eat what is set before you like a human being, and do not chew greedily, lest you be hated.
Be the first to stop for the sake of good discipline; do not be insatiable, lest you stumble.
If you have sat among many, do not stretch out your hand before them.
If you have been forced to eat too much, rise, vomit at a distance, and you will find rest.
Listen to me, child, and do not despise me; in the end you will find my words true. In all your works be skillful, and no illness at all will meet you.
Do not show your manliness with wine, for wine has destroyed many.
At a wine banquet do not rebuke your neighbor or despise him in his gladness. Do not speak a reproachful word to him or distress him with a demand for repayment.
Have they appointed you leader? Do not exalt yourself. Be among them as one of them; take care of them, and then sit down.
Rise at the right hour and do not linger at the rear; hurry home and do not be slack.
There enjoy yourself and carry out your thoughts, but do not sin by a proud word.
For these things bless your Maker, who intoxicates you with His good things.
Do nothing without counsel, and after doing it, do not regret it.
After attending to every duty, recline, so that you may rejoice because of them and receive a crown for good order.
Do not walk on a road of obstacles, and do not stumble among stones.
Do not trust a road free of stumbling blocks,
and guard yourself even against your children.
In every undertaking trust your soul, for this too is keeping commandments.
The one who trusts the law attends to commandments, and the one who trusts the Lord will not be diminished.
Speak, elder, for it is fitting for you, with exact knowledge, but do not hinder the music.
Where there is a performance, do not pour out chatter or display wisdom at an unsuitable time.
Speak, young man, if you are needed; scarcely twice, if you are asked.
Sum up your speech, much in few words; be like someone who knows and at the same time keeps silent.
Among dignitaries do not make yourself their equal, and while another speaks do not chatter much.
Look in this way at all the Most High’s works: two by two, one opposite the other.
Consider that I have labored not for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.
Listen to me, dignitaries of the people; give ear, leaders of the assembly.
Do not give son or wife, brother or friend authority over you during your life. Do not give your money to another, lest afterward you regret it and beg for it.
As long as you still live and breath is in you, do not exchange yourself for any flesh.
In all your works be preeminent; do not put a blemish upon your glory.
On the day when your life’s days are completed, at the time of death, distribute your inheritance.
Make a servant work, and you will find rest; release his hands, and he will seek freedom.
A yoke and strap will bend a neck, and racks and tortures are for a wrongdoing household slave.
Put him to work so that he is not idle, for idleness has taught much evil.
Assign him tasks as befits him, and if he does not obey, make his fetters heavy.
Do not go to excess against any flesh, and do nothing without judgment.
If you have a household slave, let him be as yourself, because you acquired him with blood.
If you have a household slave, treat him as a brother, because you will need him as your own soul.
If you mistreat him and he leaves and runs away, on what road will you look for him?
Prepare your speech, and so you will be heard; bind instruction together and answer.
Unless they are sent from the Most High in a visitation, do not give your heart to them.
Do not bribe, for He will not accept it, and do not rely on an unjust sacrifice.
Do not appear empty before the Lord, for all these things are for the commandment’s sake.
Glorify the Lord with a generous eye, and do not diminish the firstfruits of your hands.
With every gift make your face cheerful, and consecrate a tenth with gladness.
Give to the Most High according to His gift, with a generous eye according to what your hand has found.
Do not take counsel with someone who looks suspiciously at you, and hide your counsel from those who envy you.

Do not consult a woman about her rival, a coward about war, a merchant about exchange, a buyer about selling, a grudging person about gratitude, a merciless person about kindness, a lazy person about any work, a yearly hired worker about completing it, or an idle household slave about much labor. Do not rely on these for any counsel.
Instead, remain with a godly man whom you know to keep commandments, whose soul is in accord with your soul, and who will share your pain if you stumble.
Establish the counsel of your heart, for you have nothing more trustworthy than it.
Besides all these things, petition the Most High to make your road straight in truth.
Child, in your life test your soul; see what is bad for it and do not give it that.
Do not be insatiable in every luxury, and do not abandon yourself to dishes of food.
Do not forget a friend in your soul or be unmindful of him in your wealth.
Guard your soul against a counselor, and know beforehand what he needs—for he too will counsel for himself—lest he cast a lot against you
Honor a physician with his due honors, according to the need for him; for the Lord created him also.
Put wrongdoing away, straighten your hands, and cleanse your heart from every sin.
Give a fragrant offering and a memorial of fine flour, and make your offering rich, as one who is no more.
Give the physician a place too, for the Lord created him; do not let him leave you, for you need him.
Child, shed tears over the dead and begin a lament as one suffering terribly. Lay out his body according to his due, and do not neglect his burial.
Make your weeping bitter and your lament fervent; mourn according to his worth for one day or two because of slander, and be comforted because of grief.
Do not give your heart over to grief; put it away, remembering the last things.
Do not forget: there is no return. You will not benefit this person, and you will harm yourself.
“Remember my judgment, for yours is likewise: yesterday for me, today for you.”
When the dead person rests, bring his remembrance to rest, and be comforted concerning him when his spirit departs.
Child, do not be negligent in your illness, but pray to the Lord, and He Himself will heal you.
Listen to me, holy sons, and sprout like a rose growing beside a flowing stream.
Give a fragrant scent like frankincense, and blossom like a lily. Spread a scent and offer a song of praise; bless the Lord for all His works.
Ascribe greatness to His name and give thanks with His praise, with songs of lips and lyres; and thus you will say in thanksgiving:
And now sing hymns with all your heart and mouth, and bless the Lord’s name.
Child, do not deprive the poor person of his livelihood, and do not keep needy eyes waiting.
Be like a father to orphans and in place of a husband to their mother. Then you will be like a son of the Most High, and He will love you more than your mother does.
Do not grieve a hungry soul, and do not provoke a man in his helplessness.
Watch for the right time and guard against evil, and do not be ashamed concerning your soul.
Do not show partiality against your own soul, and do not defer to someone to your own downfall.
Do not withhold a word at a time of need,
Do not speak against the truth, and be ashamed of your lack of instruction.
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not force your way against a river’s current.
Do not lay yourself down beneath a foolish person, and do not show partiality to someone powerful.
Struggle for the truth until death, and the Lord God will fight for you.
Do not be rash with your tongue and sluggish and slack in your deeds.
Do not add trouble to an embittered heart, and do not delay a gift to someone in need.
Do not be like a lion in your house, indulging vain fancies among your household slaves.
Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive, but drawn back when repaying.
Do not reject an afflicted supplicant, and do not turn your face away from a poor person.
Do not turn your eye away from someone in need, and do not give anyone occasion to curse you.
Make yourself welcome to the assembly, and bow your head to a person of high rank.
Incline your ear to the poor person, and answer him peaceably with gentleness.
Rescue the one being wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer, and do not lose courage when you judge.
Child, do not live a life of begging; it is better to die than to beg.
Take care of your name, for it will remain with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold.
Therefore, be ashamed in accordance with my word. For it is not good to preserve every kind of shame, and not everything finds approval with everyone in good faith.
Be ashamed before father and mother concerning sexual immorality, and before a leader and ruler concerning a lie;
before a judge and magistrate concerning an offense, and before an assembly and people concerning lawlessness;
before a partner and friend concerning injustice, and before the place where you reside concerning theft;
before the truth of God and His covenant, and of planting your elbow upon bread;
of contempt in receiving and giving, and of silence toward those who greet you;
of looking at a courtesan, and of turning your face away from a relative;
of taking away a portion and a gift, and of scrutinizing a married woman;
of meddling with his maidservant—and do not stand over her bed;
before friends concerning words of reproach—and after giving, do not reproach;
of repeating a report you have heard, and of concealing secret words.
Then you will be truly modest and find favor before every person.
Do not fear death’s sentence; remember those before you and those who come afterward.
Do not be ashamed of these things, and do not show partiality so as to sin:
Keep a firm watch over a headstrong daughter, lest she make you a delight to enemies, a subject of talk in the city, and an outcast of the people, and put you to shame among a great multitude.
Do not gaze at any person’s beauty, and do not sit among women.
of the law of the Most High and His covenant, and of a judgment that acquits the ungodly;
of an accounting with a partner and fellow travelers, and of giving an inheritance to companions;
of accuracy in scales and weights, and of acquiring much or little;
of profit from merchants’ sales, of much discipline for children, and of making an evil household slave’s side bleed.
With an evil woman, a seal is good; where there are many hands, lock things up.
Whatever you hand over, do so by number and weight; every giving and receiving should be in writing.
Do not be ashamed of disciplining the senseless and foolish, or an extremely old man who contends with young people. Then you will be truly instructed and approved before everyone living.
Look at the rainbow and bless the One who made it, exceedingly beautiful in its radiance.
The Lord is fearsome and exceedingly great, and His power is wondrous.
As you glorify the Lord, exalt Him as much as you can, for He will surpass even that. As you exalt Him, increase your strength; do not grow weary, for you will never reach the end.
Let us now praise glorious men, our fathers according to their generations.
Do not rely on your possessions, and do not say, “They are sufficient for me.”
Be firm in your understanding, and let your word be one.
Be quick in listening, and give your answer with patience.
Do not be called a whisperer, and do not set an ambush with your tongue. For shame rests upon a thief, and harsh condemnation upon someone double-tongued.
In great and small matters do not act ignorantly, and do not become an enemy in place of a friend. For a bad name will inherit shame and reproach; that is how it is with the double-tongued sinner.
Do not follow your soul and your strength in walking according to the desires of your heart.
Do not say, “Who will have power over me?” For the Lord will certainly exact retribution.
Do not say, “I sinned, and what happened to me?” For the Lord is patient.
Do not become fearless about atonement, adding sin upon sins.
Do not say, “His compassion is great; He will atone for the multitude of my sins.” For mercy and wrath are with Him, and His anger will settle upon sinners.
Do not delay turning to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day. For the Lord’s wrath will go out suddenly, and at the time of retribution you will perish.
Do not rely on unjust possessions, for they will be of no benefit to you on the day of calamity.
Do not winnow in every wind or walk on every path; that is how the double-tongued sinner acts.
And now bless the God of all, who does great things everywhere, who exalts our days from the womb and deals with us according to His mercy.
May He entrust His mercy to us, and in our days may He redeem us.
Draw near to me, you who are uninstructed, and lodge in a house of instruction.
Why do you say you are lacking in these things, while your souls thirst exceedingly?
I opened my mouth and said, “Acquire for yourselves without silver.
“Put your neck beneath the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction. She is near at hand to be found.
“See with your own eyes that I labored a little and found much rest for myself.
“Take part in instruction at the cost of much silver, and acquire much gold through her.
“May your soul rejoice in His mercy, and may you not be ashamed in His praise.
“Do your work before the appointed time, and He will give you your reward in His time.”
Separate yourself from your enemies, and be cautious with your friends.
Do not lift yourself up in the counsel of your soul, lest your soul be torn apart like a bull.
Listen, child, and receive my judgment; do not reject my counsel.
Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar.
Place your shoulder beneath her and carry her, and do not resent her bonds.
Approach her with all your soul, and keep her ways with your whole strength.
Trace her out and seek her, and she will become known to you; when you have gained hold of her, do not let her go.
If you are willing, child, you will be instructed; if you give your soul to it, you will become skillful.
Stand among a multitude of elders, and if anyone is wise, cling to him.
Be willing to listen to every godly discourse, and do not let proverbs of understanding escape you.
If you see someone understanding, rise early to go to him, and let your foot wear down the steps of his doors.
Consider the Lord’s ordinances and meditate continually on His commandments. He Himself will establish your heart, and the wisdom you desire will be given to you.
Let those at peace with you be many, but your counselors one out of a thousand.
If you acquire a friend, acquire him through testing, and do not trust him quickly.
Do not do evil things, and evil will certainly not overtake you.
Do not lose heart in your prayer, and do not neglect to give alms.
Do not laugh at someone in bitterness of soul, for there is One who brings low and raises high.
Do not plow a lie against your brother, or do the same to a friend.
Do not be willing to tell any lie, for persisting in it leads to no good.
Do not chatter among a multitude of elders, and do not repeat a word in your prayer.
Do not hate laborious work or farming, which the Most High created.
Do not count yourself among the multitude of sinners; remember that wrath will not delay.
Humble your soul greatly, for the retribution of the ungodly is fire and the worm.
Do not exchange a friend for profit or a true brother for gold of Souphir.
Do not disregard a wise and good wife, for her grace is beyond gold.
Withdraw from injustice, and it will turn aside from you.
Do not mistreat a household slave who works faithfully, or a hired worker who gives his soul to the task.
Let your soul love an understanding household slave; do not deprive him of freedom.
Do you have livestock? Look after them, and if they are useful to you, let them remain with you.
Do you have children? Discipline them, and bend their neck from youth.
Do you have daughters? Attend to their bodies, and do not make your face cheerful toward them.
Give a daughter in marriage, and you will have completed a great task; give her to an understanding man.
Do you have a wife after your heart? Do not put her away; and do not entrust yourself to an unloved woman.
Glorify your father with your whole heart, and do not forget your mother’s labor pains.
Remember that through them you were born; what will you repay them to match what they have given you?
Revere the Lord with your whole soul, and honor His priests.
Son, do not sow in the furrows of injustice, and you will certainly not reap them sevenfold.
Love your Maker with your whole strength, and do not abandon His ministers.

Fear the Lord and glorify the priest; give him his portion, as you have been commanded: firstfruits, the guilt offering, the gift of shoulders, the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of holy things.
Stretch out your hand also to the poor person, so that your blessing may be complete.
Let the favor of a gift extend to every living person, and do not withhold kindness from the dead.
Do not hold back from those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
Do not hesitate to visit a sick person, for through such deeds you will be loved.
In all your words remember your last things, and you will never sin.
Do not seek leadership from the Lord or a seat of glory from a king.
Do not justify yourself before the Lord, and do not make yourself out to be wise before a king.
Do not seek to become a judge, lest you prove unable to remove injustices, lest you be afraid before someone powerful and place a stumbling block in your uprightness.
Do not sin against the population of a city, and do not cast yourself down among the crowd.
Do not bind a sin twice, for even with one you will not be innocent.
Do not say, “He will look upon the multitude of my gifts, and when I present an offering to God Most High, He will accept it.”
Do not fight with a powerful person, lest you fall into his hands.
Do not kindle a sinner’s coals, lest you be burned in his blazing fire.
Do not rise up against an insolent person, lest he sit in ambush against your mouth.
Do not lend to someone stronger than you; if you do lend, regard it as lost.
Do not stand surety beyond your means; if you do stand surety, take thought as someone who will have to pay.
Do not litigate with a judge, for they will decide in his favor in keeping with his prestige.
Do not travel on a road with a reckless person, lest he become a burden against you. For he will act according to his own will, and you will perish along with him through his folly.
Do not fight with a hot-tempered person or cross the wilderness with him. For blood is as nothing in his eyes, and where there is no help, he will strike you down.
Do not take counsel with a fool, for he will not be able to keep a word concealed.
Do not do something secret before a stranger, for you do not know what it will bring forth.
Do not reveal your heart to every person, and do not let him return you a favor.
Do not quarrel with a rich person, lest he set his weight against yours; for gold has destroyed many and turned aside the hearts of kings.
Do not fight with a talkative person, and do not pile wood upon his fire.
Do not jest with someone uninstructed, lest your ancestors be dishonored.
Do not reproach someone turning away from sin; remember that we are all under penalties.
Do not dishonor a person in his old age, for some of us too grow old.
Do not rejoice over a dead person; remember that we all die.
Do not disregard the discourse of the wise; dwell among their proverbs, for from them you will learn instruction and how to serve people of high rank.
Do not neglect the discourse of the old, for they themselves learned from their fathers; from them you will learn understanding and how to give an answer at a time of need.
Do not be jealous of the wife at your bosom, and do not teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
Do not abandon an old friend, for a recent one is not his equal. A new friend is new wine; when it has aged, you will drink it with gladness.
Do not envy a sinner’s glory, for you do not know what his downfall will be.
Do not take pleasure in the prosperity of the ungodly; remember that even down to Hades they will certainly not be acquitted.

Keep far away from a person who has authority to kill, and you will certainly not suspect the fear of death. If you do approach him, do not offend, so that he does not take away your life. Recognize that you are crossing among traps and walking upon a city’s battlements.
To the best of your strength, take the measure of your neighbors, and seek counsel with the wise.
Let your deliberation be with people of understanding, and let all your discourse be in the law of the Most High.
Let righteous men be your table companions, and let your boast be in the fear of the Lord.
Do not give your soul to a woman so that she steps upon your strength.
Do not encounter a woman who acts as a courtesan, lest you fall into her traps.
Do not spend your time with a female musician, lest you be caught by her undertakings.
Do not study a virgin closely, lest you stumble into penalties on her account.
Do not give your soul to prostitutes, so that you do not lose your inheritance.
Do not look around in the streets of a city, or wander in its deserted places.
Turn your eye away from a shapely woman, and do not study another’s beauty closely. Many have been led astray by a woman’s beauty, and from it affection is kindled like fire.
Do not sit at all with a married woman or share a wine feast with her, lest your soul turn toward her and you slip in your spirit into destruction.
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your breasts are better than wine.

They drew you; we will run after you into the fragrance of your perfumes. The king brought me into his chamber. Let us exult and rejoice in you; we will love your breasts more than wine. Uprightness loved you.
Do not look at me because I have been darkened, because the sun looked upon me. My mother’s sons fought against me; they made me a keeper in vineyards. My own vineyard I did not keep.
Tell me, you whom my soul loved, where you pasture, where you rest at noon, lest I become like a woman covering herself beside your companions’ herds.
My kinsman answers and says to me: Rise, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove,
The fig tree has brought forth its early figs; the vines are flowering and have given fragrance. Rise, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove,
and come, my dove, in the shelter of the rock, close to the outer wall. Show me your face and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your face lovely.
until the day breathes and the shadows move. Turn back, my kinsman; be like a gazelle or a young stag upon mountains of hollows.
Bring me into the house of wine; arrange love over me.
Strengthen me with sweet cakes, heap apples about me, for I am wounded by love.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field: do not awaken or stir up love until it wishes.
Go out and look at King Solomon wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on his wedding day, on the day his heart rejoiced.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field: do not awaken or stir up love until it wishes.
Awake, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow through my garden, and let my spices flow. Let my kinsman come down into his garden and eat its tree fruits.
Come from Lebanon, bride, come from Lebanon. You will come and pass through from the beginning of faith, from the summit of Senir and Hermon, from lions’ enclosures, from leopards’ mountains.
I entered my garden, my sister, bride; I gathered my myrrh with my spices. I ate my bread with my honey; I drank my wine with my milk. Eat, companions, and drink and become drunk, brothers!

I sleep, but my heart keeps watch. The voice of my kinsman—he knocks upon the door! Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is filled with dew and my curls with the drops of night.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they have given me wings. Your hair is like herds of goats that have appeared from Gilead.
Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, and we will look at you. What will you see in the Shulammite? She comes like dances of the camps.
Come, my kinsman, let us go out into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
Let us rise early for the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has blossomed, whether the bloom has flowered, whether the pomegranates have flowered. There I will give you my breasts.
You who sit in gardens, companions are attending to your voice; let me hear it.
Flee, my kinsman, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon mountains of spices.
I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field: why awaken or stir up love before it wishes?
Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy harsh as Hades. Its wings are wings of fire, its flames.
Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think of the Lord in goodness, and seek Him in simplicity of heart.
Therefore guard yourselves against useless grumbling, and restrain your tongue from slander; for a secret utterance will not pass away without effect, and a lying mouth destroys a soul.
Do not pursue death through the wandering of your life, nor draw destruction upon yourselves through the works of your hands;
Through such works Thou didst teach Thy people that the righteous person must love humanity, and make Thy sons hopeful, because Thou givest repentance for sins.
so that it might be known that one must rise before the sun to give Thee thanks and appeal to Thee at the rising of the light.
Listen, then, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of the earth.
Desire my words, then; long for them, and you will be instructed.
Give ear, you who rule a multitude and boast over crowds of nations;
If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, rulers of peoples, honor wisdom, so that you may reign for ever.
Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will benefit.
